523329|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose 63% YoY to INR 50.3 crores and PAT rose 382% to INR 15.1 crores, with collections up 68% to INR 131.2 crores.
523329|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong start, with collections outpacing bookings and profitability improving sharply year on year. Bookings normalised to INR 105.7 crores (1.26 lakh sq ft) after the exceptional Q4 FY26 launch quarter. Margin gains were driven mainly by the high-margin horizontal Imperia Phase 2 project, which accounted for about 85% of quarterly revenue. Management added a 50+ acre Lucknow land contract and about 15 acres of aggregated land, but gave no firm FY27 sales or booking guidance and was cautious on Faith (Trinity) launch traction.

523367|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, but PBDIT fell to INR400 crore from INR426 crore on sugar cost pressure.
523367|2026-03.overview: DCM Shriram's Q4 FY26 net revenue (net of excise) grew 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, while PBDIT declined to INR400 crore from INR426 crore. Chemicals revenue rose 32% and Vinyl PBDIT jumped 68%, but Sugar and ethanol PBDIT fell 18% on higher cane prices and Fenesta's margin was diluted by costs. FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR13,538 crore and PBDIT rose 15% to INR1,694 crore, with net debt at INR1,767 crore and ROCE at 13%. Management flagged high PVC price volatility and an unresolved ethanol allocation problem as the main near-term concerns.

segments.name: Sugar and ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue down 3% to INR991 crore; ethanol prices -15% on sales mix. PBDIT down 18% to INR207 crore as cane prices rose 8%. Crush fell to 473 lakh quintals with recovery of 10.8%; sugar inventory 32.2 lakh quintals vs 39.9 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Fenesta Building Systems
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,112 crore (+28%). Q4 revenue +34% YoY, but PBDIT up only 6% to INR37 crore given fixed costs and new platforms. Order book up 15%.

segments.name: Shriram Farm Solutions
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in FY26; research wheat sales +22% to a record. Q4 revenue +32% YoY in an off-season quarter. 13 new products launched in FY26, four from in-house R&D.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue down 11% on a maintenance shutdown. Outstanding subsidy INR189 crore vs INR161 crore last year. Gas supply risk from the West Asia conflict flagged.

segments.name: Bioseed
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue down 1% and PBDIT loss of INR8 crore. Management said the FY26 cotton seed environment was challenging; kharif placements are reasonable, with cotton inventory a concern.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR1,000-1,200 crore, including board-approved projects and pipeline.
INR217 crore capex for ~48 MW additional renewable power for Bharuch, taking RE provision from 50.4 MW to 98.4 MW; completion around Q1 FY28.
INR101 crore capex to expand formulated resins capacity by 36 KTPA to 50 KTPA; commissioning by Q2 FY28.
Management expects Epoxy/advanced materials unit to reach break-even in FY27 and be slightly better than break-even this year.
Management expects sugar margins to shrink versus last year but the shrinkage to be not significant, with prices expected to improve from record-low inventory.
Management expects caustic capacity utilisation to stay robust in FY27 and reasonable margins in ECH if raw material and product prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Pujan Shah (Molecule Ventures): outlook for PVC pricing given China property weakness and possible closures of inefficient Chinese PVC plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Shriram said pricing is very volatile and hard to forecast; hoped the rupee depreciation supports import parity and that the 11% import duty returns from 1 July 2026. Current PVC prices around INR81-82/kg; China capacity is so large that closures cannot be verified.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj (360 ONE): when will MIP be in place and is there accelerated Chinese dumping or domestic inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MIP is under dialogue with government, which has recommended a price considered too low; industry is pressing for a realistic MIP. China was ~50% of India's PVC imports last year, and no timeline can be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj: how will Middle East alumina capacity outages affect the global caustic balance and domestic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Shriram said regional balances matter and the impact of one demand region cannot be directly correlated to price; expects robust Indian demand long term with some short-term volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha (Unifi Capital): ECH utilisation and margin outlook, and epoxy break-even timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ECH running at 60-70% utilisation, ramp-up over one to two quarters; management expects healthy ECH margins if raw material and product prices hold. Epoxy/advanced materials expected to reach break-even in FY27, with Amit Agarwal saying slightly better than break-even this year.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: is ECH margin still in the 20-25% range and will chemicals EBITDA margin (about 20% in FY26) improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said Bharuch should be assessed as an integrated complex; complex revenue +38% and EBITDA +50% last year; new products rose from ~14% to ~34-35% of revenue. Aditya Shriram declined to give a margin number.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: will sugar margins be material in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said margins are lower than last year, but record-low industry inventory (~4 million tonnes) should lift prices; shrinkage expected but not significant. The export ban has only short-term sentiment impact.

qa_highlights.question: Riya Mehta (Aequitas): Fenesta cost pass-through, margins and demand after aluminium price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said retail customers are hard to pass cost to, while institutional contracts pass through costs beyond a tolerance level; margin is hit until then. Demand is good with a record order book.

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR1,000-1,200 crore including board-approved projects and pipeline. Kharif placements are reasonable, with El Nino risk and cotton inventory as the main concern.

523367|2026-06.headline: DCM Shriram Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR3,564 crore and PBDIT 12% to INR364 crore; reported PAT of INR693 crore includes INR474 crore one-time tax credit.
523367|2026-06.overview: Consolidated net revenue grew 9% YoY to INR3,564 crore and PBDIT rose 12% to INR364 crore, led by Chemicals (revenue +33%, PBDIT +24%). Vinyl PBDIT nearly doubled on price gains despite a 25% fall in PVC volumes, while Bioseed swung to a loss on delayed monsoon. Reported PAT of INR693 crore includes a INR474 crore one-time tax adjustment and INR79 crore of other one-time gains; underlying PAT was INR147 crore, up 28%. Management flagged weak rural demand, soft Q2 vinyl offtake and a 15-20% Kharif sowing shortfall as near-term headwinds.

vs INR236 crore a year ago

segments.name: Vinyl
segments.commentary: Revenue -10% YoY on PVC volumes -25% despite prices +22%; utilisation 100% vs 98%. PBDIT +88% to INR43 crore; carbide volumes and prices each +15%.

segments.commentary: Revenue -2% YoY; domestic sugar volumes -8%, realisations +2%. PBDIT INR22 crore vs negative INR7 crore last year, which included a ~INR36 crore one-time ethanol duty provision. Sugar inventory 20.8 lakh quintals vs 27.7 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Fenesta Building Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue +22% YoY; PBDIT +13% to INR40 crore, diluted by product mix and fixed costs for new platforms. Order book up 4%, roughly INR1,000 crore.

segments.commentary: Revenue +11% with realisations +19% and flat volumes; PBDIT fell to INR23 crore from INR38 crore, as the year-ago quarter had a INR24 crore one-time gain.

segments.name: Bioseed
segments.commentary: Revenue -26% YoY; PBDIT negative INR9 crore vs INR42 crore last year on lower corn and paddy volumes and weaker cotton margins.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give forward caustic price guidance, but said ECU is just below INR30,000/t and expects prices in that range or higher; chlorine is at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t.
Bharuch aluminium chloride and calcium chloride projects expected to start commercial production in Q2 FY27.

Kota 68 MW peak hybrid renewable project under commissioning, with average injection of 25 MW in July; Serentica 58 MW hybrid agreement signed to take peak renewable capacity at Bharuch and Kota to about 176 MW.
Cash tax outgo expected at about 19% for at least five years through MAT credit utilisation of INR376 crore, while P&L tax rate stays at 25%.
Net borrowings at FY27 end expected to be similar to current levels, with a reduction of about INR200 crore possible; capex of about INR1,000 crore planned this year.
Demolition of the group demerger: application to government targeted within FY27, timeline uncertain.
Vinyl demand expected soft in Q2 FY27; government reinstated basic customs duty on PVC imports and DGFT set minimum import price of US$766/t for six months.
Bioseed: large part of Kharif volume lost; no firm recovery guided for Q2.
capex_capacity: Caustic soda utilisation 82% in Q1; expected to improve as downstream projects commission. New flaker facility lets part of caustic output be exported.
Vinyl utilisation 100% in Q1 FY27.
Epichlorohydrin and epoxy plants running at ~70% utilisation with ramp-up ongoing; epoxy plant in Gujarat acquired October 2025.
Grain-based ethanol capacity can be run up to 260 KLD; management said it does not plan to add ethanol capacity.

Fenesta setting up a wooden door manufacturing facility; two acquisitions worth ~INR450 crore completed in the 12 months to June 2026.
demand_pricing: Domestic caustic demand steady from alumina, soaps and detergents, and textiles; hydrogen peroxide oversupplied in Asia.
PVC: imports surged after temporary customs duty waiver and Chinese imports; offtake weak on labour shortages, heatwave and cautious buying.
Sugar: global deficit of ~0.7 mt expected in 2026-27; domestic sugar price around INR4,450/quintal, expected to stay firm for a couple of months.
Ethanol: installed capacity ~2,000 crore litres vs OMC allocation ~1,060 crore litres; sugarcane feedstock only 28%.
Kharif sowing shortfall of 15-20% all-India and much higher in Bioseed markets; rainfall patchy after July.
Urea: subsidy regime governed by FICC; management says government is paying domestic makers on time, and gas-price spikes are a pass-through.
Fenesta order intake only up 4%; management attributes slowdown to customers deferring decisions amid West Asia crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Caustic soda price outlook for the near term and FY27, and current chlorine price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it normally avoids forward price statements, but noted ECU is just below INR30,000/t and expects that level or higher. Chlorine is at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SFS profitability up on flat top line, and how will Kharif profitability shape up if monsoon holds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited farmer reach, new R&D products and market credibility. It said monsoon has been good only in pockets, sowing is 15-20% lower, and it cannot project Aug-Sep outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: Will more capacity be diverted to grain ethanol given better sugar prices, and how is ethanol profitability set to move?
qa_highlights.answer: Grain-based ethanol can run up to 260 KLD and will be optimised for margins, which are currently good on maize. Management said it does not plan to add capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR400-odd crore tax reversal and the cash tax impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a six-year ITAT-backed position, with MAT credit of INR376 crore. P&L tax stays at 25%, but cash tax outgo is about 19% for at least five years.

qa_highlights.question: Crushing outlook for next season and sugar price expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call next year's cane harvest given the monsoon. Sugar prices, around INR40-50/kg per the analyst, are expected to stay firm for the next couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for urea margins given global price spikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Urea pricing is governed by FICC rules, so international prices do not hit domestic makers. Government is paying on time; gas price spikes are a pass-through that can strain cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise and what is the year-end net borrowing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt did not rise in Q1; the comparison is year-on-year, covering about INR450 crore of acquisitions and about INR1,000 crore of capex. Year-end net borrowing should be similar, with about INR200 crore reduction possible; debt/EBITDA is kept below 1.5x, with AA+ rating.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the group demerger and expected Bioseed recovery in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is committed to the demerger and aims to file the application with government in FY27, with no firm timeline. Bioseed: large part of Kharif volume is lost and no firm recovery was guided for Q2.

risks_watch: Kharif sowing shortfall of 15-20% all-India, with much higher gaps in Bioseed markets; August-September rainfall under El Nino is the swing factor for SFS, Bioseed and rural demand.
Vinyl: soft Q2 offtake, PVC import surge after the temporary duty waiver, and whether reinstated basic customs duty and US$766/t minimum import price support domestic prices.

Caustic and chlorine: ECU near INR30,000/t and chlorine at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t; caustic utilisation at 82% depends on downstream commissioning, including Bharuch aluminium and calcium chloride in Q2 FY27.
Reported PAT of INR693 crore is inflated by INR474 crore one-time tax and INR79 crore other gains; underlying PAT is INR147 crore, so track the MAT-driven cash tax rate of about 19%.
Fenesta order book up only 4% (about INR1,000 crore), attributed to customers deferring decisions amid the West Asia crisis; margins diluted by new platforms.

And yes, there will be some reduction by about INR200-odd crore probably, but it will all depend how the sugar season pans out, how much will be the inventory.
Our R&D focus is now the key issue which is going to be a major driver going forward, where there is a lot of stress from the management's side.

523405|2026-03.headline: JM Financial FY26 PAT rose 46% to INR1,202 crore (ROE 11.7%); Q4 segment profits weak as capital markets deals stalled amid FPI selling.
523405|2026-03.overview: JM Financial's Q4 FY26 call framed FY26 as a strong year on a two-year pivot basis: reported PAT after minority rose 46% to INR1,202 crore, or INR1,133 crore excluding a one-off tax-refund interest gain and Labour Code impact, up 38%. Q4 was weak across capital markets, wealth and private markets because primary issuance stalled amid FPI selling and West Asia-related volatility. Management said the IPO pipeline (INR1.4 lakh crore across 55 filings) remains strong and expects the second half of FY27 to be better than the first. Guidance centred on Wealth Management productivity, Private Markets loan book growth of 15-20%, and Affordable Home Loans AUM growth of 25%.

523405|2026-06.headline: JM Financial Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 13% YoY to INR883 crores, with Private Markets doubling to INR462 crores offsetting weak capital markets.
523405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated net revenue grew 13% YoY to INR883 crores and pre-provision operating profit rose 21% to INR469 crores. PAT ex-provisions before minorities rose 24% to INR379 crores, but after minorities it was flat at INR302 crores; reported PAT was INR292 crores (annualised ROE about 11%). Private Markets, led by a large distressed-credit resolution, carried the quarter while Corporate Advisory & Capital Markets and Wealth were weak on lack of primary issuance. Management said July revenues on the transaction side already exceeded June.

segments.commentary: Net revenue INR185 crores vs INR211 crores; PAT INR19 crores. Wealth loan book up 43% YoY to INR2,417 crores; recurring AUM about INR33,400 crores, now 30% of total AUM; 1,000+ RMs, 71 branches.

segments.commentary: Mutual fund management fees up 62% YoY to INR13 crores; loss after minorities flat at INR5 crores. Non-liquid AUM about INR10,900 crores, up 16% QoQ; employees up 10% YoY to 222.

segments.commentary: Net revenue doubled YoY to INR462 crores; pre-provision operating profit about 2.3x to INR375 crores; segment PAT after minorities INR228 crores. Gross ARC resolutions over INR2,000 crores, group share of cash flows over INR1,200 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cyclicality break in wealth and private credit, and when does organic credit growth start?
qa_highlights.answer: Bespoke book reached about INR3,000 crores, a 5-quarter high, and is about halfway to the 15-20% annual growth guided in Q4. Wealth is a 2-3 year build-out, with FY27 and FY28 expected to be productivity-led.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wealth profitability drop sharply, and will employee costs as a share of revenue fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower transactional revenue and gestation of 100+ RMs hired in 18 months, who take 2.5-3 years to turn profitable. Management said headcount has likely peaked, with hiring now selective.

qa_highlights.question: Asset management SIP book down about 30% and AUM flat; what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-liquid AUM rose 16% QoQ; decline was linked to small/mid-cap concentration. Management engaged more distributors and expects SIP and AUM to recover over the next couple of quarters. Quantitative targets to be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state ROE is achievable excluding market peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 ROE was about 11.5%, constrained by the 50% NBFC payout cap. Management expects a similar or better range this year, with stronger ROE from Wealth and AMC operating leverage in about 2 years; CACM is about 15% ROE in a weak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Private Markets carries 60-65% of capital and drags ROE; will capital mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity is at a low of 0.8x and will rise toward 2x in about 3 years as syndication grows, lifting ROE into the teens. Dividends constrained to 50% of NBFC profits.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 Private Markets revenue came from the single large ARC transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARC income is lumpy and largely booked on resolution; the June quarter included a big resolution, while book value fell by about INR1,200 crores of recovery and about INR600 crores was redeployed.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for demerger or listing of wealth and asset management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth and AM are still small; it will evaluate a listing or demerger at scale, subject to no tax leakage. Affordable housing listing is planned in 2-3 years.

523642|2026-03.headline: PI Industries FY26 revenue ₹67,137 mn with ~25% EBITDA margin; Q4 revenue ₹15,652 mn up sequentially, FY27 guided to growth led by H2 exports recovery.
523642|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹15,652 mn, up sequentially as guided last quarter, and FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹67,137 mn with a stated 25% EBITDA margin and ₹34,265 mn cash. AgChem exports declined on lower volumes amid a global downcycle, while domestic demand was hit by channel inventory, price pressure, and lower acreages. Management guided to revenue growth in FY27, with exports recovering in H2, but declined to give a specific growth number or margin guidance beyond maintaining last year's average gross margin. Pharma grew 40% for the year and biologicals are targeted to scale, with the first homegrown NCE (Pioxaniliprole) nearing market.

523694|2026-03.headline: Apcotex Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 42% YoY to INR 55 crore at a 13.76% margin, with PAT up 107% to INR 35 crore.

523694|2026-09.headline: Apcotex Q2 FY27 revenue rose 48% YoY to Rs 499 crore, but EBITDA margin eased to 11.69% as gross margins compressed.

EBITDA margin was 11.69% versus 12.06% a year earlier, and PAT margin was 6.98%. H1 FY27 was the company's strongest half-year, with revenue of Rs 1,025 crore (+44%), EBITDA of Rs 175 crore (+121%, margin 17.12%) and PAT of Rs 114 crore (+156%). Management attributed the Q2 margin dip to high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses, and more aggressive pricing to win export volumes.

segments.commentary: Sole Indian producer, entirely import-dependent; plant has run at full capacity for about 1.5 to 2 years. Capex project targeted for commissioning around April 2027. H1 NBR margin said to be slightly higher than synthetic latex.

segments.commentary: Serves about five industries; construction strongest, paper and textiles decent, tyres okay, carpets a laggard due to MENA dependence. SBR latex plant at Valia expected around Q2 of next year.

Competitor shutdowns in Q1 benefited the company, which kept plants running; overcapacity in nitrile latex persists from COVID-era additions.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins at a four-quarter low, and what drove the rise in export volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses in the quarter, and more aggressive pricing. Exports improved with better ship availability to Saudi Arabia and Fujairah, plus orders from other markets. EBITDA per ton and ROCE were better YoY.

qa_highlights.answer: Running close to full capacity; Q2 margins normalised from a strong Q1 but are much better than the last three years. Overcapacity from COVID-era additions remains even after some smaller and older plants shut. Expansion decision deferred for a couple more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a timeline and funding breakup for the Rs 210 crore expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: NBR commissioning targeted for about April 2027, with two to three years to full utilisation. Management said about Rs 65 crore is spent and Rs 155 crore remains, but did not give a debt versus internal accrual split in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Which synthetic latex industries are growing or lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction (repairs, waterproofing, oil drilling) has grown strongly; paper and textiles are decent and tyres okay. Carpets are the laggard due to MENA and Western market exposure from tariffs, war and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: What long-term volume growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 10% average volume CAGR over three to five years, driven by population and GDP growth in India and Southeast Asia, plus substitution of European supply in MENA.

qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the Q1-to-Q2 seasonal decline from monsoon-linked demand. It said it had not analysed Q2-to-Q3 patterns and would review five years of data. It urged investors to focus on annual trends, given oil-linked inventory gains and losses.

523704|2026-09.headline: Mastek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% QoQ cc to $107.3M, but 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M and EBITDA margin slipped to 14.4%.
523704|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 2.4% QoQ in constant currency to $107.3M (Rs 1,018.7 crore, up 8.3% YoY in INR), with PAT of Rs 105.7 crore. Operating EBITDA margin fell about 100 bps QoQ to 14.4%, mainly from increments and ESOPs (190 bps), partly offset by AI-led efficiency and extra working days. The 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M, attributed to a delayed US federal start and slower UK consumption, though it grew 2.3% YoY in USD. Management reiterated that FY27 should beat FY26, with North America turning around from H2 and UK Healthcare recovering after recontracting.

financial_highlights.change: -7.7% QoQ, +2.3% YoY in USD, +10.4% YoY in INR

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and investments (net of debt)
financial_highlights.change: up about Rs 36 crore after Rs 50 crore dividend and Rs 55 crore loan repayment

segments.name: UK-Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4.1% in the quarter, and UK EBIT was 18%. Financial Services grew over 16% QoQ, and public sector grew 6.1% QoQ. Healthcare & Life Sciences lagged on right-shifted starts, and several public-sector orders were put on hold pending the new government's budget.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Total backlog rose 7.8% QoQ and 47.9% YoY. Management expects a meaningful growth turnaround from H2, though a $25M federal deal start has slipped to after the mid-term elections.

segments.name: APAC & Middle East
segments.commentary: Some older contracts were signed, giving a revenue bounce-back in Q2. Management said the Middle East outlook is uncertain and performance is well below plan, especially in Saudi Arabia.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Public sector grew 6.1% QoQ and Financial Services grew 15.3% QoQ. Healthcare & Life Sciences has been slow for two quarters, with management expecting recovery after beta-phase contract awards in Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: Margin target: improve EBITDA by at least 160 bps in the medium term, with the return to the 16% mark dependent on macro and geopolitical factors.
US and Middle East margins expected to improve from Q3, which should offset some of the UK mix-driven margin loss.
FY27 expected to beat FY26, with H2 seen as no slower than H1, though management flagged Middle East and geopolitical risk.
North America expected to see a meaningful growth turnaround from H2.
A UK NHS-related data transformation contract (north of GBP 100M) is an H2 event and would be incremental to TCV; a bridge contract covers about six months.
Subcontracting expected to stay around 18-20% of revenue, moving by about one percentage point in the short term.
Revenue and AI metrics, plus a Data & AI horizontal split, to be disclosed from next quarter (Q3 FY27).
capex_capacity: Headcount closed at 4,810, down 87 QoQ due to workforce restructuring and a change in onsite/offshore mix.
Utilisation including trainees fell 0.8% QoQ, reflecting investment in domain resources.
Sale of Chennai property completed, booked as an exceptional gain, offset by restructuring costs and a write-off of old receivables (one-time).
Attrition (LTM) fell to 15.2% from 16.4%, the second consecutive quarterly decline.
Added 18 new customers in the quarter versus 13 in Q1.
demand_pricing: AI deals made up more than 40% of deals won in the quarter, and about 45% of the total order book. 53 AI deals were closed.
AI transformation deals run at roughly $0.5M to $5M each. AI productivity takeout deals can be much larger, with a $10M+ North America life sciences win.
AI transformation and foundation deals earn 40%+ gross margin, sometimes above 50%. AI productivity deals are price-aggressive with compressed margins.
Project business rose to 44-45% of revenue from about 40%, mostly fixed-bid. UK public sector and healthcare buy on rate cards.
Average deal tenure is about 3 years plus 2 years in UK-Europe and 18-24 months in North America.
Pipeline includes $100M+ deals to be adjudicated over 6-9 months.
Healthcare softness in UK-Europe is tied to the alpha-to-beta recontracting gap and a ramp-down in an offshore UK healthcare account.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book weakness execution-led or UK pressure? Is FY27 still expected to beat FY26? What is the ramp on new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: A $25M US federal deal start was delayed until after the mid-term elections, and a UK contract is consuming more slowly than planned, with pickup expected around Q4. Management still expects FY27 to beat FY26, citing H2 strength in UK and US and a Middle East dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI deals from new or existing clients, what are the deal sizes, and when will AI revenue be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: AI deals come from both new and existing clients, with at least two net-new wins in the examples shown. Typical AI deal size is $0.5M-$5M, and AI revenue figures will be presented from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline, and what is the bridge to the 160 bps recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments and ESOPs cost 190 bps. A UK mix shift from high-margin projects to lower-margin sovereignty and security-cleared work cost about 200 bps. AI-led efficiencies and restructuring recovered about 200 bps. Forex was a 20 bps tailwind. US and Middle East margins are expected to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America growth muted, and how do BFSI and healthcare trends differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a North America turnaround from H2. Healthcare & Life Sciences remains its strongest vertical, and BFSI growth is mainly UK-led. North America financial services is still early-stage.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI deals grow after the initial POC, and what margins do they earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI engagements typically expand into more process areas after the first win. Transformation and foundation deals earn 40%+ gross margin, while AI productivity deals carry compressed margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter energy and utilities, and what is the Top 5/Top 10 trend and subcon outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The energy and utilities push uses the public-sector framework playbook, with three frameworks landed in 90-120 days. Subcontracting is 18-20% of revenue and may move about one point; UK localisation and security-cleared demand may drive short-term subcon increases.

Disclosure is changing: the horizontal split and AI revenue will be reworked from Q3, and the factsheet client metrics were redefined.

523716|2026-03.headline: Ashiana Housing FY26 booking value hit record Rs 2,421 crore (+25% YoY); Q4 bookings Rs 1,290 crore driven by Gurugram Aaroham launch.
523716|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 bookings of Rs 1,290 crore rose 124% YoY, led by Ashiana Aaroham Phase-I and II in Gurugram (about Rs 833 crore at launch), with realisation up 71% YoY to Rs 11,566 per sq ft. Q4 total income rose 46% YoY to Rs 335 crore on handovers in Jaipur, Pune and Chennai, while PAT was flat at Rs 21 crore (6.26% margin). For FY26, total income more than doubled to Rs 1,187 crore, EBITDA rose 281% to Rs 176 crore (14.85% margin) and PAT reached Rs 118 crore versus Rs 18 crore in FY25. Management added about 2.9 lakh sq ft-equivalent of Senior Living land and reiterated a Rs 2,200 crore FY27 pre-sales target.

segments.commentary: FY26 bookings Rs 570 crore (+55% YoY); management targets over Rs 700 crore in FY27. Five projects with GDV over Rs 6,500 crore to launch in 12-24 months across Chennai, Bangalore and Bombay-Pune.

segments.name: Residential (Gurugram, Jaipur, Bhiwadi, Pune, Chennai, Jamshedpur)
segments.commentary: Q4 bookings driven by Gurugram Aaroham Phase-I/II (about Rs 833 crore at launch). Jaipur and Jamshedpur realisations now above Rs 7,000 per sq ft; management flagged early oversupply signs in Gurugram and Pune.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales target of Rs 2,200 crore, with Senior Living target above Rs 700 crore.

Launches planned in FY27: Ashiana Oma (Jaipur, about 10 acres, Rs 7,500-8,000 per sq ft, within a couple of months), Ashiana Aaranya and Tattvam (Q4 FY27), Aaroham Phase-III, and at least one phase in each Senior Living project.

capex_capacity: Land bank of about 96 lakh sq ft post recent additions (about 4x annual throughput); management says more land must be added this year.

Acquired 8.83 acres in Raigad for about Rs 450 crore sales potential; Panvel (agreement, about Rs 1,000 crore); Vadgaon (28.5 acres, about 20 lakh sq ft, Rs 1,800-2,000 crore GDV); Bangalore (about 11 lakh sq ft, CP resolution pending, about 2 months).

Amodh newer phases at about Rs 8,200-8,300 per sq ft; Amodh Phase-III around Rs 8,500 per sq ft used as the Vadgaon benchmark.
Competition in Senior Living seen as market-expanding; few peers building large (12-15 acre) projects with comparable amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Mahindra World City (Jaipur) lease terminated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the counterparty could not obtain social infrastructure approvals after about 18 months, so the transaction could not proceed; the lease was terminated, with scope to restart later.

qa_highlights.question: Project-level margin and cost breakup for Senior Living?
qa_highlights.answer: Project margins are expected at 30-35%; gross margin 35-40%, selling cost 5-6%. Land is 10-20% and hard construction 40-50% of revenue, with soft costs about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Construction cost inflation assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: No inflation underwritten at land purchase; management expects 8-10% construction cost increase in FY27 YoY on current information.

qa_highlights.question: Is annuity or leasing a major Senior Living revenue stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Not within five years; yields are low and leasing deposit structures are not viable. Home sales remain the main profit source, and assisted living is outsourced partly to Epoch Elder Care (Nirmay, Bhiwadi).

qa_highlights.question: Is there oversupply in the markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No oversupply yet overall. Gurugram and Pune show early signs; Jaipur, Jamshedpur and Bhiwadi show none.

qa_highlights.question: What is the class action suit status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has moved the Delhi High Court against class action applicability; a ruling is hoped for within FY27, but consumer complaints will continue for the filers regardless.

risks_watch: Construction cost inflation (8-10% expected in FY27) and labour and material shortages affecting delivery timelines.

Class action litigation over an older Kolkata/Pune-area project (Project Maitri-related disputes settled separately); outcome timing uncertain.
Execution of Bangalore land (CP still pending) and Panvel pricing not yet fixed; Maharashtra senior living policy not yet notified.
Management flagged that a sustained rise in unsold inventory in Gurugram would signal oversupply.

523828|2026-03.headline: Menon Bearings FY26 consolidated PAT rose 53.41% to INR 38.25 crore; Q4 PAT up 108.55% YoY, with management guiding 20-22% EBITDA margin.

Management guided to 25% annual volume growth, 20-22% EBITDA margin for the next two years, and INR 500 crore revenue by FY28. Alkop (aluminium) growth was flagged as a key swing factor after a slow prior two years.

FY27 target revenue about INR2,700 crore; company expects around 15% annual top-line growth on existing capacity.
Management said the company is maintaining its earlier FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and 15-20% PAT growth, and that it may improve slightly.
Quarter-to-quarter margins are not guided; management prefers full-year commentary. The price uptick is expected to hold for one or two quarters.

Greenfield land (100 acres, near Bhatinda Highway): capex of INR200-250 crore a year funded by internal accruals, total outlay about INR1,200-1,400 crore over four to five years; project to start in four to six (or six to eight) quarters, subject to pending approvals.
Paracetamol utilisation on the new 10,800 MT plant expected to reach 70-75% in FY27 and full capacity in FY28.
capex_capacity: Greenfield 100-acre site: environmental clearance in place, other approvals partly secured, capex not yet initiated; management expects most approvals within three to four months.
Capex split roughly 60% growth and 40% infrastructure, automation and land; the FY27 plan is about INR200 crore.

Price increases came in the later part of Q4 and were driven by higher crude-linked raw material and logistics costs; management said the spread is broadly unchanged because raw material costs were passed through.
Ethyl acetate spreads are better in April and May than in the March quarter, per management's confirmation.
Management said a Q4 inventory gain was not meaningful, as the price uptick came late in the quarter.
Management sees no supply problems on raw materials except for about one week in early March when crude-based chemicals and gas supply were disrupted.
Non-Ibu customers are mainly direct consumers rather than traders, which limits the upside from price moves.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield land: timeline and capex quantum?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 gross margin sustainable, or was it an inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to efficiency, product mix and capacity utilisation, plus a late-quarter price rise; it said there was no meaningful inventory gain and that quarter-to-quarter prediction is risky.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance being maintained or upgraded?

qa_highlights.question: How much R&D spend, and what products are in the launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 2-3% of revenue annually and is mainly process-related. Management did not name specific upcoming launches, saying products are announced when a decision is taken.

qa_highlights.question: Paracetamol utilisation and margin impact of the 3x capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: The new 10,800 MT plant is at about 55% utilisation, targeted at 70-75% in FY27 and full in FY28; higher utilisation is expected to lower unit cost.

qa_highlights.question: US FDA status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two US FDA inspections have been done, all products have CEPs, and approvals for Brazil and others are in place; ANDA approvals are granted without a site visit.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost trend and guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Rise driven by variable pay provision and new plant headcount; employee cost guided at about 9-10% of revenue.

Greenfield project (INR1,200-1,400 crore) depends on pending regulatory approvals, and management gave conflicting timelines (four to six vs six to eight quarters).
Paracetamol new-plant ramp (55% to 70-75%) needs to be delivered in FY27.

524164|2026-06.headline: IOL Chemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR756 crore and PAT 90% to INR64.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.6%.
524164|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR756 crore against INR551 crore a year earlier, up 37%. EBITDA rose 60.7% to INR111 crore, lifting margin to 14.6% from 12.4%, and PAT grew 89.9% to INR64.5 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher capacity utilisation, product mix, export realisations and operational efficiencies, and said there was no material inventory gain in the quarter. FY27 guidance was retained at 15-20% revenue growth, 14-15% EBITDA margin and 25-30% exports, with management saying revenue could exceed the INR2,600-2,700 crore range but not upgrading guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs 36% in Q1 FY26; non-ibu revenue up 67% YoY
Management did not split volume vs price

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals (API)
segments.commentary: Non-ibuprofen products were 43% of pharma revenue, up 67% YoY; growth described as broad-based across the portfolio. Most assets run at 80-95% utilisation, with paracetamol lower at about 55% of enhanced 10,800 MTPA capacity.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Management said the chemical segment margin trended up in the quarter, helped by higher ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride capacity, better realisations and higher exports. Triacetin plant (6,000 MTPA) started production only in May 2026, with steady-state revenue potential of about INR120 crore a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue growth of 15-20% (management said around 20% in Q&A), EBITDA margin 14-15%, exports about 25-30% of revenue.
Management said the INR2,600-2,700 crore full-year revenue guidance remains unchanged, may be crossed in the current scenario, but will not be upgraded.
FY28 (indicative, conditional on current scenario): revenue growth 15-20% and EBITDA margin 15-17%.
Near term: non-ibuprofen to reach about 50% of pharma revenue, with roughly 50% ibuprofen; by FY29, non-ibu expected at 50-55% of API segment with margins similar to ibuprofen.
Capex of about INR200 crore a year; about 60% expansion and new products, 40% infrastructure and efficiency. Next major project on the 101-acre land is not expected in FY27.

Capacity of ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride increased during the period.

R&D spend of INR26 crore in FY26; analytical equipment bought (XRD, LCMS, GCMS).
101-acre land parcel held for future expansion; statutory permissions in process; no project expected to commission in FY27.
demand_pricing: Healthy demand across paracetamol, pantoprazole, metformin, fenofibrate, clopidogrel and levetiracetam. Management said price increases were passed on to customers.

Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices rose sharply in March 2026 after the US-Iran conflict; since then prices have been stable to slightly easing, and management expects the raw-material-to-ethyl-acetate spread to hold.
Energy and logistics costs rose in the quarter; management said most of the increase was passed on.
Sequential gross margin fell as input costs rose before finished-product prices fully caught up. Some prices were pre-agreed with large customers.
Exports: some export customers have agreed quantities, so the export share can move quarter to quarter.

Regulatory: CEP approval for all products; US FDA approval for five products, with two to three more pending ANDA approval by formulators; NMPA China approval for clopidogrel; ibuprofen previously approved in China.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paracetamol given weak demand in past years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was tripled to 10,800 MTPA, utilisation is about 55%, and it expects about 70% by year-end. Demand is growing, with domestic traction and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 profit came from one-time inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no material inventory gain this quarter; a 10-15 day benefit existed at the end of Q4 FY26. The improvement was attributed to utilisation, mix, efficiencies and export realisations.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA outperformance came from operating leverage versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin gain mainly to internal efficiencies and higher utilisation, with no major product mix change apart from greater export penetration.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a split of pharma growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a numerical split. It said the majority came from higher volumes, with higher export realisations also contributing, and most assets at 80-95% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted in prior quarters and how long will demand last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher volumes, better pricing on established products and new products, and cost pass-through. It said there is reasonable order-book visibility for the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Triacetin revenue potential and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Production started only after May 2026, so about one month was in Q1. Steady-state revenue potential is about INR120 crore a year from the 6,000 MTPA plant. Management declined to compare its margin with ethyl acetate.

risks_watch: Raw material and energy price volatility (linked to the US-Iran conflict); margin sensitivity to lag in passing through costs.
Export share (28.5% in Q1) may fall back toward the 25-30% guidance band if customer agreed quantities shift.
Paracetamol utilisation at about 55% against the target of 70% by year-end.
Pending US FDA approvals for two to three ANDA-linked products and Triacetin regulatory approvals expected in two to three quarters.
FY28 margin outlook is explicitly conditional on the current scenario; management said it may not hold if conditions change within six months.
Lack of disclosure on the volume versus price split and on the regulated versus non-regulated export mix.

It was evasive on the pharma volume/price split, the R&D pipeline, CMO opportunities and the regulated-market export mix.

rows.why: Non-ibuprofen share of pharma revenue rose to 43% (from 36%) and is guided to ~50% near term, with two to three more US FDA ANDA approvals pending and Triacetin approvals expected in two to three quarters.

rows.why: Management expects two to three more quarters for Triacetin approvals and two to three more US FDA ANDA-linked approvals are pending, with CEP approval already for all products and US FDA approval for five.

524200|2026-03.headline: Vinati Organics FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 17% to INR741 crores and PAT 18% to INR488 crores, with the company still debt-free.
524200|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone net income including other income rose 17% QoQ to INR631 crores, EBITDA grew 20% QoQ to INR203 crores and PAT rose 27% QoQ to INR137 crores. For FY26, standalone net income was flat at INR2,281 crores while EBITDA and PAT grew 17% and 18%. Demand softened from October 2025 and management says it has since recovered. IBB volumes fell about 20% versus FY25 because of raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, which management says is now resolved. Management guides about 15% company-level volume growth in FY27 and FY27 capex of INR200-250 crores.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of FY26 revenue; management expects about 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next three years. Plant running at about 80% utilisation (about 75% post-expansion). Phase 2 of the expansion comes into effect by October 2026, with fuller utilisation in FY28.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Roughly 15-20% of FY26 revenue; revenue grew 15% in FY26. Management said FY26 AO volume was roughly flat-to-5% up, and the anti-dumping duty (ADD) application was rejected and reapplied, with a decision 6-9 months away.

segments.name: IB and HP-MTBE
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; stable in FY26, with management expecting double-digit growth in FY27.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; volume fell about 20% versus FY25 due to raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, now reported as resolved.

segments.name: Butyl phenols
segments.commentary: Capacity about 50,000 tonnes running at roughly 70-75% utilisation; management expects moderate growth in FY27 with no room for further expansion, so incremental demand goes first to captive use.

segments.name: Customised and others
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in FY26 on higher customer demand. Remainder of revenue mix.

segments.name: VOPL (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales were only about INR10 crores. Process reengineering of about 6 months to finish by September 2026, with production from October and revenue of about INR100-120 crores expected in FY27, from Q2/Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company-level volume growth guided at about 15%.
ATBS volume growth of about 15% YoY expected for at least the next three years.
FY27 capex earmarked at INR200-250 crores (about INR200 crores at Vinati Organics and INR40-50 crores at VOPL); management says about INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years.
AO and butyl phenol revenue targeted at INR800-900 crores in the next two years.
Long-term EBITDA margin of 26-27% considered achievable, given expansions, new products and raw material swings.
Gross block addition of about INR500 crores assumed at 1:1 asset turn.
Two to three new downstream products expected in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.
Company will continue to fund expansion from internal accruals and remain debt-free.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR270 crores, including VOPL capacity expansion, new product development and operational scalability. The ATBS capacity expansion was completed during FY26.

ATBS: a Phase 1 of 10,000 tonnes is commissioned. Total ATBS capacity is about 50,000 tonnes for lower molecular weight grades and about 40,000 tonnes for higher purity grades. Phase 2 (another 10,000 tonnes) expected by October 2026. Two-phase cost about INR250-300 crores.
CWIP was about INR210 crores at year-end, of which about INR60-70 crores is yet to be capitalised at VOPL. About INR120-125 crores of VOPL CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Pipeline products are downstream derivatives of MEHQ, butyl phenols and antioxidants, plus TAA, PTAP and 4-MAP at VOPL. Isoamylene derivatives were dropped. Monomers and polymers are under consideration but not confirmed.
Butyl phenol capacity of about 50,000 tonnes is at 70-75% utilisation with no space to expand.
demand_pricing: Demand softened from October 2025. Management says demand has since recovered, and ATBS is still growing at double-digit rates industry-wide.
ATBS pricing is stable and follows a formula-based mechanism. Management says it passes raw material and logistics price moves through to customers and holds margins.

AO faces undercutting and aggressive selling by Chinese producers. Management says ADD was not granted and has been reapplied, and it notes that 80-90% of ADD applications were rejected in the sector.
Raw material and logistics availability normalised after early disruption from the Iran war in Feb 2026. Logistics is described as stable.
ATBS end-use spans polymers for enhanced oil recovery, superabsorbents, personal care, detergents, mining and water treatment. Vinati sells to polymer makers, not directly to oilfield operators.

qa_highlights.question: What new products are in the pipeline, and when will they come online?
qa_highlights.answer: Most are downstream niche chemicals for fragrance, personal care, food-additive and plastics users. Two or three products are due in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue mix by product?
qa_highlights.answer: ATBS is about one-third and AO is 15-20%. IB is 10-12%, IBB is 10-12%, and customised and other products make up the rest, with overall ATBS and AO together around 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VOPL revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26. Management expects about INR100-120 crores in FY27 once reengineering finishes, with revenue from Q2/Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned in VOPL and how much CWIP is there?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40-50 crores of the FY27 capex goes to VOPL and about INR200 crores to the parent. VOPL CWIP of about INR120-125 crores is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATBS capacity and cost of the two expansion phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 50,000 tonnes (about 40,000 tonnes for higher-purity grades) with 10,000 tonnes per phase. The two phases cost about INR250-300 crores in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will AO and butyl phenol revenue reach the targeted INR700-800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is on track, with AO and butyl phenol revenue in the INR800-900 crore range within the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 26-27% EBITDA margin is a reasonable long-term level given expansions, new products and raw material swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AO growth lagged, and what is the status of the ADD?
qa_highlights.answer: AO growth was about 5% in FY26 because of aggressive Chinese undercutting. ADD was not granted, has been reapplied, and a decision could take 6-9 months.

risks_watch: AO margins and volumes depend on the anti-dumping duty decision, which could take another 6-9 months after reapplication, while Chinese players undercut prices.
VOPL revenue of INR100-120 crores in FY27 depends on finishing process reengineering by September 2026. The plant had teething troubles with its new process.
ATBS Phase 2 utilisation is expected to build mainly in FY28, and the plant is running at about 75-80% utilisation.
Butyl phenol capacity is at 70-75% utilisation with no room to expand, so growth may cut merchant sales.
Sector cyclicality has shortened, with sharp swings in raw material prices, logistics and customer destocking.
Management guidance rests on about 15% volume growth, a recovery from the October 2025 slowdown and IBB volumes resuming after the Iran war disruption.

524208|2026-03.headline: Aarti Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 2,422 crore and EBITDA 29% to INR 342 crore, with FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore.
524208|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,422 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 342 crore (up 29%) and PAT INR 137 crore (up 43%), helped by volume growth and higher utilisation. West Asia disruption raised benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene and methanol prices by over 60%, lifted freight costs and cut Middle East shipments, which are about 9-10% of revenue. Zone IV projects are delayed 3-4 months on contract labour shortages, with the bulk now expected in FY27. Management guided FY27 capex to INR 700-800 crore and aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite working-capital pressure.

segments.name: Energy applications
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue; volumes down 4% QoQ on lower Middle East exports. Expansion to 360 KTPA is on track and expected to commission soon. Middle East is about 9-10% of company revenue, mostly energy.

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Steady volume growth but margin pressure continues. A new $150 million multiyear agro intermediate contract runs to March 2030 with no incremental capex.

segments.name: Polymers
segments.commentary: Strong growth phase on EV-linked demand; MPDA continues to underperform due to Chinese competition.

segments.name: Dyes, pigments and paints
segments.commentary: Share of revenue about 10-11%. Demand pressure in 3,3'-DCBH globally, partly offset by domestic demand; some low-margin demand destruction possible in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Stable in the quarter; PNCB chain expected to benefit from China anti-involution from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore (about INR 150 crore a year is maintenance), funding Zone IV completion and a new INR 200-250 crore backward-integration contract.
Zone IV: calcium chloride and multipurpose plant to be commercialised within the quarter; remaining blocks commissioned through FY27 after a 3-4 month delay; initial revenue from Q2 FY27.
Management aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite higher working capital, as capex intensity falls and cash flow improves.
Tax rate guided at about 9-15% going forward.
Working capital target of 55-60 days, with the company currently above this level.
Augene (Superform JV) to commission around June-July 2026; recycling JV to commission in CY26.
Interest-cost and EBITDA potential from Zone IV and the UPL JV unchanged at INR 300-450 crore, but realisation may slip 6-7 months.
capex_capacity: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore; gross block expected at INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27.
Energy expansion to 360 KTPA on track for commissioning soon.
Contract labour availability in the capex region down 35%, delaying last-mile pipeline work.
Augene JV and recycling JV commissioning in 2026; DCB debottlenecking under way.
About 50% of the Bayer/Dicamba-linked asset is used for one intermediate, with steady volumes.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) rose over 60% in the quarter; some more than doubled.
Agro pricing is up sharply from January, but the company is holding spreads rather than absolute prices; full pass-through expected over 3-6 months.
NCB margins and pricing improved on China's anti-involution policy; DCB remains robust on EV demand.
MMA economics are volatile with gasoline-naphtha cracks ranging from negative to up $20/bbl; Middle East shipments physically halted, US shipments steady, Europe starting.
Physical supply of methanol (about a couple of months' cover) and sulfur (a few weeks' cover) is secure.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q4 margins, especially in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory impact was not significant; FX gain was about INR 10 crore in the quarter, and raw material costs also rose in March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9-10% of revenue on an annual average basis, mostly energy; product is being redirected elsewhere, with the full impact visible in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY27 capex fall and what is the breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore as guided, not reduced; FY27 guided at INR 700-800 crore mainly for Zone IV, the new long-term contract and about INR 150 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt high despite about INR 600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was a late-March term loan disbursement; net debt is about INR 4,300 crore, with bulk of cash used to repay debt in early April. Working capital rose INR 250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 freight and other-expense jump and inventory build?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rates rose from mid-February, exports were 57% of revenue, and US mix lengthened voyages; INR 409 crore stock build reflects goods in transit not yet recognised as revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Zone IV EBITDA and the net debt/EBITDA target at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost and operating-leverage initiatives are on track; the EBITDA potential is unchanged but may slip 6-7 months. Net debt/EBITDA was about 3.6x at year-end.

risks_watch: Middle East flows halted for 6-8 weeks; full Q1 FY27 impact on energy volumes depends on West Asia stabilisation.
Working capital and net debt rise if crude moves to USD 140-150/bbl.
Zone IV labour shortage and 3-4 month delay; check commissioning and first revenue in Q2 FY27.
Potential demand destruction in low-margin dyes and pigments over 3-6 months.
Unhedged USD 87 million FX loan; further rupee depreciation would add revaluation losses.
MPDA and agro margins remain under pressure from Chinese competition.

rows.why: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore with gross block rising to INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27, energy expansion to 360 KTPA near commissioning, and Augene JV due June-July 2026, though labour shortage (down 35%) delays the last-mile work 3-4 months.

rows.why: FY27 capex guided down to INR 700-800 crore from INR 1,125 crore in FY26, with about INR 150 crore a year of maintenance, and the focus is on optimising capex and deleveraging rather than new projects.

rows.why: Zone IV multipurpose and calcium chloride plant commercialisation in the quarter and a new INR 200-250 crore backward-integration contract are planned, but no specific new product names or launch dates beyond these were given.

rows.why: Management aims to cut net debt from about INR 4,300 crore (about 3.6x EBITDA) as capex falls to INR 700-800 crore, but working capital rose INR 250-300 crore and the bulk of the late-March cash repays debt in early April.

rows.why: Company is currently above the 55-60 day target after a INR 409 crore stock build (goods in transit), so release depends on freight and inventory normalising.

rows.why: Management guided the effective tax rate to about 9-15% going forward, with PAT FY26 at INR 419 crore.

524208|2026-06.headline: Aarti Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 2,627 crore and EBITDA 79% to Rs 385 crore, with management refusing to guarantee the run rate.
524208|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 2,627 crore (+41% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) were lifted by raw-material price pass-through, product mix, and inventory and FX gains, which management sized at roughly Rs 50-60 crore. Volumes fell sequentially (energy -17% QoQ, non-energy -7%, overall about -12%) amid West Asia disruption and high raw-material prices. Zone IV commissioning is delayed by 3-6 months due to labour shortages, and management declined to commit to a forward EBITDA run rate. The Augene JV is near commissioning, and FY27 capex remains on track at Rs 700-800 crore.

segments.name: Energy (Fuel Additives)
segments.commentary: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; West Asia share fell to about 2% from about 15%, and volumes were redirected to US, Africa, Europe and India. Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged about $15-18/bbl, and management expects the capacity to reach high utilisation in Q1 itself.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Polymers
segments.commentary: Demand was soft in Q1 on weak downstream US and China demand, and low shipments followed heavy Q4 FY26 bulk shipments to the US. Management expects recovery in Q2 and full-year growth.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Dyes & Pigments
segments.commentary: Demand remained subdued amid high raw-material prices and seasonality. Price increases in dyes and pigments and pharma were partly linked to China's VAT removal on the NCB chain.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Pharma and Agro
segments.commentary: Pharma demand was stable. Agrochemical volumes were marginally lower as customers resisted elevated raw-material-linked prices; recovery is expected in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800 crore retained; the Augene JV is included in this guidance, but management said Zone IV ramp-up may be slower than originally assumed.
Management declined to guide to a sustainable quarterly EBITDA run rate, citing plus/minus 15-20% monthly price volatility; it expects volume growth to offset lost inventory gains.
Augene JV (50:50, consolidated at PAT level) expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, with steady-state revenue retained at Rs 300-400 crore.
FY27 capex on track at Rs 700-800 crore; capex intensity expected to fall significantly from FY28.

Zone IV commissioning is delayed 3-6 months; the MPP is expected to produce first product in August 2026 and commissioning will be announced thereafter. Management expects 5-10 products in FY27 and 25-30 by FY28.
Sabic-linked backward-integration project commissioning expected around Sep-Oct 2027.
capex_capacity: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; management said there is no fixed limit on further expansion, and it will first demonstrate utilisation over the next 12 months.
Zone IV: 97% of equipment erected and 85% of piping complete across the five chemistry blocks; full manpower restored, with commissioning expected in FY27 and ramp-up over FY28-FY29.
PEDA project in market seeding and expected to commercialise soon; DCB debottlenecking to 140 KTPA under evaluation.
NCB chain debottlenecking is being evaluated within existing assets given demand in India.
Aarti Circularity plastic recycling plant with Re Sustainability slated for commissioning in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inflation (benzene, sulphur, methanol, aniline) was passed through to customers; high prices reduced purchasing power in dyes, selected agro and polymer compounds.
Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/bbl, which management described as healthy, while the energy business remains volatile.
Exports were 59% of revenue; US-bound DAP shipments carry 2-3 month voyage times that delay revenue recognition.
China's suspension of export tax rebates is creating opportunities for the NCB value chain.
Non-energy volumes fell on delayed purchasing in a high-price environment, with some supply-chain effects; management said Middle East exposure in non-energy is low.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FX and inventory gains in Q1, and what is the impact on the EBITDA base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a Rs 50-60 crore impact but said it is hard to quantify because of intra-quarter volatility; the CFO said FX gains came from squaring off import positions as the rupee moved in a Rs 92-97 range, and management advised treating this as operating profit with no forward commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin lower sequentially despite the inventory and FX benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly gross margin is not a reliable steady-state indicator, citing timing of raw-material purchases and product placement, freight, lower volumes raising operating costs, and the chemical business running on absolute rupee deltas rather than percentage margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zone IV delay affect FY28 EBITDA visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MPP and calcium chloride unit are on track, but the five chemistry blocks face slower ramp-up than originally planned, and it will share ramp-up details once the blocks commission.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Augene JV affect reported EBITDA, and is it in the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that the Rs 1,800 crore FY28 guidance includes Augene EBITDA, while the Re Aarti JV is not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY28; reporting treatment for JVs is yet to be finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the energy business's volume, capacity and market share sustainable once West Asia normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business remains in a market-development phase; the portfolio is diversified across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India (Southeast Asia not yet penetrated), and it expects utilisation gains rather than volume shifts when West Asia reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing absolute sales volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it removed absolute sales numbers from slides because they were being used in an unfavourable way, and now gives energy/non-energy volume growth plus value-chain utilisation ranges.

risks_watch: Zone IV: five chemistry blocks face a 3-6 month delay and slower ramp-up; the MPP first product is expected in August 2026, and the FY28 Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance (which includes Augene) depends on this ramp-up.

Earnings quality: management said FX and inventory gains (Rs 50-60 crore, roughly Rs 47 crore per an analyst's figure) helped Q1, and it declined to commit to a forward quarterly EBITDA run rate given plus/minus 15-20% monthly price swings.

Energy seasonality and West Asia: management expects winter weakness from late October to December, and West Asia volumes (share down to about 2% from about 15%) are not yet restored; utilisation of the 360 KTPA fuel additives capacity is the key test over the next 12 months.
Working capital and leverage: management said working capital expanded and debt and finance costs rose in Q1; watch debt levels as imported-raw-material inventory (1-1.5 months) carries price risk.

Augene JV commissioning in Q2 FY27 and the Re Aarti JV reporting treatment, which management has yet to finalise; watch the Rs 300-400 crore steady-state revenue assumption and PAT-level consolidation.
key_quotes: In our guidance, we had given the numbers that will come from the capex-led programs and in capex-led, Zone IV was a significant contributor.
I would again hesitate to hazard a guess.
So we did not see the EBITDA run rate can be maintained.
The actual sales numbers is something that we have removed from the slides because they was getting utilized in a situation which was not favourable for the company.

524332|2026-03.headline: BCL Industries FY26 revenue INR2,913 crore, EBITDA INR251 crore (+18%), margin 8.6%; 150 KLPD Bathinda unit nearing commercial output.
524332|2026-03.overview: BCL Industries reported FY26 total revenue of INR2,913 crore, with EBITDA up 18% YoY to INR251 crore and margin up 130 bps to 8.6%. Q4 PAT was INR126 crore, up 23% YoY at a 4.3% margin. Ethanol allocation from OMCs was lower than expected, so the company diverted output to ENA and SBF, which kept utilisation near full but pressured realisations. The packaged edible oil business was exited, while the refinery and trading businesses continued. The 150 KLPD Bathinda grain-based distillery is in testing, taking total installed capacity to 900 KLPD.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue largely in line with FY25 despite packaged edible oil exit

financial_highlights.metric: Distillery EBITDA margin Q4 FY26 (as cited by analyst)

less than 7%; INR120 crore on interest subvention at about 4.25%

segments.name: Potable liquor (PML, Punjab Made Liquor)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales of almost 4.5 lakh cases, up 20% YoY. Punjab Special Whiskey relaunched in glass bottle and Punjab Raspberry added. Management cited 18-20% PML market growth.

segments.commentary: Revenue under INR749 crore with EBITDA margin of 3.74% in FY26. Packaged edible oil exited; soft oil refinery continues, with bulk supply expected at INR700-800 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 revenue and EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR300 crore from the 150 KLPD unit at full utilisation and similar or slightly better EBITDA margins as overheads stay flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new 150 KLPD unit run at 100% in year one?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects at least 75% utilisation from Q2 FY27, with rated capacity by early July after a 15-day trial production.

qa_highlights.question: Can distillery EBITDA hold at 11.8% in Q4 given peers guide 12-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold, citing the paddy straw boiler and consolidation of vegetable oil operations. Pure ethanol could reach 15% at full OMC allocation, but ENA/SBF are raw-material linked and not fixed-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year strategy and real estate exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate projects date from 2005-2010 and are winding down with no new projects. Focus is biofuel: Fatehabad ethanol, later CBG and sustainable aviation fuel, and a debt-free balance sheet within 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR300-335 crore including fund and non-fund based; INR120 crore on interest subvention at about 4.25%; average cost below 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the OCF improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital release is not one-off: no capex currently, ENA/SBF cash-and-carry sales, OMC receivables cut to 21 days, and edible oil inventory liquidation adds to it.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit packaged edible oil and sell land?
qa_highlights.answer: City unit had to move due to red-category restrictions. Machines were shifted or sold, and about 18 acres of city land is being sold for about INR30 crore. Proceeds go to cash and expansion.

rows.why: OMC receivables cut to about 21 days, ENA/SBF sold cash-and-carry, and residual edible oil inventory being liquidated within 4-6 months, which management says is not a one-off release.

rows.label: E30 blending and flex-fuel norms
rows.why: Government evaluating E30 and E85/E100 norms; management says higher crude prices make blending more profitable for OMCs, but no decision date was given and ethanol allocation remains below capacity.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Bathinda ramp, the paddy straw boiler and the policy outlook (E30, flex fuel), but declined to commit on biodiesel pricing and distillery margins citing commodity risk; analysts pushed on whether the 11.8% distillery margin can hold against peers guiding 12-15%.

524332|2026-06.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
524332|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 820 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)
from 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26

segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 12.41% in Q1 FY27 versus 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26. ENA volume rose to 19,376 KL from 7,960 KL YoY, but ENA realisation fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. The 115 TPH paddy straw boiler meets 100% of steam and power needs.

segments.name: Country liquor (PML)
segments.commentary: Sold 6,37,993 boxes, up 42% QoQ and 46% YoY. Punjab Raspberry launched in Q4 FY26 and Jamun Vodka in July 2026. Management targets 30 lakh cases this year out of a market of about 1.25 crore cases per annum in Punjab.

segments.commentary: Exit completed, including closure of the Bathinda oil and vanaspati unit. Soft oil refinery and trading continue as legacy operations. Revenue decline was mainly from this exit.

Order book described as full for about the next three months, supported by OMC allocation of about 4.5 crore litres from a Supreme Court order covering until November.

Working capital limit to be reduced by INR 50 crore in August 2026; management aims to bring working capital utilisation towards zero over about 1.5 years.
