Management said maize-based ethanol to OMCs is profitable, while FCI-rice-based ethanol is near cost. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same. Blended average EBITDA is about 12%, roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA.
Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter. Current maize price is about INR 25/kg, and management said ENA prices have been revised upwards.
DDGS prices have eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for both maize and rice based.
Management expects ethanol demand to improve only slightly next year, as sugarcane-based ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel demand is a long-term driver, with few FFV models on sale so far.
Management said E20 is in place for about 18 months with no major vehicle damage seen, but blending expansion beyond E20 may be delayed. Isobutanol and SAF are cited as future demand sources.

qa_highlights.question: At what price is ethanol sold to private players, and is it FCI rice or maize based?
qa_highlights.answer: Private ethanol buyers are mainly Reliance at an average ex-factory price of about INR 58/litre. Private buyers use damaged grain, while the company's own FCI-rice ethanol is tied to 40% of OMC allocation. Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Cause of the Bathinda fire and safeguards for other plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the likely cause was static charge, possibly from clothing of a nearby worker. The company has added facilities to prevent such incidents and called it rare.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for grain ethanol after E20 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is expected to improve only slightly next year because sugarcane ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel is a long-term driver, with isobutanol and SAF as additional sources, and cooking fuel use was also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics across FCI-rice, OMC maize and ENA/private ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: FCI-rice ethanol to OMCs is near cost. Maize-based ethanol to OMCs is quite profitable. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same, with blended EBITDA margin near 12%, or roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA on average.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Goyal bio-CNG, biodiesel and the 250 KLPD Goyal Distillery project?
qa_highlights.answer: Bio-CNG is under active evaluation after a favourable new policy, though paddy straw is tricky, mainly due to by-product sale. The company is not making biodiesel. The 250 KLPD Goyal project is on hold pending industry clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project on hold, and does maize oil locally sourced change this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biodiesel prices are not remunerative and biodiesel feedstock is largely imported, so government has focused less on it. Isobutanol is being tested to promote indigenous feedstock. Management said the government's view could not be commented on.

qa_highlights.question: Malt plant and IMFL entry timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Malt plant is still at conceptualisation with no timeline. IMFL entry is being worked on and is hoped for next year. Management views country liquor as more profitable than competitive IMFL.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the 250 KLPD Fatehabad project after the July statement about construction by August?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash against the ethanol policy. Machinery orders are finalised and the company is waiting before starting construction.

qa_highlights.question: Land sale timing, debt repayment and release of pledged shares?
qa_highlights.answer: No update on the land sale, as Bathinda real estate is slow and there is no rush. Working capital utilisation is low, some small loans were repaid, and banks released pledged shares. Working capital limit to be cut by INR 50 crore in August.

qa_highlights.question: Trend in DDGS realisations and Punjab country liquor market share?
qa_highlights.answer: DDGS prices eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for maize and rice based. Punjab country liquor market is about 1.25 crore cases a year, with a 30 lakh case target for this year.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook, total debt level and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes should stay about flat until the 200 KLPD unit restarts in about 15 days. Working capital utilisation is about INR 60 crore, with total debt around INR 360 crore including working capital. Debt rises only with a new capex project, and working capital is to be run towards zero over about 1.5 years. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol mixing in diesel, E20 damage, and government mandates beyond E20?
qa_highlights.answer: Management distinguished ethanol-in-diesel, which faces a flash point issue, from isobutanol, which it said is still under trial and not shelved. It said E20 has run 18 months without major vehicle damage, but further blending could be delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance cover and stock lost in the 200 KL tank, and expected restart?
qa_highlights.answer: The tank held about 90,000 litres at the time. The plant is being repaired and is expected to restart in about 15 days. Management said both stock loss and profit loss are covered by insurance, and the P&L impact is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of the Supreme Court-allowed OMC volume and the order book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is among the biggest gainers, with about 4.5 crore litres from both units under the Supreme Court order, covering until November. The order book is more than full for the next 3 months. Flex fuel demand will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Current maize price, margin outlook and state subsidy for CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize is about INR 25/kg now. ENA prices have been revised upwards, but raw material and fuel costs are rising. Management guided margins at about 10-12% with variation. Haryana has a CBG policy and the central policy is also favourable.

524342|2026-03.headline: Indo Borax Q4 FY26 revenue rose 25.7% to Rs 63.01 crore and PAT rose 41.9% to Rs 14.53 crore, with new promoter Zenrock in control.
524342|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was Rs 63.01 crore (up 25.7% YoY), with EBITDA of Rs 12.82 crore (20.4% margin) and PAT of Rs 14.53 crore (21.5% margin). FY26 revenue was Rs 215.45 crore (up 22.9%), EBITDA was flat at Rs 44.16 crore, and PAT was Rs 50.27 crore (up from Rs 42.51 crore). Management said the company changed control in January 2026 with Zenrock Chemicals as new promoter, and a new leadership team took over. A special dividend of Rs 30 per share plus a final dividend of Rs 10 per share (total Rs 40) was declared after monetising non-core assets. Management guided to Rs 250-plus crore revenue next year and 20-35% growth, but gave no formal numeric guidance, and no dividend policy has yet been declared.

financial_highlights.change: +41.9% YoY vs Rs 10.24 crore; PAT margin +250 bps

segments.name: Boric Acid Technical
segments.commentary: About 85-90% of current business per CEO; roughly 15,000-plus tons in FY26. Capacity is 20,000 tpa nameplate but historically 15,000-16,000 tons output, and it is running at full utilisation.

segments.name: Boric Acid I.P. Grade
segments.commentary: About 900 tons in FY26. Realisation is 10-15% higher than technical grade, using the same equipment with tighter specifications. Management intends to expand its share.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: 980 tons in FY26 (about 600 tons two years ago), out of 6,000 tpa capacity, so utilisation is low. Target is about 1,500 tons next year. Realisation is about Rs 150/kg and the Indian market is about 8,500 tons.

segments.name: Boron Oxide
segments.commentary: 4,000 tpa capacity project under construction; first lot expected in three to four quarters. Management pegs realisation at 2-3x Boric Acid pricing (cited 2.5x).

segments.name: Other / traded products
segments.commentary: Borax Pentahydrate (mostly traded), Gypsum (by-product, largest by volume), and other products together about 400 tons in FY26 per the CEO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about Rs 250-plus crore from debottlenecking and higher DOT sales, subject to raw material pricing.
Management said it is 'definitely surpassing' Q4 numbers in Q1 FY27 (April), though it did not give figures.
Revenue growth guided at 20-35% (about Rs 40-60 crore increments), with EBITDA margin maintained at or above the current 20-21% level.
Boron Oxide first lot expected in three to four quarters; CAPEX to be completed within FY27 plus a few months.
Capex plans for the next year are still under discussion and will be shared after board approval; a stated dividend policy is being framed but not yet declared.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity is about 26,000 tpa: 20,000 tpa Boric Acid and 6,000 tpa DOT. Boron Oxide 4,000 tpa is a project under way.

Boric Acid effective output is about 15,000-16,000 tons versus 20,000 nameplate due to planned shutdowns and raw material gaps. Management aims to add 1,000-1,500 tons through debottlenecking and tighter shutdown planning.
Possible Boric Acid capacity expansion is under internal board debate, not yet approved.
Management says cash on hand is sufficient for the capex budgeted over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Indian Boric Acid market is about 40,000 tpa, projected to reach about 53,000 tons by 2030 (8% CAGR). Steel and refractory accounts for 55-60% of demand. The company claims about 50% share.
Realisation was about Rs 127-128/kg in FY26 versus Rs 114-115/kg in FY25. EBITDA is about Rs 28-29/kg (20-21%) for Boric Acid.
Management said Boric Acid is sold out, and growth in value depends on price pass-through. Raw material costs rose sharply due to geopolitics, but management said pass-through has been achieved.
Raw material (boron ore/Ulexite) sourcing is concentrated in Turkey. The company is diversifying to South America and North America.
Top 10-15 customers have been stable for years, and management said the company has a premium price because of technical specifications, especially in steel refractories.

qa_highlights.question: Sales mix across Boric Acid Technical, I.P., DOT and Boron Oxide, and the EBITDA margin trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Boric Acid is about 90% of sales, DOT about 8%, others about 2%. Boric Acid EBITDA is about Rs 28-29/kg (20-21%), down from the 25-30% management said it earned in past years, and management said it expects to hold 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Without new capex, management said revenue could rise 25-30% over about 1.5 years, and up to 20-35% depending on raw material inflation and pricing. The base is about Rs 215 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Boron Oxide timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: First lot is expected in three to four quarters. Management said realisation is 2-3x Boric Acid, so it used 2.5x in its estimate.

qa_highlights.question: How did the new promoter's team (Zenrock) and the special dividend fit with reinvestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash was not fully distributed and enough remains for two years of budgeted capex. The dividend came from selling non-core assets (flats, cars) and was a one-time payout shared with old shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 revenue could be Rs 250 crore-plus, with growth of 20-35% and EBITDA margins held at or above current levels. Absolute numbers were not given to a retail participant due to insider trading policy.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge and debt (raised by one participant)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company has zero debt. A participant cited Rs 400 crore of debt, and management referred the query to its IR team without answering.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility (boron ore sourced largely from Turkey) and geopolitical pressure on margins. Management says about 2 quarters of hedged purchasing.
DOT utilisation is very low (980 tons of 6,000 tpa). Management gave no clear reason for the slow growth, and a participant questioned quality or customer issues.
Governance and disclosure: promoter shares reportedly 100% pledged (not answered), a conflicting debt claim of Rs 400 crore, and a board-approved dividend policy still pending.
Zenrock's operating background was questioned; management said Zenrock is a holding company and the operating team is led by industry professionals.
Boron Oxide, new product lines and I.P. grade ramp are still at exploratory or project stage; timing is uncertain.

rows.why: Boric Acid runs at full utilisation on 15,000-16,000 tons versus 20,000 tpa nameplate, and management says capex plans for next year will be shared after board approval; a possible Boric Acid expansion is under board debate, but the size is undisclosed and the dividend policy is still being framed.

rows.why: Realisation rose to about Rs 127-128/kg in FY26 from Rs 114-115/kg in FY25 (about +11%), and management says pass-through has been achieved, though growth depends on raw material pricing.

rows.why: A Rs 30 special plus Rs 10 final (Rs 40 total) was paid from non-core asset sales and a dividend policy is being framed but not declared; cash is said to be sufficient for two years of budgeted capex.

rows.why: Promoter shares reportedly 100% pledged (not answered), a Rs 400 crore debt claim was referred to IR while the CFO said zero debt, and the Zenrock operating track record was questioned.

tone.note: Management was confident on the near-term run rate (Q1 FY27 'not less than' Q4) and the 20-35% FY27 growth range, but evasive on DOT growth history, Boron Oxide applications, capex size, pledge and debt; analysts pressed on governance and the Rs 400 crore debt claim.

524342|2026-06.headline: Indo Borax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.3% to Rs 70.36 crore and PAT rose 59.3% to Rs 16.25 crore, but management guided Q2 to be softer.
524342|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue was Rs 70.36 crore (+31.34% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 19.8 crore (+62.16%) at a 28.1% margin and PAT of Rs 16.25 crore (+59.31%) at a 22.3% margin, with EPS of Rs 5.07. Management attributed the quarter to improved capacity utilisation, higher realisations and new leadership after the Zenrock promoter change. The call was dominated by the proposed acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences from its promoters for about Rs 250 crore, funded partly by internal accruals, asset sales and a term loan. Management said Q2 margins will fall versus Q1 because of raw material inflation from the war and the monsoon-weak quarter, and reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 250-260 crore revenue at about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Boric acid (technical and IP grade)
segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from boric acid; IP grade is 7-8% of boric acid volume (about 100 tonnes vs 1,500 tonnes technical, per the speaker). Capacity utilisation expected at 96-98% of practical capacity, with output rising to about 18,000 tonnes this year from 15,917 tonnes last year.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume about 900 tonnes; FY27 target 1,500 tonnes against 6,000 tonnes nameplate. Contributes about 9% of revenue this year vs 7% last year. Margin expected broadly in line with boric acid.

segments.name: Kronox Lab Sciences (proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: Vadodara-based listed specialty chemicals company with 185 products across excipients, reagents, API and nutraceuticals. Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore planned in phases over 18-24 months, with benefits from FY29 and full impact in FY30-31; management expects 3-3.5x current revenue post-capex.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance Rs 250-260 crore vs Rs 215 crore in FY26, with EBITDA margin about 20% and absolute EBITDA growth of about 11-12%.
Q2 expected to be softer on monsoon-weak volumes and raw material inflation from the ongoing war; margins not expected to match Q1's 28.1%.
Q3 expected to pick up again.
Boron oxide and boric acid capacity additions planned; management expects these to lift margins in FY28.
Capex of about Rs 50 crore over the next two to three years (Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore, boric acid Rs 20-25 crore, plus contingency); the Rs 50 crore figure is a business-plan rounding.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity about 26,000 tonnes per year at Pithampur: about 20,000 tpa boric acid and 6,000 tpa DOT.
Practical output expected at about 18,000 tonnes this year vs 15,917 tonnes last year, after planned maintenance days.
Boron oxide capex about Rs 20 crore; boric acid capex Rs 20-25 crore, with plant size flexible between 5,000 and 20,000 tpa.
Kronox Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore in phases: first phase about Rs 55-60 crore; benefits from FY29, full impact FY30-31; execution 18-24 months.
Management says there is capacity upside of 15-20% at existing Indo Borax plants through process changes.
demand_pricing: Indian boric acid market estimated at about 40,000 tpa, projected to grow about 8% CAGR to about 53,000 tpa by 2030; steel and refractory is 55-60% of demand.

Boric acid prices moved from about Rs 127/kg early in FY27 to about Rs 155-160/kg, per management, as costs rose during the war; some pass-through still pending and spot prices were soft in Q2 seasonally.
Management says Indo Borax prices at a premium to market (market plus), citing specifications.
DOT: management cites about 8,500 tonnes of imports and about 10,000 tonnes total market; Indo Borax targets 1,500 tonnes.
Kronox's Indian market growing about 11% CAGR per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kronox's previous promoter exit, and what is the status of the Dahej capex delayed by environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on the promoter's reasons. It said the Dahej land and design are ready, audits and studies are complete, and customers have been approached; the capex is to be executed as a first priority once the deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kronox to be merged into Indo Borax, and what is the group acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet on merger; both entities will continue as separate listed companies for now. Future acquisitions by Zenrock will be evaluated case by case; Indo Borax will focus on integration.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 250 crore to promoters. Rs 134-135 crore from internal accruals plus Rs 48-50 crore from sale of two Mumbai office properties. Enmetazobactam in Europe depends on formulary and government tender inclusion; South Europe inclusion is driving sales growth. Enmetazobactam treated about 30,000 patients in the last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak sales and timing for Enmetazobactam?
qa_highlights.answer: Lifetime sales are still held at $1-2 billion over the patent life. Peak sales are now expected in the fourth or fifth year after launch rather than the third.

qa_highlights.question: How will Cefiderocol capacity utilisation ramp?

qa_highlights.question: Will US ANDAs be filed from a CMO first?

524372|2026-06.headline: Orchid Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 15% YoY to INR304 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR25 crore, on a merged Dhanuka basis.

Revenue from operations rose to INR304 crore from INR263 crore, and gross margin improved about 3 percentage points to 33%. EBITDA rose to INR25 crore from INR10 crore a year earlier. Management described the quarter as mediocre and said recovery would be gradual, with cephalosporin pricing still under pressure from overcapacity. Project milestones for 7-ACA (March 2027) and cefiderocol (commissioning December 2026) were reiterated.

524394|2026-03.headline: Vimta Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.6% YoY to INR1,120 million, with EBITDA margin of 37.6% and a net debt-free balance sheet.

Management said Q4 was helped by pre-clinical and seasonal food testing, but some expected growth did not materialise, and the company missed its earlier INR500 million annualised run-rate goal. The company entered biologics contract research (biologics and peptides) in FY26, with FY27 framed as a year of execution with no meaningful revenue expected yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Unichem margins and inventory?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Lyka Labs, Krebs Bio and other subsidiaries?

524494|2026-06.headline: Ipca Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 21% to INR2,788 crores and EBITDA margin reached 22.88%; FY27 growth guidance raised to 14-16%.
524494|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR2,788 crores, with consolidated EBITDA of INR638 crores (22.88% margin) versus INR425 crores (18.39%) a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA rose about 34% to INR557 crores. Management raised FY27 guidance: revenue growth to 14-16% (from 12-13%) and consolidated EBITDA margin to around 23% (from around 22%). Exports (+34%), domestic formulations (+13%) and institutional generics (+107%, helped by about INR40 crores of shipments slipping from March to April) drove the quarter. Management said margin gains came mainly from lower personnel and manufacturing costs as a share of sales, not material savings.

FY28 guidance to be given with Q4 results.

qa_highlights.question: Why did acute underperform, and what is the India outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed underperformance, citing IPM growth of 4.5% vs Ipca's 8.9% acute growth. Antimalarials fell about 24%. Pain management grew about 13%, CV and diabetes about 17%, CNS about 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12-13% guidance hold, and what is the institutional outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was raised to 14-16%. Institutional growth is expected to be single digit, since the Q1 spike was largely about INR40 crores of delayed shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the US launch plans, and can growth reach 20-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3-4 Ipca launches and 7-8 combined Ipca and Unichem launches a year. Mid-teens growth (15-17%) is possible; source-change approvals are progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Will material cost pressure hit margins in the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: No margin pressure expected; material cost should fall slightly relative to sales. Q1 margin gains came mainly from personnel and manufacturing cost ratios.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation or price renegotiation affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices are rising, not being renegotiated down. FX adds to revenue and is partly offset by dollar-linked costs such as freight, testing, salaries and non-trading offices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about INR193 crores with a INR70 crore term loan at year-end, repaid next year. No short-term borrowings. Interest cost to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: Where will margins settle over 2-3 years, and what are the biotech plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years, with Ipca standalone up to about 30%. About 7 biosimilar candidates, mostly off-patent. Clinical revenue expected in FY29-30.

524558|2026-03.headline: Neuland Q4 FY26 revenue rose 134.9% YoY to INR788.7 crore and FY26 PAT reached INR363.1 crore, with management flagging lumpiness and weaker Q3.
524558|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR788.7 crore, up 134.9% YoY, led by CMS (commercial manufacturing) projects, which contributed over two-thirds of revenue. Gross margin was 62.1% and EBITDA INR319.4 crore (40.5% margin), which management said should not be read as a run-rate. FY26 revenue grew 37.1% to INR2,053.1 crore, EBITDA rose to INR603.4 crore (29.4% margin) and PAT to INR363.1 crore, but free cash flow was negative INR49.4 crore as working capital days rose to 137. Management said FX tailwinds helped and that the business remains lumpy, with Q3 FY26 muted.

segments.name: CMS (commercial manufacturing services)
segments.commentary: Drove Q4 growth and contributed over two-thirds of Q4 revenue. Growth came from volume ramp-up of previously commercialized products plus one new commercialization in FY26; management expects one commercialization in FY27 and one or two later.

segments.name: GDS (development services)
segments.commentary: Softer in FY26 per management. Substantial resources deployed across development, customer engagement and capability building for growth in the short, medium and long term.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Large-scale peptide commercial facility due to be ready by July 2026 as scheduled; 8-10 peptide programs in development, mostly early-stage, with no near- or mid-term revenue expected from the publicly announced early-stage program.

guidance_outlook: No formal quantitative guidance to be given going forward, but management cited 18-20% CAGR as an aspirational, non-linear potential over about 5 years.
FY26 was expected to be a strong year versus FY24; management said Q4 and FY26 performance met expectations, slightly better helped by favourable exchange rates.
Working capital days of 137 expected to normalize in FY27.

ROCE expected to moderate as the company enters longer capital deployment cycles.

Capex cash outflow FY26 INR397.1 crore.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth aided by shipments made as the rupee depreciated; management put the currency benefit at roughly 10-12% by analyst estimate, which management did not dispute.
Management said volatility comes from shipment timing and newer high-value molecules, and does not expect a return to a steady quarterly run-rate soon.
Funding decline in early-stage biotech discovery has not yet hit the business, which focuses on IND-filed molecules entering Phase I onwards; funnel effect expected over time.
Peptide CDMO market estimated by outside consultants at USD 5-6 billion, supported by GLP-1 and next-generation peptide pipelines.
Freight costs rose late in Q4 due to the Middle East conflict; raw material coverage and price volatility being tracked.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the CDMO growth beyond currency, and were there any order bunching effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth came from existing pipeline, recently commercialized molecules and volume ramp-up, with one new commercialization in FY26. Some volatility is shipment-based and may even out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the early-stage peptide contract a near-term revenue driver?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it is very early-stage with no near- or mid-term revenue expected; it will take at least a few years for commercial benefit. Neuland has 8-10 peptide programs in development.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Esperion (bempedoic acid) change of ownership on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name customers due to confidentiality. It said supply agreements typically carry inherited clauses, change of ownership does not automatically disrupt supply, and it would flag any short-term issues if seen.

qa_highlights.question: Should investors rely on the 18-20% CAGR and how should margins be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 18-20% a fair but non-linear assumption and aspirational over five years. It said budgets are conservative, so margins tend to beat expectations, and it declined to give H1 vs H2 margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capital allocation becoming longer-term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at around INR2,000 crore revenue, the company will add hundreds of crore a year in capex, so it must build production blocks ahead of demand to engage new clients including big pharma.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CEO and MD role change from Sucheth to Saharsh effective April 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a pre-planned role separation: Saharsh focuses on day-to-day operations given his end-to-end CDMO build role, and Sucheth moves to a longer-term role covering the Neuland Foundation, enterprise risk and sustainability.

524654|2026-03.headline: Natural Capsules posted FY26 EBITDA loss of Rs 1.56 crore (-0.83% margin) on revenue of Rs 187.20 crore; FY27 guidance targets Rs 274 crore consolidated revenue.
524654|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 55% QoQ and 30% YoY to Rs 58.45 crore, with EBITDA recovering to Rs 1.33 crore (2.28% margin), helped by about Rs 6 crore of deferred Puducherry dispatches. For FY26, revenue grew 11% to Rs 187.20 crore, but EBITDA turned negative and net loss reached Rs 24.66 crore, driven by the Puducherry shutdown and pre-commercial API subsidiary costs. Commercial API sales started at the Tumkur facility in Q4 FY26, and a contract manufacturing deal with Fermbox Bio was signed. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs 274 crore, with restoring capsule-segment profitability as the primary target, while balance-sheet and liquidity pressure remained a stated concern.

segments.name: Gelatin capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 gelatin revenue about Rs 163 crore, against a guidance of about Rs 171 crore; Puducherry shutdown cost about Rs 6 crore. Management cites a 12-13% EBITDA margin, with lines running above 93% utilisation.

segments.name: HPMC capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue only about Rs 8 crore against a Rs 25 crore target, with about Rs 3 crore from the US that stopped after July 2025. Installed capacity rose from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum with the new HPMC line; management cites about 18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: API (Natural Biogenetics / Natural Biogenex, Tumkur)
segments.commentary: Commercial API sales began in Q4 FY26, with about Rs 9 crore of API revenue in that quarter. Domestic API margins are guided at 2-3% gross and still negative at EBITDA; fixed cost is about Rs 15 crore a year. Utilisation is about 25-30%.

segments.name: Fermbox contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Contract manufacturing with revenue sharing; FY27 forecast about Rs 14 crore with about 20% EBITDA assumed. Fermbox plans about Rs 60 crore of downstream equipment on site, owned by them.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue of about Rs 274 crore: gelatin about Rs 170 crore, HPMC about Rs 20 crore, domestic API about Rs 70 crore, Fermbox about Rs 14 crore.
HPMC revenue expected only from H2 FY27, subject to US customer machine-suitability approvals; FY27 HPMC base case assumes utilisation below 50%.
Management expects a very low consolidated net margin in FY27 and said EBITDA at API level could still be negative; restoring capsule-segment profitability is the primary FY27 target.
PLI-linked minimum import price benefits excluded from guidance; prednisolone and dexamethasone commercial-scale production targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27, betamethasone for Q4 FY27 per the call.
WHO GMP certification targeted in the next quarter; CEP filing and WHO GMP inspection around Q2 FY27; USFDA around Q3/Q4 FY27. Management said USFDA timeline is about 24 months.
Total debt expected at Rs 100-110 crore in FY27 and FY28, with annual repayments of Rs 10-12 crore; possible additional borrowing of Rs 20 crore over two years.
Rs 240-250 crore API revenue target retained for FY29, needing an additional Rs 25-30 crore to complete two clean rooms.
capex_capacity: New HPMC line commissioned in FY26 takes installed capacity from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum; ready for double-zero production, with revenue expected from H2 FY27 subject to US approvals. Each HPMC line is about 750 million capsules a year, and two lines give about 1.5 billion.
Tumkur API facility: utilisation about 25-30%; management says the fixed cost burden is about Rs 15 crore a year.
Fermentation capacity freed up: about 40% spare after the enzymatic route, with Fermbox to use spare capacity under a no-compete clause.
Reaching the Rs 240-250 crore API target requires about Rs 25-30 crore to finish two clean rooms; infrastructure is already in place.
Pending HPMC approvals are machine-suitability checks: the new machine was installed in March 2026 and is in validation, with two to three months of customer stability testing.
demand_pricing: US Neutra/wellness demand is weak after the 2025 tariffs. Management expects improvement in 3-6 months, and HPMC exports to Mexico and Brazil are now the main export markets.

Steroidal API pricing in India is pressured by Chinese overcapacity. Management says Indian prices are much lower than Chinese export prices and sometimes below cost; generic-customer API margins are in the single digits.
Prednisolone and dexamethasone trial batches are about 10% above Chinese cost at kilo scale; the government's minimum import price on four products could close this gap.
Domestic API volumes are price-sensitive, and raw-material prices have risen after the Iran-US conflict hit petrochemical supply, per management.
Management said the company has about 36 days of order backlog across capsule types.

qa_highlights.question: How will management prioritise bandwidth and working capital across about five concurrent initiatives with near-zero cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Dedicated teams run each business; management said liquidity is a real pressure. Options under review include a BIRAC RDI application, preferential allotment (with promoter participation), and a rights issue, with limited promoter dilution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 HPMC revenue assumption, and what if approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case is about Rs 20 crore of HPMC revenue, against about Rs 8 crore in FY26. Management did not quantify the impact of a delay.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Natural Biogenex claw-back linked to FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the claw-back refers to FY29 figures, is already in the shareholders' agreement, and there is no current discussion on extending it.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are assumed for FY27 capsules?
qa_highlights.answer: HPMC is assumed at 18% EBITDA and gelatin at about 13%, the same as the Q4 FY26 level, with some upside from a weaker rupee.

qa_highlights.question: Was PLI income received in FY26, and what is assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI income was received in FY26, and none is included in FY27 forecasts because of timing uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the API guidance rely on Q4 run-rate, and what is the EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: API guidance is based on Q4 API revenue of about Rs 9 crore, growing gradually. Domestic API EBITDA is expected to be negative to low single-digit, and consolidated net margin very low.

qa_highlights.question: How big can the Fermbox contract become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could grow well beyond Rs 14 crore, with multiple products from Europe and the US and a better profit share; the Rs 50 crore scenario was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY26 API target missed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited yield gaps on PLI products, the failed Chinese technology support, and volatile intermediate prices; intermediate-based domestic sales started only in December 2025 and the Chinese yield consultant visa did not come through.

risks_watch: Liquidity and balance-sheet pressure: near-zero cash, a loss-making consolidated P&L, and fundraising options still open.
HPMC revenue depends on US machine-suitability and stability approvals, and US demand is still weak.

Regulatory timelines (WHO GMP in Q2 FY27, USFDA in about 24 months) have slipped in the past, per analyst questions.
Steroidal API pricing and Chinese overcapacity; raw-material cost inflation from petrochemical disruptions.

524669|2026-03.headline: Hester Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 22% and PAT 174% YoY; FY26 consolidated PAT nearly doubled on 7% revenue growth.

Consolidated revenue grew 22% in Q4 and 7% for FY26, with full-year PAT almost doubling, partly aided by an exceptional gain from the partial divestment of Texas Lifesciences. Poultry Healthcare led growth (+41% in Q4, +21% for FY26), while Animal Healthcare lagged on tender delays. Management said Animal Healthcare demand is intact and expects recovery from Q1 FY27.

Competition is three or four private animal vaccine producers, with most governments having small state-owned units and most vaccines imported.

qa_highlights.answer: Exports to other African countries are invoiced in USD; local sales are in local currency. Management declined to give the local versus other-country split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the high Q4 poultry revenue and ~30% margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an endeavour to continue and that the level is a base to sustain, citing product mix and bottom-line focus, but could not predict external factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why were bad debt write-offs about INR 6.5 crore, and will they fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it reflects provisioning on debtors plus identification and write-off of some old unrecovered debts. Management expects the figure to reduce, though not to be alarming.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables of INR 92 crore look high versus revenue; what is being done on working capital and is the new BSL-3 facility being used?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Animal Healthcare in FY27 and will subsidiaries break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged tender delays through FY26 that did not go to plan. It said Animal Healthcare picked up from Q4 and will recover from this quarter. No subsidiary breakeven timeline was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hester's share in pet vaccination?
qa_highlights.answer: None, as the company has no commercialised pet vaccines yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage come as debt falls and capacity is in place, and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant capacity is installed and utilisation will be optimised, but evolving regulatory requirements and new technologies mean future capital needs cannot be ruled out.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state revenue mix between poultry and animal healthcare and what net debt/equity level is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is around 50:50, as two years ago, and FY26 skewed toward poultry. CFO said debt is about INR 70 crore (down from INR 102 crore) and debt-to-equity of 0.19x is comfortable.

qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said operating cash flow is positive and conversion has improved. Rajiv Gandhi said higher receivables are seasonal and not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Africa operation's slow scale-up a natural gestation period or a tendering problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said it is a formative period in a new continent with economic and political strain. He declined to give directional guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa tax holiday timeline?

524715|2026-03.headline: Sun Pharma to acquire Organon at $14/share (EV $11.75B, equity $3.99B), funded by $2–2.5B cash plus bank debt; net debt/EBITDA rises to ~2.3x.
524715|2026-03.overview: Sun Pharma announced a definitive agreement to acquire Organon & Company at $14 per share, implying an equity value of $3.99 billion and an enterprise value of $11.75 billion. Management described Organon as a similar-sized company to Sun with similar profitability but no growth, and framed the deal as a growth-turnaround and innovative-platform play. Sun will move from net cash to net debt, with combined net debt/EBITDA of about 2.3x, and management said debt repayment is the priority. Closing is expected in six to nine months, subject to Organon shareholder and regulatory approvals; management said the deal is EPS accretive from day one and dividend policy is still under review.

segments.name: Organon – Innovative medicines
segments.commentary: About 33% of Organon revenue; women's health leader with #2 position in contraception and #3 in fertility. Key products cited include VTAMA (dermatology) and Emgality (migraine, Europe).

segments.name: Organon – Established brands
segments.commentary: About 55% of Organon revenue; 50+ brands with 15 brands above $100 million sales, including Zetia, Atozet, Arcoxia, Hyzaar and Cozaar. Organon's growth is about 1–2%.

segments.name: Organon – Biosimilars
segments.commentary: Portfolio of six products (including Renflexis and Hadlima), grown from about $400 million in 2021 to close to $700 million; biosimilar segment growing more than 13%.

segments.name: Sun – Innovative / branded generics
segments.commentary: Sun's innovative business is about 20% of sales. On a combined basis innovative rises to 27%, and established brands plus branded generics reach over 51%.

segments.name: Combined company
segments.commentary: Combined revenue of $12.4 billion; generics ~15% and biosimilars ~6% of combined revenue. Sales mix: US 27%, emerging markets 29%, India 17%, RoW 28%.

guidance_outlook: Synergies estimated at about $350 million, purely cost-side (procurement, people, supply chain), to be realised over two to four years.
Management said the deal is EPS accretive from day one, i.e. in the first 12 months after closing; no detailed EPS figures given.
Closing expected in six to nine months, subject to Organon shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.
Combined free cash flow of about $2–2.5 billion annually; priority is repaying acquisition debt from surplus cash flow.
Dividend payments post-deal not yet decided; management said cash flow planning has always assumed continued dividends and specifics will follow.
Management did not give organic growth targets for Organon; said the established-products business could show single-digit growth over time.
capex_capacity: Organon operates six sites across EU and emerging markets, with a manufacturing complex noted for complex product development.
Organon has about 10,000 employees, of which about 4,000 are in the field force.
Combined commercial front-end of about 24,000 people across more than 150 markets.
Management said Organon's R&D capability for long-acting products (e.g., Nexplanon, a contraceptive developed in-house) could be applied to other chronic-disease products.
Sun plans to enter 10 new markets (including China and South Korea) where it is not present today, via its own field force after closing.
demand_pricing: Organon's China sales are above $800 million across eight large brands growing at a single-digit rate; management said most of Organon's China established-brand portfolio has already undergone volume-based procurement (VBP).
Women's health global market is $35 billion, growing 6–10% CAGR; Organon has more than 100 women's health assets under development.
Management expects established brands to hold share and premium pricing despite generics, citing China examples of 20–30 generics with brands holding 20–30% share.
Biosimilar market opportunity: more than $320 billion of drugs losing exclusivity by 2035, which management sizes as a $70 billion biosimilar opportunity.
Management said the US biosimilar market has not settled, with ongoing change in approvals and interchangeability dialogue; no specific US channel claim made.
Negligible product overlap between Sun and Organon; only a small product divestment, which Organon has already done.

qa_highlights.question: How will Sun manage cultural fit and management bandwidth for the integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Shanghvi said the approach will be to learn from Organon's strengths, following the Taro and Ranbaxy playbook; an integration management office will be set up and senior management time is expected, with Organon talent seen as a strengthening of Sun's bench.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost synergy breakdown and Organon's cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayashree Satagopan said the $350 million is purely cost-side. Organon has gross debt of about $8.5 billion, cash of about $900 million and net debt interest of about 5.5%; Sun intends to work with lenders on swaps of bonds and to finance via its banks, expecting a higher credit rating than Organon.

qa_highlights.question: How will Sun grow innovative and biosimilar businesses, and what is the in-licensing roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar said in-licensing will be part of the strategy, citing women's health pipeline depth; Alok Shanghvi said the plan is to in-license pre-LOE biosimilars to use the combined commercial footprint, without specific numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a revenue synergy number, and how will Organon's established brands grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar gave no sales synergy number, citing early stage. Organon's established-brand business is expected to move from flat to single-digit growth through line extensions and bioequivalence-based products, a multi-year effort.

qa_highlights.question: Is EPS accretive, and does the deal require FTC divestments?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayashree Satagopan said the deal is EPS accretive from day one. Kirti Ganorkar said overlap is negligible and no major divestments are needed; the footnote refers to an Organon divestment already done.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Sun pursue a large acquisition now, and does it solve US commercial reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Shanghvi said the aim is to strengthen innovative capability and global reach, using a cash deal to avoid Ranbaxy-style dilution (about 15%). Alok Shanghvi said it is too early to claim a US channel breakthrough.

risks_watch: Leverage rises to ~2.3x net debt/EBITDA; repayment pace and any dividend decision are open.
Organon's flat-to-low growth; the turnaround depends on in-licensing and execution, with no quantified target yet.
Regulatory approvals and Organon shareholder vote within six to nine months; US tariff exposure for Organon was not addressed (deferred to Organon).
Nexplanon generic entry timing (around 2030 per analyst question) and commentary withheld until closing.
Undisclosed in-licensing milestone payments; management said these are in Organon's plan and valuation but gave no figure.
Amortisation post-deal not addressed; to be clarified at closing.
Organon attrition and employee cost issues were not addressed; management pointed to diligence.
524715|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on strategic rationale and cost synergies, but cautious and deferential on specifics: dividend policy, amortisation, Organon attrition, tariffs, Nexplanon, milestones and organic growth were deferred to closing or to Organon.
key_quotes: So the key difference as we see is the relative high level of growth for Sun and no growth for Organon.
we will be taking on a significant amount of debt to close this transaction.
So we believe this will be EPS accretive from the beginning.
Sun would become top 25 global pharma company which gives us the ability to reaching more people touching more lives.

524715|2026-06.headline: Sun Pharma Q1 FY27 sales rose 10.1% to INR151,836 million; EBITDA up 2.7% to INR44,177 million with 28.9% margin.
524715|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10.1% YoY to INR151,836 million, with gross margin at 80.5% on product mix. EBITDA rose 2.7% to INR44,177 million, and margin fell YoY because Q1 FY26 included Lenalidomide benefit. Reported PAT was INR28,948 million and adjusted PAT INR30,894 million, after a INR1,617 million Organon acquisition-related exceptional charge. India formulations grew 16% to INR54,749 million, while US sales fell 9.7% to USD427 million on Lenalidomide erosion and generic competition. Management held high single-digit full-year sales growth guidance and said the Organon deal is expected to close in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Global Innovative Medicines
segments.commentary: Sales USD351 million, up 12.8% YoY, 21.9% of consolidated sales; growth led by ILUMYA, ODOMZO and CEQUA across US and ex-US.

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Sales INR54,749 million, up 16%; market share 8.5% per Pharmarack MAT June 2026 (8.2% prior), ranked number 1; volume growth 5.4% vs IPM 2%. Five new products launched in Q1.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Sales USD427 million, down 9.7% YoY, driven by Lenalidomide erosion and added competition in generics; QoQ decline partly seasonal for Levulan. Five generic launches in the quarter.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Formulation revenues USD311 million, up 4.2% YoY, 19.4% of consolidated revenue; management cited geopolitics and macro conditions.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Formulation revenues USD218 million, marginally lower YoY and flat QoQ, about 13.6% of consolidated revenue.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 sales growth guidance of high single digit retained, with management flagging FX translation as a factor.
Effective tax rate expected in a similar range to Q1 (around 27.8%) until Organon closing.
Organon acquisition expected to close in Q4 FY27 (early 2027); further acquisition-related exceptional charges expected in later quarters, mostly accrued at closing, with no full estimate given.
R&D spend guided to annual number; management expects to meet it despite lower Q1 spend.
Other expenses expected to stay elevated from continued launch investment (Leqselvi, Unloxcyt), FX translation and normalising R&D; no specific number given.
capex_capacity: Semaglutide: API made in-house, formulation in-house, device components sourced from partners; company says it is prepared to meet demand in India, South Africa and Brazil.

Semaglutide generic launched in India from March 2026 (number 2 generic player; only company offering an auto-injector in India), launched in South Africa after approval last week, Brazil launch via partner expected shortly.
Organon integration management office working on day-one preparedness; regulatory filings complete and some approvals received.
demand_pricing: India: management attributed 50% of growth to volume and new products (later said 60% of growth from volume and new products, 40% volume and 20% new products); field force expansion aiding tier 2 and tier 3 growth. Management declined to explain industry growth step-up beyond June being strong.
US Leqselvi: over 1,000 prescribers in June, strongest month since launch, majority of covered lives now available after a new plan added in the quarter.

US Unloxcyt: launched earlier in 2026, formulary additions at cancer centers and integrated delivery networks; Medicare Part B product; updated ASCO 2026 data showed more than one in four patients achieving complete tumor response.
Levulan seasonality hit the QoQ US comparison; management expects similar seasonality next quarter.
Emerging markets growth slowed to 4% USD; management cited geopolitics and macro conditions and said pricing pressure was not the main driver. ROW flat at USD218 million for a second quarter.
Semaglutide slowdown reports in India were disputed by management, which said Sun grew in prescriptions, value and units.

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty growth decelerate in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined product-level detail; Levulan seasonality was the only specific cited factor, with similar seasonality expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much semaglutide supply is secured for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said API and formulation are made in-house, device components are contracted, and it is well prepared for India, South Africa and Brazil.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp step-down in US generic revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest part is Lenalidomide on a YoY basis; QoQ decline is a slight base business drop from competition on a few products.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin trend and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by product mix, with higher shares from branded generics and innovative medicines; CFO did not give a forward margin level.

qa_highlights.question: Is top-line guidance conservative after 10.1% Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said to stick to high single-digit full-year growth, citing FX translation that is positive so far but uncertain for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual increments, additional field force for the two US launches and other innovative markets, and forex translation.

risks_watch: US generic erosion from Lenalidomide and added competition, with no clear turnaround timeline.
Emerging markets growth slowed to 4% USD; watch whether geopolitical and macro pressure persists.
Organon closing (Q4 FY27) and rising acquisition-related exceptional charges with no full estimate.
Launch costs for Leqselvi and Unloxcyt are sustained, not one-time, which keeps other expenses elevated.
Effective tax rate rising to about 28% as India tax benefits are used up.
Management withheld product-level revenue, Unloxcyt share and Leqselvi revenue timelines, so the launch ramp is not yet measurable.

rows.why: India formulations grew 16% with volume growth of 5.4% vs IPM 2% and five new Indian launches; Leqselvi over 1,000 prescribers in June; but US sales fell 9.7% to USD427 million, so the net is only high single-digit sales growth guidance.

rows.why: Management expects completion in Q4 FY27 with regulatory filings complete and some approvals received; further exceptional charges, mostly accrued at closing, have no full estimate (Q1 charge INR1,617 million).

rows.why: South Africa launched after approval last week and Brazil partner launch expected shortly, on top of India generic launch from March 2026 (number 2 generic player).

524735|2026-03.headline: Hikal Q4 FY26 revenue INR519 cr with 20.3% EBITDA margin, but FY26 PBT negative INR79.3 cr after INR85 cr exceptional items; no FY27 guidance given.
524735|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR519 cr with EBITDA of INR105 cr (20.3% margin) and PAT of INR14.4 cr after a INR47 cr impairment at Panoli. FY26 revenue fell to INR1,713 cr with EBITDA margin of 12.9%, and PBT was negative INR79.3 cr after INR85 cr of exceptional items (new labour code and impairments); PBT before exceptionals was about INR7 cr. Pharma was weak in H1 on a US FDA warning letter at Bangalore and recovered sequentially in H2, while Crop Protection improved on volumes. Management declined to give FY27 revenue or margin guidance until Q1 FY27 results, but said FY27 would show growth.

financial_highlights.change: Declined YoY per analyst; exact % not stated

financial_highlights.change: INR85 cr exceptional items for the year

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,021 cr, EBIT INR58 cr (5.7% margin). Q4 revenue INR292 cr, EBIT INR35 cr (12% margin); plants at Panoli and Bangalore running at about 80-85% utilisation. Own-product shipments from Bangalore slowed in Q4 after the FDA warning letter.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR692 cr, EBIT INR58 cr (8.4% margin). Q4 revenue INR228 cr with 17.1% EBIT margin (INR39 cr), driven by higher volume offtake and gradual industry normalisation.

segments.name: Animal Health
segments.commentary: No revenue figure disclosed. Management reiterated a target of a INR500 cr+ business in 4-5 years (set in Sept 2025); a CDMO multinational contract has completed product validation and moved into commercial phase.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management will update after Q1 FY27 results.
Management said FY27 will show growth and that FY27 margins should sustain at improved levels, with price pass-through partly offsetting raw material inflation.
FY26 was described as a transition year, with significant growth from FY27 and meaningful growth in FY28-FY30.
The FY30 plan (earlier INR3,500-4,000 cr medium-term and INR6,000 cr FY30 targets) is said to still stand but is delayed by 2-3 years; no reaffirmation of figures.
Management expects the US FDA matter to be resolved by end of this year, with an inspection expected towards year-end; the Bangalore site is not expected to receive new approvals this year.
Pharma volumes expected to improve QoQ and grow; Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter because of annual maintenance shutdowns.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR149 cr for debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades and CDMO capacity. Over FY23-FY26, about INR900 cr capex, of which about INR600 cr growth and INR300 cr infra, regulatory and maintenance.

Panoli multipurpose agrochemical plant (about INR300 cr investment) impaired INR47 cr and about INR250 cr being retooled for Pharma and Animal Health lines; expected on stream next financial year (FY27).
New high-potency laboratory, expanded R&D centre in Pune and pilot plant at Panoli are now operational; expanded Kilo lab in Pune planned.
Planned HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted over FY28; HPAPI and ADC chemistries expected to take 3-5 years to scale.
New Panoli facility for DMF filings; Panoli approved by US FDA in May 2023 with no warning-letter issue.
demand_pricing: Pharma: H2 FY26 demand recovered over H1, with improved demand in API and CDMO; 5-6 DMF filings targeted annually vs 2-3 historically, all from Panoli; RFP activity rising.
Crop Protection: volumes improving YoY on key products; management says inventory correction is largely over but agrochemical pricing pressure persists and China has not raised agrochemical prices.

Raw materials: solvent prices (toluene, methanol, acetone, benzene) rose sharply over the last 3 months and stayed at higher levels; availability is not an issue. CDMO pass-throughs lag by about a quarter; old products face competitive pressure, so pass-through may be partial.
Animal Health: no degrowth signalled by customers on current portfolio; move towards more complex molecules with lower competition and higher margin sustainability.
Pharma loss in Q4: some own-product business was lost in Q4 per management, though the order book is intact and CDMO demand is long term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Pharma fall short of the 10% growth guidance given in February, and is Pharma weak YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FDA-related GMP consultant advice to slow some production at Bangalore slowed shipments and price releases in Q4; no customers lost, though some business was lost in Q4 and expected to recover over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give a FY27 top-line growth figure and a path to make up three lost years?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 guidance until Q1 results because of war-related uncertainty in raw materials and logistics. Management expects growth to return in FY27 and sees FY28-FY30 as meaningful growth years; ROCE target of 18-20% is acknowledged.

qa_highlights.question: When will the US FDA issue be resolved and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes to resolve it by end of this year; CAPAs nearly complete, milestone meetings with FDA planned in the next few months, with a likely inspection toward year-end. Typical resolution time cited as 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY30 INR3,500-4,000 cr / INR6,000 cr target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY30 plan still stands but is delayed by 2-3 years; no explicit guidance given; growth expected every year, mainly from CDMO, Pharma, Animal Health and Specialty Chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 5-6 DMF filings target include Animal Health, and how is the Animal Health ramp-up tracking?
qa_highlights.answer: 5-6 DMF filings are Pharma only; Animal Health is additional. Management reaffirmed the INR500 cr+ Animal Health target in 4-5 years and declined to give FY27 revenue guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Did Hikal sell steroid or hormone products for animal health?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hikal is not into steroids or hormones currently; the older website reference was outdated.

risks_watch: US FDA warning letter at Bangalore: resolution timing (management targets end-2026) and any new approvals from Bangalore, which management does not expect this year.
Raw material cost inflation from solvent prices and geopolitical volatility, with a one-to-two-quarter lag on CDMO pass-through and limited pass-through on old competitive products.
Q4 loss of some own-product Pharma business; management says it should recover over the next two quarters.
Capacity-utilisation metric may be inflated by longer batch cycle times after post-FDA slowdown, per management.
Impairment of INR47 cr at Panoli and retooling of about INR250 cr; the new Pharma/Animal Health lines are expected in FY27 and need to deliver returns.
Multi-year growth shortfall: FY24-FY26 revenue flat to down, and the ROCE target of 18-20% is far from current levels.

524774|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 57% YoY to ₹149.23 crore and EBITDA margin hit 14.35%, but margins were marginally lower QoQ on cost pressures.
524774|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was ₹149.23 crore, up 57% YoY and 17% QoQ, driven by higher volumes and better capacity utilisation. EBITDA rose to ₹21.41 crore (14.35% margin, up 769 bps YoY) and PAT to ₹13.49 crore from ₹0.54 crore. Management said margins were slightly lower sequentially because fixed-price contracts blocked immediate pass-through of higher freight and raw material costs, and because of forex and investment mark-to-market provisions. FY26 revenue was ₹500.95 crore (+36%), EBITDA ₹72.69 crore (14.51% margin) and PAT ₹48.13 crore (+128%). Phase II commissioning slipped to early Q2 FY27 due to gas and labour shortages, with commercial production still guided for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Animal API
segments.commentary: Core business, contributing 95% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Top 10 customers were 29% of sales and top 10 products 66%. Company now offers about 45 APIs versus about 20 three years ago.

segments.name: Regulated markets (Europe/US)
segments.commentary: Europe sales expected to start in FY27 and US in FY28, with significant revenue from FY28. Europe has three CEPs approved, three under review and two being prepared; US VMS filings are five done with six planned this year.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin target of 15% to 18%; management said the company is close to this band, with Q1 FY27 possibly 1-2% lower as price increases only started flowing mid-quarter and margins expected from Q2 onwards.
Partial price pass-through achieved in Q1 FY27; management declined to quantify the overall price increase.
Phase II (Tarapur greenfield) commissioning moved to early Q2 FY27 from Q1 FY27; commercial production still targeted for H2 FY27.
Expected total Phase II capex of ₹210 crore, of which ₹182.75 crore was spent up to Q4 FY26; ongoing capex after completion estimated at ₹15-20 crore.
New expansion revenue potential of up to ₹350 crore turnover, to be reached over three to four years; the company declined to combine it with existing-plant revenue.
Regulated market margins expected to be 3-5 percentage points higher than the 15-18% band, but management declined to give regulated revenue figures.
capex_capacity: Phase I of the expansion is contributing meaningfully and is operating at about 70-80% utilisation, with Q4 volumes absorbed within it.
Phase II includes five clean rooms and is expected to be commissioned in early Q2 FY27, with commercial production from H2 FY27.

Phase II capex rose from ₹160 crore to ₹210 crore: about ₹20 crore for automation and digitisation and about ₹50 crore from higher metal costs; management said the increase will not add sales capacity.
Brownfield expansion of existing facilities is planned for FY27 to add ROW capacity.
Peak utilisation of the new plant is expected to take three to four years.
Company outsources about 20% of its intermediate requirements.
demand_pricing: Volume growth reported across geographies, with Latin America a successful new market and customer count up 47 QoQ on new country registrations.
Competition from Chinese and Indian players continues; price erosion on fluralaner has largely settled, and Chinese producers have begun raising prices from April/May 2026.
Oversupply in 2024 and 2025 drove price erosion; management does not expect return to prior 20-21% margins for at least two to three years.
Management plans to add 9-10 new products per year, and five new APIs were added in Q4.
Fixed-price contracts delayed pass-through of freight and raw material cost increases linked to geopolitical developments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue run rate from Phase I without Phase II, and how is outsourcing contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a run rate of about ₹150 crore per quarter from Phase I plus outsourcing, with 10-15% growth on top; Phase II's five clean rooms commission next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the USFDA inspection and the Phase II utilisation until then?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the audit timing depends on the regulator and could fall in 2026 or 2027; until then Phase II will serve ROW and Europe, with European business expected in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How many CEPs and DMFs are approved, and when will the rest come through?
qa_highlights.answer: Three CEPs are registered and three are under review, with a ~18-month review period; management expects six CEPs and nine DMFs by year-end 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise ₹10-11 crore QoQ, and how much was forex loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to mark-to-market provisioning on forex and investments; it did not have the exact forex figure on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to hit a higher margin band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is 15-18% EBITDA margin and it is close; it said partial pass-through is done and China has started raising prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation and dividend plan given the debt and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth capex is funded internally without new borrowing, and it has not yet set a dividend strategy for three years out.

risks_watch: USFDA audit timing is entirely at the regulator's discretion, and US regulated revenue could slip beyond FY28.
Phase II commissioning already slipped one quarter due to gas and labour shortages.
Fixed-price contracts and the lag in pass-through leave margins exposed to crude-linked freight and raw material inflation; Q1 FY27 margins may be 1-2% lower.
Forex and investment mark-to-market provisions weighed on Q4 margins and other expenses; the amount was not disclosed.
Chinese supply and capacity could keep pressure on prices and limit recovery to the earlier 20%+ margin range.

526247|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores with net profit up 78%, but FY26 revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores; FY27 guided at INR600-700 crores.
526247|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores, with EBIT up 35% to INR9.6 crores (10.8% margin) and PAT up 78% to INR6.6 crores. For full FY26, revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores as FY25's high-value chaffs and flares emergency orders were not repeated, while EBIT rose 42% to INR69.3 crores (17.8% margin) and PAT rose 61% to INR45.8 crores, helped by one-off other income. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin to 15-20%, with the order book at a record INR1,569 crores. Execution remains the central concern: raw material shortages (MIL, DRDO alternate materials), the Katepally plant accident, and pending free-issue material from BDL and DRDO all delayed deliveries.

526247|2026-06.headline: Premier Explosives Q1 FY27 revenue fell 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore, EBIT margin 4.7%, order book INR1,393 crore (94% defence).
526247|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore as dispatches and project execution slipped, mainly on export deliveries held up by maritime disruption and imported countermeasure components. EBIT fell 80% YoY to INR4.8 crore (4.7% margin) and PAT fell 80% to INR3 crore (3% margin), with raw material costs squeezing margins. Management said the export licence backlog is largely cleared and expects the delayed execution to complete in Q2 and Q3. Order book stands at INR1,393 crore, and FY27 revenue target is retained at about INR600 crore. Apollo Micro Systems' acquisition of promoter stake was discussed, with synergy details deferred to next quarter.

526263|2026-03.headline: Mold-Tek Q4 FY26 PAT turned to INR 2.28 crore from a loss, but FY26 PAT fell 17% to INR 10 crore on a INR 4 crore FX MTM hit.
526263|2026-03.overview: Management reported a Q4 FY26 profit of INR 2.28 crore versus a loss of about INR 1.6 crore a year earlier, despite a roughly INR 4 crore MTM loss from rupee depreciation on forward contracts. Full-year PAT was about INR 10 crore against INR 12.16 crore in FY25, with management citing EBITDA of about INR 20 crore standalone (INR 19.64 crore consolidated) against INR 23 crore a year earlier. Beryl, acquired in November 2025, contributed five months of revenue, and the MES automobile (BIW) team was cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March. Management reiterated plans to move into structural design and targets of INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin for FY27. Analyst questions were pointed on EBITDA definition, the cancelled preferential issue, receivables and hedging, and several figures were disputed or left for follow-up with the CFO.

segments.commentary: Work on hand grew from about $4 million at start of FY26 to about $5 million at end-March 2026, which management described as growth of about 60-70% versus $2.84 million in June 2024. Structural design is about 10% of civil revenue, versus nearly 0% three to four years ago. Management targets 30-40% of revenue from design in three to four years.

segments.commentary: Team cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March; the team was closed from April 1. The segment lost about INR 7-8 crore a year and about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 FY26. Work on hand fell from about $0.5 million in Q1 to about $0.25 million.

segments.commentary: Team grew from 45-50 to about 80 people. FY26 revenue was about $0.8 million; management expects FY27 to cross $1.5-2 million. Around 80-90% of this work comes from the USA.

segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 80% permitting/inspection and 20% design. Team of about 40 in Tampa with no resignations in five months. Management guided Beryl margin at 8-10% for FY27 and said it can grow to about $5-7 million with India design support.

segments.commentary: Now about 5% of revenue, down from being the core business before 2010.

segments.commentary: Mandate for 20 people; 3 fulfilled so far. Contract period 1-3 years, potential about $0.5 million per annum within a year.

Standalone engineering business (MES plus civil from India) expected to grow at least 15-20%, with EBITDA margin in the 15-16% region.

Salary hike of 8.5-9% provided in Q4 for Indian teams; Beryl not yet covered.

Nashik owned building site acquired a couple of years ago; municipal approvals expected by end of May, ground work in June, completion by end FY27.
Management is in talks for an acquisition of a high-rise steel structural design company; one target is near the Atlanta office. No deal concluded.
Two PEs (professional engineers) certified in more than 20 US states; PE support needed for full member design.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand up to about $5 million at end-March 2026, against about $4 million at start of the year (per Q4 opening remarks); Q&A figure of $2.5 million at start of year.

Trade uncertainty between the US and India has stalled Interarch and Mold-Tek building orders in the US; no revenue progress from Interarch or Affordable Robotic Partnership.
BIW automobile demand fell as EV adoption and new model launches slowed; European work was over 50% of MES, while poles and towers are 80-90% US.

Operating cash flow was $21 Mn, or about $38 Mn excluding roughly $17 Mn of delayed customer remittances collected in early April. qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline and how does the margin path look?

qa_highlights.question: Why did the TTM TCV-to-revenue correlation fall from above 0.9 to 0.74?

526367|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue INR122 crore (up 33% QoQ), EBITDA INR98 crore, PAT INR61 crore; FY26 PAT INR316 crore vs FY25 INR598 crore, with no FY27 guidance until Q1.
526367|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year marked by West Asia-related cost pressures and a high FY25 base. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR122 crore, up 33% sequentially, with EBITDA of INR98 crore (about 80.7% margin) and PAT of INR61 crore. FY26 revenue was INR539 crore and PAT INR316 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR1.5 per share (15%). Million Minds Phase 1 was inaugurated on May 17, 2026, with about 60-65% of leasable area leased or in final stages as LOIs, and Malabar Retreat is about 79% complete. FY27 guidance on revenue and EBITDA was deferred to the Q1 FY27 results.

financial_highlights.change: lower than FY25 (not quantified on call)
vs INR598 crore in FY25 per analyst; FY24 INR461 crore

Malabar Retreat completion and handover targeted by end FY27; full recognition of INR450 crore GDV expected only after completion.
Two new launches planned in FY27: Million Minds Phase 2 commercial around Q2 and a residential project around Q3; Million Minds Phase 2 construction to take about 3 years.
Management cited a free cash flow estimate of INR9,950 crore from planned projects on a conservative basis at current prevailing rates; no timeline or detailed assumptions provided.
capex_capacity: Million Minds Tech City spans about 65 acres with long-term potential of over 18 million sq ft across commercial, residential, hospitality, retail and social infrastructure.

Malabar Retreat bookings of about INR175 crore against INR450 crore project value; management expects traction to rise as completion nears.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be given for FY27 revenue and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 guidance will be given at Q1 FY27 results; it stated annual guidance is normally given at the start of the year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said annual lease revenue is expected to exceed the earlier INR72 crore target, reaching about INR75-77 crore, with partial rentals in FY27 and full-year from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Thaltej One and Smile City launch delayed for multiple quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited changing project configuration, market developments and past unsold launches; said Thaltej One details will come in Q1 FY27 and that Godhavi land sales are counted as project sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LOI percentage at Million Minds rise only from about 60% to 66%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier figures were inquiries while the current figures are LOIs or near-final; large tenants are waiting for BU before committing, which is expected imminently.

qa_highlights.question: Why was dividend reduced to 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Board chose lower payout to conserve cash for growth opportunities in Ahmedabad; management expects dividend to rise if cash position and projects progress.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said a REIT or monetisation option will be evaluated after full lease-up, possibly within one to two years, but no decision has been taken.

526367|2026-06.headline: Ganesh Housing Q1 FY27 revenue rose 86% YoY to Rs 280 crore on One 91 Thaltej land sale, but PAT fell to Rs 42 crore on one-time tax; FY27 guided at Rs 1,000-1,200 crore revenue.
526367|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 280 crore, up 130% QoQ and 86% YoY, driven largely by the One 91 Thaltej land sale plus some completed old-project inventory. EBITDA was Rs 110 crore and PBT about Rs 105 crore, while PAT was Rs 42 crore because the land carried a higher tax cost from a 2020 amalgamation. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs 1,000-1,200 crore and PAT of Rs 300-325 crore, with Million Minds lease rentals starting in Q4 FY27. Management said the Thaltej sale was a capital-allocation choice rather than a liquidity need, but did not disclose buyer, consideration or margin details.

Management said up about 10% or roughly flat

segments.commentary: Construction about 83% complete; 73 units booked, about 45% of units and Rs 183 crore, about 45% of sale value. Sale value above Rs 450 crore; no revenue recognised yet in Q1 as project is incomplete.

segments.commentary: Phase-I inaugurated; fit-out in final stages. LOIs executed for about 43% (2.64 lakh sq ft) of leasable area, with a further 15-20% under negotiation; lease rentals to start in Q4 FY27. Management said FY28 rentals could exceed Rs 75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Thaltej land sold and why did margins fall to about 39%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the sale was a present-versus-future value decision rather than a liquidity need. Margins were lower because the land cost from the amalgamation was higher, and the one-time tax was elevated by the same cost basis.
