526371|2026-03.headline: NMDC guides FY27 production to 60 million tonnes and FY27 capex to about INR6,000 crore, with Q1 FY27 output up about 15% YoY.
526371|2026-03.overview: NMDC reported FY26 production above 50 million tonnes and an 11% PAT rise despite sluggish prices, with management citing a record capex of about INR3,300 crore. Management guided FY27 production to 60 million tonnes, with the first two months of Q1 FY27 about 15% higher YoY at roughly 10 million tonnes. New iron ore (Deposit 4, Deposit 13) and coal (Tokisud, Rohne) assets are being commissioned, and a INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag is sanctioned. The EBITDA margin was 33% group-level, down from 42%, due to a one-time HR coil trading arrangement with NMDC Steel; standalone iron ore EBITDA was stated at 42%.

segments.name: Iron ore (NMDC standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin at 42%, with FY27 guided at 42-43%. Kirandul FY26 about 21 million tonnes (to ~30 million by decade-end); Bacheli about 18-19 million tonnes (to ~35 million).

segments.name: NMDC Steel (NSL)
segments.commentary: NSL has turned profitable; the HR coil trading in the last quarter was a one-time cash-flow support and is not expected in Q1 FY27. NSL dues are being recovered at about INR100 crore per month, with full liquidation in 16-18 months (pre-demerger dues about INR2,500 crore, now about INR1,800 crore).

segments.name: Coal
segments.commentary: Tokisud (2.3 million tonnes peak, thermal, opened) targets 0.75-1 million tonnes in FY27 from Q2; Rohne (8 million tonnes peak coking coal) opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 production. Management expects INR500-600 crore revenue per 1 million tonnes at G10 grade, at 30-40% EBITDA (approximate).

segments.name: Pellets (KIOCL)
segments.commentary: KIOCL 3 million tonne job-work plant: FY26 about 2.4 million tonnes; FY27 target 3-3.3 million tonnes. Pellet grade achieved 66.5% Fe; targeting 67% DR-grade with a $20-30/t premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 60 million tonnes including NSL, built from Deposit 14 (+1 mt), NMZ (+1 mt), Kumaraswamy (+~3.3 mt), Deposit 5 (+2 mt to 12 mt), plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt).
Deposit 4 expected to start commercial mining in Q2 FY27: about 1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, and 7 mt peak rated capacity after 1.5-2 more years.
Deposit 13 start targeted around Q2 FY27 after pending clearances: under 0.5 mt in FY27, about 2 mt next year, 10 mt initial peak rising to 20-21 mt in 4-5 years.
Capex guidance: about INR6,000 crore in FY27 (range INR6,000-7,000 crore); INR7,000-10,000 crore per year over the next 2-3 years; INR40,000-50,000 crore over 3 years to reach 100 mt.
Overseas critical mineral and mineral asset acquisitions: INR2,000-3,000 crore expected in FY27; a couple of overseas assets targeted this year.
Management reiterated a 100 million tonne target by end of decade and said the 60 mt FY27 guidance is achievable without the railway doubling, but 100 mt requires it.
No immediate plans to leverage the balance sheet; internal accruals expected to fund capex and acquisitions, with debt possible late FY27 only for large global acquisitions.
Iron ore prices expected to stay range-bound in FY27; monthly price calls to be taken.
capex_capacity: Railway: 131 km doubling; two sections remaining, one by end of June 2026 and the Bhansi-Bacheli section by December 2026; evacuation capacity to rise from 28-30 mt to ~40 mt, with 60 mt+ after doubling beyond Jagdalpur.
Slurry pipeline (15 mt, Bacheli to Nagarnar), Nagarnar pellet plant and Bacheli grinding mill in pre-commissioning; commissioning expected by end-June or mid-July 2026.
EC capacity 64.8 mt vs CTO ~55.4 mt; CTO enhancement sought in three places to ~58.8 mt. All mines reached EC capacity as of 1 April 2026 (Deposit 5 the exception in FY26).
Deposit 5 downhill conveyor and bottleneck fix due June-July 2026, enabling 12 mt. New infrastructure at Deposit 14, NMZ, 11 and 11C takes about 1.5 years, adding 5-6 mt.
INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag (board sanctioned, ~2-2.5 year build); Vizag land parcel ~1,100 acres; pellet plant at Vizag on drawing board, pending slurry pipeline route decision.
Expansion works (~INR15,000-20,000 crore worth of major tenders) expected to be awarded by end-June or July 2026.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is not a constraint even at 100 mt, citing JSW, AMNS (10 mt plant near Vizag, 17 mt total), JSPL and NSL expansions; NMDC's phosphorus content of 0.05% is a claimed differentiator.

Iron ore prices expected range-bound in Q1 FY27 after steel prices peaked Dec-Feb and stabilised in March-April; the company sets prices monthly, citing international prices, competitor prices and logistics, not a direct steel-price link.
RINL consumes 7-8 mt per year; bills discounted at ~10% premium with a 45-day payment lag; no recourse to NMDC in FY25 or FY26.
Blended/branded iron ore (Vizag) planned as a premium product; exports unattractive given 30% export duty, so pellets are preferred for export.
Iron ore realisation slightly down ~2% per an analyst question; no quantified FY27 realisation guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Mine-wise bridge to 60 mt FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 14 +1 mt, NMZ +1 mt, Kumaraswamy +~3.3 mt (MPAP relief from 8.6 mt), Deposit 5 +2 mt (to 12 mt), totalling ~5.3 mt; plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt) gives ~60 mt including NSL.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mine economics and grade?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial volume mostly via auction at prices above CIL FSA; 1 mt is estimated at INR500-600 crore revenue with 30-40% EBITDA. Grade is G10; figures described as very preliminary.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery of NSL and RINL receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: NSL dues cut from ~INR2,500 crore to ~INR1,800 crore; recovery at ~INR100 crore per month, 16-18 months for NSL, about a year and a half to two for the rest. RINL is 100% government-owned, with timing slower but no risk assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and critical minerals spending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR6,000 crore (range 6,000-7,000), then INR7,000-10,000 crore per year. Overseas acquisitions INR2,000-3,000 crore in FY27; domestic rare earth via GMDC MoU in Gujarat, no firm profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Can 60 mt be reached without railway doubling?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 60 mt is achievable without it, but 100 mt is not possible without the doubling completing (Vizag/Bhansi-Bacheli section due December 2026).

qa_highlights.question: Deposit 4, Deposit 13 and Rohne ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 4 ~1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, 7 mt peak; Deposit 13 under 0.5 mt FY27, 2 mt next year, 10 mt initially rising to 20-21 mt; Rohne opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 output and 8 mt peak coking coal.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA guidance and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore EBITDA margin to be maintained at 42-43% for FY27; no specific per-tonne realisation or EBITDA-per-tonne figures were given.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 output and CTO enhancement to ~58.8 mt (vs EC 64.8 mt) are needed to hit 60 mt; EC and forest clearances remain a continuous process.
Railway doubling completion (December 2026 for Bhansi-Bacheli) is a prerequisite for 100 mt.
NSL and RINL receivables recovery pace and any repeat of HR coil trading; the one-time trading hit margins in Q4 FY26.
Pending approvals for Deposit 13 and Rohne coal; Rohne has no FY27 output.
Govt pay revision: provisions already taken from 1 January 2026; further provisioning for executives from 1 January 2027.
Overseas acquisition pipeline and the decision to use debt for large global deals late FY27.

526381|2026-03.headline: FY26 PBT crossed INR10 crore at INR10.30 crore (up ~34%), with PAT of INR9.58 crore and a 30% payout dividend of INR0.40 per share.
526381|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 total income from operations up 11.68% YoY to INR96.74 crore, with PBT up nearly 99% to INR3.70 crore and PAT up over 60% to INR2.98 crore. For FY26, total income from operations was INR357.25 crore, PBT INR10.30 crore (up over 34%) and PAT INR9.58 crore (up over 26%). The air freight segment profit rose to INR11.26 crore from INR8.53 crore, and finance cost fell by INR35 lakh to a lower level from INR1.18 crore. A new subsidiary, Rajpat Logistics Limited, was formed in the December 2025 quarter as an additional trucking-booking vertical.

financial_highlights.change: from INR1.18 crore in previous year

segments.name: Air freight logistics
segments.commentary: Segment profit rose to INR11.26 crore in FY26 from INR8.53 crore in FY25. The company says it operates from around 100 airports with more than 60 airlines, and serves pharma, auto parts, engineering, electronics, FMCG and documents.

segments.name: Rajpat Logistics Limited (new subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Formed in the December 2025 quarter; management says it is at a nascent stage. It will book trucking for top corporates on an asset-light basis, and management expects it to add about 25% to the INR400 crore revenue base and to earn ROCE above 15%.

guidance_outlook: Management said momentum continued into April 2026 and expects growth to be maintained.
Rajpat Logistics expected to build meaningful turnover over the next two to three years, with about 25% addition to the current INR400 crore base as per management.
Management expects rates to harden more than volumes; international air rates reportedly up about 15% since March 2026.
No plan to own warehouses or trucks for now; management says current operations earn higher ROCE than warehousing would.
Management expects a valuation re-rating, though no numeric target was given.
capex_capacity: No new capex, capacity or commissioning plans were announced; management said the company is asset-light and will not own trucks.
Management is pursuing redevelopment of a non-core property with two adjacent property owners; a meeting was planned for the following week. No timeline or value was given.
Management said the company is not currently pursuing warehouse assets, though it remains open if returns are attractive.
demand_pricing: Management said industry rates are hardening, with international air rates up about 15% since March 2026, amid supply constraints linked to the geopolitical situation and higher crude and ATF prices.
Management described the environment as favourable for organised players, and expects rate increases to outpace volume growth in FY27.
Passenger aircraft fleet expected to grow from about 700 to about 1,800; government targets airports rising from 140 to 220. Navi Mumbai airport is operational and Jewar is nearing operations.
Management said the company uses an automated system that stops credit when a customer's receivables age beyond a set threshold, to control trade receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin can Rajpat Logistics deliver over three to five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rajpat would add about 25% to the current INR400 crore revenue base, with ROCE expected above 15%, higher than its margin because capital would turn quickly.

qa_highlights.question: How are the war and higher crude and ATF prices affecting capacity and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply is tight and rates are hardening, with international rates up about 15% since March. Airline-capacity access was described as favourable for organised players with over 60 airlines, and growth momentum was said to continue into April.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add warehousing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no plan exists to enter warehousing now, since current operations earn more ROCE than warehousing would, but it remains open if a lucrative opportunity arises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the mobile app and AI initiatives on revenue leakage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said automation and AI are being used to control leakages, and the receivables system stops credit automatically when outstanding crosses set days. The aim is to raise employee productivity without job losses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected value and structure of the non-core property redevelopment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing redevelopment with two adjacent property owners for a larger combined project. It prefers an in-house development structure with recurring income over a one-time sale, and no value was quantified.

risks_watch: Rate-driven growth versus volume: management expects rates to rise faster than volumes, and volume outlook for FY27 was described as difficult to predict.
Fuel and geopolitical exposure: crude and ATF price increases and airline supply constraints tied to the ongoing war were cited.
Rajpat Logistics is at a nascent stage; its revenue and ROCE targets are unproven.
Redevelopment of the non-core property: no value, timeline or structure has been finalised.
Management said the company is 'practically debt free' but still carries a small amount of debt; the exact debt figure was not disclosed.
Dividend of INR0.40 per share is 30% of PAT, which will be watched against FY27 earnings.

we are very much hopeful that we will be able to maintain the growth in the volume as well.

526423|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose to INR 18 crore (margin 12.91% vs 0.15%) on revenue of INR 142 crore, while FY26 volume fell 13% to 58,630 MT.
526423|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 recovered sharply from a weak prior year: revenue grew 3% YoY to INR 142 crore and EBITDA reached INR 18 crore versus INR 20 lakh a year earlier, with net profit of about INR 4 crore against a loss of INR 4 crore. For the full year, revenue fell 19% to INR 587 crore and volume fell 13%, attributed to heavy rains in operating areas, but EBITDA rose 23% to INR 35 crore and net profit was INR 1 crore versus a loss of INR 4 crore. Management linked Q4 inventory gains to PVC price volatility from the Middle East conflict, and said capex is on hold for two quarters. Several answers deferred to the CFO, reducing detail on freight, dealers and utilisation.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 10,288 MT (+12% YoY); FY26 volume 47,638 MT (-11%). Management cites typical margins of 8-10%, varying by season.

segments.name: Building products
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 2,683 MT (+7% YoY); FY26 volume 7,685 MT (-16%). Margins stated at 14-18%, higher than agriculture; management targets substantial growth in FY27 and CPVC expansion.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 606 MT (-65% YoY); FY26 volume 3,307 MT (-29%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects healthy FY27 volume growth, off a low base, but gave no numeric target; it depends on monsoon conditions.
Management reaffirmed the earlier INR 1,000 crore revenue target and a 10% margin goal by FY28, saying it is 'doing our best'; no ROCE guidance was given.
Building products are to be the main FY27 growth driver, with CPVC expansion; OPVC is not on the agenda.
Capex is on hold; the next decision on capex or a second plant will follow after the first two quarters of FY27.
Inventory gains are possible in Q1 FY27, but management said volatility makes this hard to predict.
capex_capacity: Capex on hold: management says developments are already invested and the next decision comes after the first two quarters of FY27.
No decision on a second manufacturing plant; timing, location and whether to diversify beyond the single central plant are open.
CPVC capacity is being expanded; OPVC capacity is not planned at present.
Q4 plant utilisation described as 'fairly good' and above the company average; no percentage given.
Company runs a single central plant and relies on depots to serve other regions; management said building products can bear distant logistics but agriculture is limited to a regional territory.
demand_pricing: Demand for agri and building products was hit when the Middle East war pushed raw material and finished goods prices up sharply; management says demand is now back to near normal.
Management says PVC prices are volatile after the Iran-Iraq conflict; Q4 included inventory gains, and the company stocked up in March ahead of the April-June agri season.
The government withdrew import duty on PVC and other polymers until about 1 July; management said there is no anti-dumping duty.
Competition is aggressive with many national players present in MP; branded players are gaining share from unorganised ones.
Market share: MP and Rajasthan described as strong, Maharashtra sub-10% and still in development; dealer count about 400, with expansion mainly in adjacent regions.
PVC resin is sourced from a mix of imports and local purchases; management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be inventory gains in Q1 FY27, and when will volume growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 may still show some inventory advantage but this is hard to predict given volatility. Demand has normalised after the war, and FY27 growth is expected from a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex being put on hold, and how will the company compete outside its central plant location?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is on hold until the first two quarters of FY27 are reviewed. Management said expansion beyond the region is limited for agri but feasible for building materials, and any new capacity will be carefully considered.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 show negative gross margin before inventory adjustments, and was the stocking strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March inventory build is routine, to prepare for the April-June agri season, and gave no figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall 33% in FY26, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses mainly comprise freight; the CFO would provide the breakdown offline. No figures were given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Has the building products segment crossed INR 100 crore, and what is the expected contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said building products revenue fell in FY26 due to rationalisation and will see a quantum jump in FY27, but gave no figure for the segment's FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables fall, from INR 48 crore to INR 28 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are mostly from institutional customers, which the company cut in Q4 as planned.

risks_watch: Volatile PVC prices: inventory gains helped Q4 and could reverse, and the policy on import duty expires around 1 July.

Q4 cost of materials consumed (about INR 170 crore per an analyst's read) exceeded revenue of INR 142 crore, so the margin is inventory-driven; the sustainability of the 12.91% Q4 EBITDA margin is unproven.
FY26 volume declined 13%; FY27 recovery depends on monsoon conditions and needs to be seen in Q1-Q2 results.
Single-plant concentration limits reach outside central India, and aggressive competition from national players may pressure pricing.
Capex and second-plant decision deferred to after H1 FY27; ROCE of about 7% for FY26 remains low versus the FY28 targets.

526612|2026-03.headline: Blue Dart Q4 FY26 PAT fell to INR 43 crore on revenue of INR 1,533 crore; comparable PBT before exceptional items down about 17% YoY.
526612|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 6,141 crore versus INR 5,720 crore in FY25, with full-year PAT of INR 240 crore. Management said FY26 revenue and PBT before the Labour Code exceptional item each grew about 7%. Q4 revenue grew about 8%, but comparable PBT before exceptional items fell about 17%, with no exceptional item in the quarter. Management attributed the margin pressure to a mix shift toward heavier, lower-margin ground shipments, higher local vehicle hiring costs in March, and employee cost investments in sales and quality functions.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5,720 crore in FY25 (about 7% growth)

financial_highlights.metric: Comparable PBT before exceptional items, Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: of which about INR 200 crore aircraft engine and maintenance checks

segments.name: Air (time-definite, door-to-door multimodal product)
segments.commentary: About 60% of FY26 revenue by value; management said air is a transit-time product, not a mode, with about one-third of air load on commercial airlines and two-thirds on own aircraft. E-commerce air growth was described as steady with limited growth.

segments.name: Ground / surface
segments.commentary: About 40% of FY26 revenue by value and the stated growth engine; FY26 surface rate growth was 6.9% per management, and its share has risen from about 30-32% a few quarters ago.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue split 70.3% B2B and 29.7% B2C; Q4 split about 71:29. B2C is described as essentially e-commerce, split 17% air and 12% surface of total revenue.

Management said ground costs are largely variable, so ground growth may not translate into a dramatic profitability increase, unlike air where asset investment gives better incremental returns.
Management targets a yearly margin rather than quarterly and said the company aims to reach its PBT margin guidance of about 7-8% as soon as possible, without a specific timeline.
ATF/fuel impact expected from April 2026 (FY27 Q1) but described as largely neutralized by the fuel surcharge mechanism.

Capex of about INR 100-150 crore per year is expected to recur for aircraft engine and maintenance, plus ground and IT automation; standalone capex was INR 120 crore plus about INR 400 crore ROU assets.

526612|2026-06.headline: Blue Dart Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR1,658 crore (from INR1,442 crore) and PAT reached INR87 crore, driven mainly by yield and fuel surcharge rather than volume.
526612|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,658 crore against INR1,442 crore a year earlier, with PAT of INR87 crore. Management attributed growth mainly to pricing: GPI-led increases, targeted repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery after diesel and Brent prices rose from around March–May. Tonnage grew about 7% to 364,430 tons and shipments about 2% to 96.15 million, with air volume up about 2.6% and surface up about 9%. Management declined to quantify yield growth or give forward volume and margin guidance, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue but about 25% of kilos (1:3 air:surface by weight). Volume growth about 2.6%; growth is mainly yield-led. Freighter pallet utilisation 85–90%.

segments.name: Surface / Ground
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue and about 75% of kilos. Volume up about 9%; B2B revenue up about 14%. Management says surface is the faster-growing segment and is approaching air in size.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Revenue up more than 10% YoY. Management says about 50-plus million of the 96.15 million shipments are e-commerce, and Blue Dart holds about 12–13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 70% B2B and 30% B2C (plus or minus 2%).

segments.name: BFSI (documents and cards)
segments.commentary: BFSI alone is about 10–15% of total revenue; documents plus cards together, including small parcels, about 25–30%. Management says BFSI is no longer a growing segment.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not forecast volumes, citing seasonality, but expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward.
Typical GPI realisation is about 4–5%, with extra customer-specific corrections on top.

Standalone annualised capex guided at INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Aviation capex is driven by maintenance and engine cycles, with roughly 20–25% of depreciation as ongoing capex.
H2 is expected to bring higher volumes, but resourcing flex will determine margins; management aims for stable, consistent margin improvement.
No major expansion plans; growth is expected to be organic. Possible consolidation and expansion of southern hubs (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai, a few quarters away.
capex_capacity: Two major hubs added in North and a couple of medium-sized hubs in East in the prior period.
Freighter pallet utilisation at 85–90%; aircraft flown mainly at night and scheduled against available load.
Belly cargo is 30–40% of overall load in a typical month, and can reach 70–80% on lower-volume weekends. Blue Dart flies to 8 stations and carries belly cargo at 25–50 other locations.
The two aircraft acquired earlier are back to pre-acquisition pallet utilisation (as of 2024) and are integrated into the network.
demand_pricing: Growth came mainly from pricing: GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through. Management said yield was 'directionally' the main driver of revenue growth.
Fuel surcharge on surface is revised monthly based on local diesel prices, which rose in mid-May after about 5–6 years. Air fuel surcharge rose from April as Brent climbed from around mid-March.
Auto is a niche express vertical; management estimates it grows at about high-teens, in line with surface B2B. Market share is hard to quantify.
Management says e-commerce pricing remains competitive, with capacity still available in the market; Blue Dart positions itself as a premium player.
Management says it gained a very small but roughly stable market share in SME clients versus last year (informal assessment).

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue growth mainly from pricing, given volume growth was only about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed directionally. Pricing came from GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery (fuel surcharge offset fuel cost rises, which also lifted yield).

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-commerce growth lower than the industry, and is it a focus area?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce is a growth driver but not a mass-volume focus. It is prioritising premium, time-critical traffic that fits its capacity, and it is not targeting the largest e-commerce share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and new hubs?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone annualised capex is INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Two major northern hubs and some medium eastern hubs were added, and southern and Mumbai hub consolidation is being considered a few quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 brings volume opportunity but also resourcing challenges. It aims to keep or improve margins through efficiency and better realisation, without quantifying either.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 recently acquired aircraft stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said pallet utilisation was restored to pre-acquisition levels by 2024. The aircraft are part of the wider network, and capacity is not a constraint; yield is the main lever.

risks_watch: Growth quality: about 7% tonnage growth against about 15% revenue growth implies most of the increase came from pricing and surcharges, which may not persist.
Fuel: diesel and Brent rises were passed through with a lag; Q2 is expected to show the full surcharge effect, but any fall in fuel prices would reverse it.
Air volume growth of about 2.6% versus surface about 9% suggests air is stagnating in volume.
H2 resourcing: management flagged that peak-season flex will decide margins.
Competition in e-commerce pricing remains intense, with spare capacity in the market.
BFSI (documents and cards) is no longer growing, and the 25–30% documents-plus-parcels exposure needs monitoring.
Management declined to provide e-commerce split by air and surface, D2C share, or yield premium figures, limiting visibility.
526612|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's numbers and direction, but guarded on forward-looking detail: it declined to quantify yield, the e-commerce premium, and market share, and repeatedly deferred to seasonality rather than guiding.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,442 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +15%)

key_quotes: This seems to be a good quarter where what we have kind of put ourselves for seems to be bringing positive indications in terms of numbers moving in the right direction.

Blue Dart has been, I would say, focused on not playing on the volumes, but ensuring what we get as a piece from e-commerce works well to synergize with our capacities and adds profitability to the bottom line.

Iin short, from a capacity utilization, that has never been a challenge. It's a question of what kind of product that goes in, how critical or important it is for the customer to be able to pay the premium that ensures the profitability of the overall network.
So the effort will be to maintain or improve further. But we seem to be on the right path is what I would say.

526668|2026-03.headline: Kamat Hotels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 19% YoY to INR 110 crore, with EBITDA margin at 29%, and FY26 revenue INR 386 crore (+8%).
526668|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR 110 crore (+19% YoY), EBITDA of INR 32 crore (29% margin, +213 bps) and PAT of INR 18 crore (+59% YoY, 16% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR 386 crore (+8%), EBITDA INR 97 crore (25.1% margin) and PAT INR 39 crore (10.1% margin). Brand-level ARR and occupancy fell YoY because new hotels are still ramping up, and IRA Mumbai (a leased property, about INR 50 crore revenue) has been vacated from 31 March 2026. Management guided to a cautious outlook, did not give FY27 top-line guidance, and announced Milind Wadekar as incoming CFO.

segments.commentary: Occupancy and ARR fell sharply YoY (management referenced a 26% dip in the call); management attributed this to leadership change and sales-strategy issues, expects better FY27, and says the property is profitable.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand-level metrics fell because of new hotels with a wider base; Jadhavgadh had a mid-year slump, and a strategy change is under way. Management said the current EBITDA already reflects this, with gains expected next year as hotels mature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IRA Mumbai contribution, and how will it be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IRA Mumbai contributed about INR 50 crore revenue and about INR 20 crore EBITDA, and that the exit is roughly EBITDA-positive by INR 1-2 crore. Replacement will come from maturing hotels, new openings and tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 4% EBITDA compression, and is it sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Why are finance costs around INR 10 crore while borrowings fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not answer on the call and promised a follow-up. Other income of about INR 10 crore includes rent, interest from group companies, a INR 5 crore Ilex loan repayment and about INR 3 crore tax refund; a breakdown was promised.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 top line grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, but acknowledged the INR 50 crore IRA loss would reduce top line unless offset by other properties.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA drag from new properties and how many keys were added?
qa_highlights.answer: About 250-260 keys were added in FY26. The EBITDA drag is about INR 10 crore, of which about INR 6 crore should be absorbed into the gross operating profit (GOP) in the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold INR 40 crore of cash rather than prepay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers to hold cash as a contingency buffer rather than prepay the INR 86 crore loan at 9.75%, given the risk of shocks.

526797|2026-03.headline: Greenply Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit record INR776.2 crore (+19.6% YoY) with core EBITDA margin of 12%, up 150 bps YoY.
526797|2026-03.overview: Greenply reported its highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue of INR776.2 crore in Q4 FY26, with core EBITDA of INR93.2 crore at a 12% margin. MDF delivered its record quarter at INR189.4 crore revenue and 17% margin, while plywood volume grew 15.6% YoY. Management flagged a CEO/JMD resignation, a tax search operation, and a INR15.16 crore exceptional impairment linked to the Dubai entity, and guided to a 0.7-0.72 peak debt-to-equity during the MDF capex cycle. Part of Q4 volume growth was attributed to channel stocking in the second half of March, and chemical costs rose sharply, prompting price increases from April.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 record revenue INR189.4 crore on 62,000 CBM (+45.3% volume YoY), margin 17%. FY26 revenue INR635.6 crore (+19.9%), margin 13.4%. Price increases of 5% and 10% effective April 2026 (15% total per analyst confirmation); FY27 volume guidance 25-30%.

segments.name: Furniture & fittings JV
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales INR12.99 crore; FY26 revenue INR44.27 crore with PAT loss INR50.8 crore (Greenply share INR25.4 crore). Management expects breakeven around the middle of next year.

MDF volume growth of 25-30% in FY27, using near-full capacity; EBITDA margins to be kept consistent with recent performance (Q4 FY26 MDF margin 17% described as sustainable).
Management expects the March 2026 quarter consolidated margin to be the new norm, with H2 FY27 plywood margin upside from new process technology.

Plywood greenfield facility (Odisha) under construction at full pace with major orders placed.

Flooring line in MDF expected to be fully operational in early Q2 FY27, with annual top-line capacity of about INR70-75 crore at peak.

Timber prices stable in Q4 and expected flat for FY27. Imports of MDF largely wiped out due to BIS and dollar/freight conditions.

Advertising spend in Q4 lower YoY; management says the annual amount is unchanged and it is timing of expense recognition.

qa_highlights.question: Is MDF margin sustainable and is plywood double-digit margin sustainable with quality issues in the lower-end brand fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says MDF margin is sustainable, driven by volume and operating leverage on fixed costs, with cost increases already passed on. Plywood margin is sustainable if volume targets are met; process changes have improved quality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet trajectory after capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity may peak at 0.7-0.72 in one year, then return to 0.5-0.6 the following year; management does not want substantially higher debt.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-offs (Dubai/GMEL, forex) behind the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no further challenges, with all potential liability on equity, corporate guarantees and loan advances provided for in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume growth inflated by channel inventory, and does Q1 FY27 continue the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management partly agreed, noting some stocking in the second half of March, and attributed growth mainly to a shift from unorganised to organised players; Q1 FY27 has started strongly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and split of growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR425 crore MDF capex, roughly INR300 crore in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28; Odisha plywood about INR130 crore; plywood technology upgrades INR45-50 crore. Analyst estimated about INR480 crore for FY27, which management said was almost right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDF gross margin volatile and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q2 and Q3 volatility to line extension disruption and trading mix; Q4 FY26 margin is the base to deliver going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the income tax search conducted and is there any liability?
qa_highlights.answer: Search covered Greenply, Greenlam and Greenpanel; management said the reason is not known, no order or demand has been received, and the auditor has noted no liability.

qa_highlights.answer: He stepped down to pursue personal commitments and will continue as an advisor; sales, plant, IT, HR and marketing heads are in place, and a full-time replacement at his level is not planned immediately.

Plywood and MDF both delivered double-digit volume growth, but management said Q1 sales were lost to election-related labour disruption, lower plant utilisation (92-93% vs ~98-99% in Q4) and weak outsourcing. Price increases of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood were taken, and the new MDF flooring line started commercial production on 20 July 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth, and a 10% plywood margin.

526807|2026-06.headline: Seamec Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41% YoY to INR 297 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124 crore (about 42% margin).
526807|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 297 crore against INR 211 crore a year ago, up 41%, and standalone revenue was INR 283 crore against INR 201 crore. Consolidated PAT rose to INR 81 crore from INR 76 crore, while standalone PAT was flat at about INR 81 crore versus INR 80 crore. Management attributed the quarter to higher vessel deployment, healthy utilisation and cost discipline, with Paladin's dry-dock and the Middle East conflict weighing on the onshore segment. The call focused on the Seamec ANANT acquisition (USD 70 million, expected by end-August), the 40-42% margin band and the 15-20% growth CAGR target.

Gallant vessel sale: expected to complete in September 2026 after shareholder approval.
Seamec Princess/III: monsoon idle period (May-October); Princess being dry-docked in this period; contract talks for October at an advanced stage, not yet announced.

rows.why: No specific new product launch was discussed beyond the third plant and possible Aica tech transfer, which is unconfirmed.

rows.label: Aica acrylic tech transfer and possible acrylic volume
rows.why: Acrylic capacity is completely idle and Aica may begin taking acrylic, but management says this is unconfirmed and will take 3-4 months to know; Aica has joined the Board on 22 July with no operational role yet.

rows.label: Domestic restructuring (new team, distributors, warehouses)
rows.why: Domestic revenue has been stuck around INR300 crore for four years and volumes are flat versus Q4; management says the restructuring, which covers states beyond the four or five cities currently served, shows results only from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Price hike hold or reversal
rows.why: Price hikes were taken across 1 mm, 0.8 mm and compact laminates with no further hike planned; reversal would only come if war-driven input costs fall, which management says may take 6-9 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins and the plant timeline but defensive on domestic weakness and repeated delays, and evasive on price hike percentages and the next capex; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, plant slippage and the flat domestic run-rate.

527001|2026-03.headline: Ashapura Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 105% QoQ to INR1,969 crores, but management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA similar to or below Q4 on falling bauxite prices and freight.
527001|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR1,969 crores versus INR960 crores in Q3, with EBITDA of INR211 crores (vs INR143 crores) and PBT before exceptional items of INR147 crores (vs INR89 crores). For FY26, revenue rose 91% to INR5,237 crores, EBITDA rose to INR674 crores from INR445 crores, and PBT before exceptional items rose to INR450 crores from INR305 crores. Management said Q4 EBITDA per tonne fell to $5.9 on ocean freight, fuel costs and lower bauxite prices, and guided Q1 FY27 to be similar to or weaker than Q4. The Board recommended a 100% dividend for FY26.

financial_highlights.change: Decline attributed to ocean freight, fuel and bauxite prices

segments.name: Guinea (bauxite)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR4,200 crores with EBITDA of INR561 crores; bauxite exports about 8 million tons vs 3.5 million tons in FY25. Iron ore is still in commissioning and slower than planned.

segments.name: India (Bentonite & Allied Minerals, White Performance Minerals)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR998 crores with EBITDA of INR112 crores. Margins hit by fuel, transport, input costs and a lower-margin product mix.

segments.name: Specialty Adsorbent Solutions (50% JV, Ashapura Perfoclay)
segments.commentary: Impacted by a sharp rise in sulfuric acid prices, a key raw material. No segment figures given.

segments.name: Advanced Ceramic Materials (Orient Ceratech stake)
segments.commentary: Delivered encouraging growth vs prior year. No segment figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bauxite volume guided at 10-12 million tons, with 15 million tons targeted for FY28, contingent on freight, geopolitics and the quota system.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA expected to be similar to or a little worse than Q4 FY26; management expects the full FY27 EBITDA to be better than Q4 FY26 run-rate.
Management hopes FY27 EBITDA is better than FY26 but said clarity will come after the quota system is announced.
FY27 Guinea turnover guided at least about $700 million at about $70/t price; India expected to grow similarly to or slightly better than FY26, with EBITDA similar or slightly better.
Company focused on not increasing debt; debt reduction may come over the medium term as working capital rises with volumes.
India capex of about INR150 crores over the next year for plant upgrades and new products.
Boffa port capacity expansion from about 5 to about 10 million tons near completion; GSM port expansion targeted by end FY27-28; port capacity target of 27 million tons.
capex_capacity: Boffa port in Guinea being expanded from about 5 to about 10 million tons; described as on track and almost complete.
GSM port expansion to add 50-60% capacity, expected by end FY27-28.
Bauxite washing plant planned at 20,000 tonnes per day to upgrade non-marketable ore.

Iron ore beneficiation plant planned at north of 1.5 million tons; still at early due diligence, expected in 3-4 quarters. Capex may be handled by partners on a build-operate-transfer model rather than the balance sheet.
Seven new bentonite leases granted in the quarter to replenish India reserves.
demand_pricing: Management said bauxite CIF China rose from about $60 to $68-69/t, mainly due to freight increases on that route.
Aluminium metal trading near $3,600/t, expected to rise toward $4,000/t, supportive for bauxite demand.

Guinea government plans a bauxite quota system, possibly announced within the month; management expects exports to decline and net bauxite prices (bauxite minus freight) to improve after it, though details are not public.
Management said the company is a price taker and about 4% of Guinea's roughly 200 million ton export volume.
Long-term freight contracts with shipping lines held up during the quarter; talks under way with large shippers for longer-term freight arrangements.
India: value-added products in oil and gas and foundry; claimed about 35% India bentonite market share and over 40% of India's bentonite exports (to be verified).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 FOB realisation and was there a further bauxite price drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the press release figure of $5.9 EBITDA per tonne in Q4; said bauxite prices fell in Q4 and Q1 may still be difficult.

qa_highlights.question: Will Guinea's quota system stall new mining releases, and is it positive for Ashapura?
qa_highlights.answer: Details are not public; management believes the quota is aimed at large players (70-80 million tons) and should be positive for Ashapura.

qa_highlights.question: Is Ashapura required to build local refining or smelting capacity in Guinea?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ashapura's concessions carry no such terms, and no refinery or value-addition obligation exists today.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ashapura balance volume ramp-up against prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a price taker, sees no near-term constraint from prices, and would change strategy only if freight became very volatile or vessels were unavailable.

qa_highlights.question: Is there capex on iron ore and bauxite beneficiation?
qa_highlights.answer: Models under evaluation with partners, including BOT; management aims to limit balance-sheet capex, nothing finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 revenue and EBITDA ballparks?
qa_highlights.answer: Guinea turnover of at least about $700 million at about $70/t; India flat to slightly better; EBITDA to be clearer after the quota system but hoped to be better than FY26.

risks_watch: Guinea quota system: timing, allocation and impact on volumes and net bauxite prices remain unknown.
Freight and fuel costs, linked to the geopolitical conflict, may keep margins under pressure through Q1 FY27 and the monsoon quarter.
Iron ore ramp-up is slower than planned, with the quarter-to-quarter timeline for contribution still open.
India margins under pressure from sulfuric acid, fuel and product mix; FY27 India growth guided only as stable.
Working capital build from volume ramp-up could delay debt reduction despite the stated aim of not increasing debt.
Port capacity expansion timing (GSM by FY27-28) gates the 15 million ton target.

we are definitely currently more not focused on adding capex to our balance sheet as far as these projects are concerned.

527001|2026-06.headline: Ashapura Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR1,616 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR188.9 crore and margin fell to 11.7%.
527001|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations rose about 19% YoY to INR1,616 crore, while reported EBITDA was broadly flat at INR188.9 crore as higher fuel, marine freight and input costs absorbed the gain. PBT declined about 1.4% YoY to INR130.03 crore and EPS rose to INR12.07 from INR11.5. Guinea bauxite volumes fell to 2.34 million tons from 3.16 million tons in Q4, with bauxite EBITDA per ton rising to USD6.3 from USD5.9. India businesses were hit by fuel, freight and sulphuric acid costs, with the bleaching clay JV under the most pressure.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.16 mt in Q4 and 2.05 mt in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Guinea bauxite and iron ore
segments.commentary: Turnover about INR1,360 crore (84% of group) and EBITDA INR163 crore; volumes 2.34 mt, EBITDA USD6.3/t. Iron ore is in trial production with revenue not disclosed and EBITDA reported is bauxite-only.

segments.name: India bentonite and allied minerals / white performance minerals
segments.commentary: Wholly owned; bentonite broadly stable with domestic growth offsetting weaker exports, while white performance minerals profitability was hit by higher sales and distribution costs. No segment figures given.

segments.name: Bleaching clay (Ashapura Perfoclay, 50% JV)
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid, a key raw material, rose about five-fold over the past year to above INR30/kg, adversely affecting the business. No figures given.

segments.name: Advanced ceramics (Orient Ceratech, 32%)
segments.commentary: Management said segment EBITDA more than doubled on premium product mix, oil and gas demand and steel-industry materials. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bauxite volume target of 10-12 million tons retained with a potential variance of ±10% (about 9-11 mt); Q2 is seasonally weakest, with most sales in late Q3 and Q4.
Bauxite EBITDA per ton expected near USD6 (USD5.5-6 range) for the next one or two quarters; return toward ~USD10 is a medium to long-term expectation, timing not predicted.
Iron ore: 15 million ton target by FY28 reaffirmed ("achieve or even cross"), but long-term iron ore guidance needs a couple more quarters.
Guinea export quota system expected before end of CY2026, seen as supportive of realisations and freight.
Management expects bauxite revenue near USD1 billion (about INR10,000 crore) at 15 mt once conditions normalise.
India capex of close to INR200 crore planned across projects and verticals.
capex_capacity: Boffa port fully operational with capacity raised from 5 mtpa to 8 mtpa; no further expansion to 10-12 mt planned near-term, to be decided as volumes ramp.
GSM second port new jetty under construction, expected operational by Q4 FY27, raising capacity from 6 mtpa to 10 mtpa; combined port capacity about 23 mt.
Total bauxite export capacity stated at 18 million tons.
Bauxite washing plant set up with ~20,000 tons/day capacity, on an operate-and-transfer model; a comparable plant would cost about USD15 million and take about one year to build if expanded.
Ashapura has over 1 million tons of bentonite grinding capacity, which management described as the world's largest.
demand_pricing: Freight remains highly volatile and elevated; management expects volatility through 2027 and freight is the main margin overhang.
Chinese index bauxite price around USD72/t, up from ~USD61, mostly due to ocean freight rather than FOB Guinea price.
Alumina prices under pressure; management is positive on medium-term demand, citing four new Chinese refineries adding 20-30 mt of bauxite demand.
Middle East and Europe customer demand impacted by geopolitics and freight; company focusing on India, Asia and Africa.
Customer demand volatile; customers may take time to absorb market and cost changes.

qa_highlights.question: Status and timing of Guinea bauxite export quota system and expected realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the quota system before end of 2026 and sees realisations flat until then; margins also flat with freight overhang. FY28 15 mt target described as on track.

qa_highlights.question: Response to new entrants such as Nimba selling bauxite via monthly tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a new development with slow materialisation and will not significantly disrupt the market, with volumes likely going to other traders; Ashapura may participate in tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Impact and expansion of the washing plant on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is roughly EBITDA neutral and mainly a sustainability and throughput tool; no EBITDA quantification given; expansion would take about one year.

qa_highlights.question: Boffa port expansion beyond 8 mt to 10 mt by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No near-term plan; 8 mt is seen as reasonable for now, with expansion to 10-12 mt to follow volume ramp-up without a fixed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Fako deposit and China Railway arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an MOU; details under study and little progress to report, with possible update next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why no iron ore revenue disclosure, and is the 10 mt guidance achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore is in trial production with low revenue, so it is not split out; EBITDA disclosed is bauxite only. Guidance is 10-12 mt with ±10% variance, and management said it is broadly on track.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per ton outlook for Q2, FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term USD5.5-6/t; a return toward USD10/t is expected over the medium to longer term, timing uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of Orient Ceratech's EBITDA doubling and India growth levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are oil and gas product demand with debottlenecking and steel-industry materials replacing imports; India growth from cat litter, foundry, oil and gas, and kaolin for paper and paint.

risks_watch: Timing of the Guinea bauxite export quota system (management expects it before end-CY2026); realisations and freight are expected to stay flat until then.
Ocean freight volatility through 2027 and limited vessel availability; freight is the main margin overhang and the FY27 EBITDA per ton outlook (USD5.5-6) depends on it.
FY27 bauxite volume delivery: Q1 at 2.34 mt versus the 10-12 mt target with ±10% variance; Q2 is seasonally weakest and most sales land in late Q3 and Q4.
Competitive entry such as Nimba's monthly tenders, and whether Ashapura participates in tenders on viability.
India margin pressure from fuel, sulphuric acid (above INR30/kg, about five-fold YoY) and weak Middle East and Europe demand; the bleaching clay JV is most exposed.
Iron ore commercialisation remains undisclosed in revenue; long-term iron ore guidance deferred by a couple of quarters; Fako/China Railway deal is only an MOU with little progress.
key_quotes: Let us acknowledge that there is some pressure on EBITDA margin in the short-term. However, we remain optimistic about the future outlook.
So the objective of this plant is more on a sustainability perspective as we have put up the 20,000 tons kind of capacity in a short period of time.
So, I would take that also with a little bit pinch of salt.
So we are consciously taking a call to focus on profitability while this disrupted situation remains.
527001|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term Guinea bauxite and India value-added outlook but cautious on the near term, repeatedly flagging freight, fuel and vessel availability as the constraints on margins and volumes. It was evasive on quantification: it declined to give the washing plant's EBITDA impact, iron ore revenue or a firm EBITDA per ton path beyond the next one or two quarters.

rows.why: Bauxite volumes rose to 2.34 mt from 2.05 mt in Q1 FY26 (about +14% YoY) and Boffa is now at 8 mtpa, but Q1 fell from 3.16 mt in Q4 and Q2 is seasonally weak, so growth depends on the late Q3-Q4 sales concentration.

rows.why: FY27 bauxite target of 10-12 mt (±10%) was only held, not raised; Q1 volume was 2.34 mt, Q2 is seasonally weakest, and the near-term EBITDA/t range is USD5.5-6 against USD6.3 achieved in Q1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 volume of 2.34 mt is well below the 10-12 mt FY27 run-rate needed (about 2.5-3 mt per quarter on average), with Q2 seasonally weakest and most sales in late Q3 and Q4; freight volatility through 2027 is the main overhang, so the ±10% band is the safety valve.

rows.label: Guinea bauxite export quota system
rows.why: Management expects the quota system before end-2026 and says it is supportive of realisations and freight, while realisations stay flat until then.

rows.label: Orient Ceratech advanced ceramics growth
rows.why: Segment EBITDA more than doubled on premium mix, oil and gas demand and steel-industry materials replacing imports, though no figures were given.

rows.label: Fako deposit / China Railway arrangement
rows.why: Only an MOU with little progress to report; management flagged a possible update next year.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term Guinea bauxite (15 mt FY28, USD10/t medium term) and India value-added outlook but cautious near term on freight, fuel and vessel availability; analysts pushed on the washing plant EBITDA impact, iron ore revenue and the EBITDA/t path, which management large

530005|2026-03.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated volume about 44 Mt, EBITDA of INR1,253/t, and a INR240/share FY26 dividend, with India Cements brand migration completed.
530005|2026-03.overview: The call was the UltraTech Q4 FY26 earnings call, transcript filed by India Cements Ltd as a subsidiary disclosure. UltraTech crossed 200 Mt India capacity and committed to 242.5 Mt by FY28. Q4 realisations rose about 2.5% on grey cement pricing, with consolidated EBITDA per tonne at INR1,253 (INR1,296 excluding acquired assets). Management flagged West Asia-linked cost pressure, mainly bags (about INR90 crore hit in March) and a mark-to-market forex loss (about INR120-130 crore), and said price hikes taken in April offset it. The Board recommended a INR240/share dividend for FY26, and India Cements' 100% brand migration to UltraTech was completed at end-March 2026.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY25 excl. acquired assets was INR1,225/t; excl. acquired assets Q4 FY26 INR1,296/t
UltraTech brand volume up 19% YoY as stated
first profit after a long time, as stated
as stated by CFO in closing remarks
up from INR333/t in Q2 and INR305/t in Q3
dividend payout 37% of profit last year as stated

segments.name: India (UltraTech India, ~196 Mt capacity)
segments.commentary: Average utilisation above 80% and about 90% per the CFO; trade mix around 66-67%. Ex-West Asia aberrations, India EBITDA was about INR1,240/t per management.

segments.name: UAE / overseas (~5 Mt)
segments.commentary: Utilisation fell from 100% pre-conflict to about 80%, now recovering. Bulk-only, so no bag cost. Q4 EBITDA INR278 crore.

segments.name: India Cements (acquired)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA INR497/t, with INR200/t of underlying margin sitting in UltraTech's books under the tolling arrangement, giving about INR670/t on a combined basis. Target above INR1,000/t by FY28. Q4 volume 3.12 Mt, of which 0.39 Mt non-UltraTech brand.

segments.name: Kesoram (acquired)
segments.commentary: Already operating at more than INR1,000/t EBITDA in Q4 per management. Brand migration fully complete.

segments.name: Cable and wire
segments.commentary: About INR800 crore of an INR1,800 crore capex spent; management expects launch around Q3 FY27 (first month of Q3).

guidance_outlook: Sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum; double-digit volume growth targeted for FY27 (industry 6.5% for FY26 as cited by management).
Capacity to reach 242.5 Mt in phases by FY28 with 37 Mt of further additions committed; growth beyond 240 Mt being planned.
Annual capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore from internal accruals for the foreseeable future; leverage to stay below 1x.
Cost efficiency programme: about INR185/t delivered; target above INR300/t, now expected to be exceeded by FY28.
Clinker factor (clinker-to-cement ratio) target 1.54x by FY28, from 1.48x currently; the company will remain fully clinker-backed.
Green power: about 43% of power from green sources; target about 85% by end FY30.

Price hikes taken in April 2026 management views as sufficient to offset bag cost increase (about INR6/bag) and sustain profitability; diesel and June-quarter fuel (about INR1.77-1.8/kcal) not fully factored in.
capex_capacity: Capacity at 200 Mt in India; 37 Mt more committed in a phased manner, taking capacity above 242.5 Mt by FY28.
India Cements: INR1,592 crore committed for efficiency improvement, plus INR400 crore for capacity expansion; Kesoram cost-improvement capex of INR400-500 crore.
Acquired ICL and Kesoram assets together are about 13% of consolidated capacity.
No thermal capacity to be added; the mix shifts to WHRS and renewables. Lead distance 367 km; new Lucknow bulk terminal.
demand_pricing: Grey cement prices rose about 2.5% in most geographies in Q4, helped by trade mix and premiumisation; April 2026 cement price increases were taken.
Industry volume growth in the March quarter estimated at 6-7%; FY26 industry growth estimated at 6.5%.
Trade/non-trade mix about 65-68%; rural demand described as steady.
Bag prices rose from about INR9 to INR15 a bag during March, and about INR13-14 by late April. Bag supply was described as expensive but not a constraint.
Management said price hikes were 'here to stay' given cost inflation across the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Is a high payout ratio sustainable given the balance sheet and capex funded from internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on performance and the Board; FY26 dividend of INR240/share is described as the highest level, with a possible repeat next year but no commitment.

qa_highlights.question: How much West Asia cost impact is in Q4 and how should June quarter look?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental bag cost in Q4 was about INR90 crore, which cannot be annualised. Power and fuel are not expected to be a large issue in June; a mark-to-market forex hit of about INR120-130 crore is in EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India Cements' INR1,000/t target comes from cost versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost programmes and price increases are both contributors. INR200/t of EBITDA sits in UltraTech's books; combined EBITDA is about INR670/t already, with the target including both books.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the India Cements merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy legal cases inherited with India Cements have to be closed first; management wants no risk to UltraTech before the next phase of integration.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UltraTech balance sheet ring-fenced from the group's RCB exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not a penny has moved from the UltraTech balance sheet for other purposes, and it is committed to keeping it ring-fenced.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cement lagging other building materials on price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the lag mainly to industry fragmentation, and said price increases typically come in Q1 of the financial year.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: sustained high pet coke (about $160/t cited by an analyst), oil near $100/bbl and diesel pass-through, which management says is not yet factored in.
Bag cost volatility and whether the April price hikes hold through monsoon (July-September).
Forex: $950 million of hedged foreign currency borrowings marked at INR94.85/$ at 31 March; the rupee moved to about INR94.2 by late April, so a mark-to-market effect can reverse.
Whether India Cements' remaining legal cases close, allowing the next integration phase.
Whether the INR200/t of India Cements EBITDA in UltraTech's books comes through and the INR300/t efficiency programme is delivered.
Sustainability of the dividend payout beyond the special FY26 payout, and the RMC (ready-mix concrete) growth plan (no monetisation planned).
530005|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on capacity, integration and dividend, but guarded and deflecting on West Asia cost trajectory, diesel, forward pricing and the India Cements merger timeline. Several answers were framed as 'we will wait and watch'.
key_quotes: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.
We said we would do these things, we have done them and we enter fiscal '27 in a stronger strategic position than at any point in our history.
Not a penny has moved from UltraTech balance sheet for any other purposes.
