rows.why: Utilisation at about 90% across the network with 37 Mt already committed, and management plans INR8,000-10,000 crore of annual capex from internal accruals, so further expansion beyond 240 Mt is being planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth and 7-8% sustainable growth, and the April price hikes are described as sufficient to offset bag costs, but no revenue or margin guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: West Asia pressure is not yet fully in the numbers: diesel and June-quarter fuel (about INR1.77-1.8/kcal) are not factored in, bag costs rose from about INR9 to INR15 a bag in March, and the INR120-130 crore forex MTM hit is in EBITDA, though April price hikes are said to offset it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The INR1,800 crore cable and wire business has INR800 crore spent, with launch guided around the first month of Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Efficiency programme to INR300/t+ by FY28
rows.why: About INR185/t already delivered against a target above INR300/t, now expected to be exceeded by FY28.

rows.label: Leverage below 1x while funding capex
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA is 0.94x consolidated and capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore a year is funded from internal accruals, with leverage guided to stay below 1x.

rows.label: April 2026 price hikes hold
rows.why: Price hikes taken in April are seen as offsetting bag costs of about INR6/bag, but grey cement prices rose only about 2.5% in Q4 and the monsoon is a test.

tone.note: Management was confident on capacity, volume growth and the dividend, but guarded on West Asia cost trajectory, diesel, forward pricing and the India Cements merger timeline; analysts pushed on those cost and integration points.

530005|2026-06.headline: UltraTech Q1 FY27: domestic grey volume up 13.1% to 81% utilisation, EBITDA INR5,146 crore and PAT INR2,604 crore (+17.2%).
530005|2026-06.overview: The document is headed India Cements Ltd but the enclosed transcript is UltraTech Cement's Q1 FY27 earnings call (held 20 July 2026), with CFO Atul Daga presenting. Domestic grey cement volume grew 13.1% YoY, with capacity utilisation at 81% versus 76%, and revenue rose 16%. Management flagged a fuel and packing cost shock during the quarter and guided to a further INR130-140 per ton cost increase in Q2 FY27. India Cements turnaround continued, with EBITDA per ton at INR603 versus roughly INR386 in Q2 FY26, and Cables and Wires remains on track for Q3 FY27 launch.

financial_highlights.value: About INR12 per bag average from INR9
financial_highlights.change: up about INR3/bag average in quarter

financial_highlights.metric: India Cements revenue (ex-factory, net of freight)

financial_highlights.change: from about INR386 in Q2 FY26, INR400 and INR509 in intervening quarters

segments.name: Grey cement (UltraTech incl. India Cements and Kesoram)
segments.commentary: Domestic volume up 13.1% with 81% utilisation on a 200 mtpa base; brand growth of 21.3%. East was the slowest region in the quarter, South and North were just below 15%, West and Central above 15%.

segments.name: India Cements (turnaround)
segments.commentary: Brand migration to UltraTech is 100% complete; revenue up 21% and volume up 19% like-for-like; conversion ratio 1.5x. Management targets INR1,000 per ton EBITDA with the full capex benefit from Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Cables and Wires
segments.commentary: INR1,800 crore programme with INR888 crore spent or committed to date; commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Oct-Dec 2026 quarter (Q3 FY27).

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting double-digit grey cement volume growth for FY27.
Industry volume growth in Q1 FY27 estimated at 7-8% (management's marketing intelligence), though 'too early'.
Q2 FY27 cost increase guided at INR130-140 per ton (fuel, maintenance, operating deleverage, monsoon), with measures planned to absorb part of it.
Industry expects cement prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter; management said it will attempt higher prices.
Capacity to reach 212.7 mtpa grey by end FY27 and about 235 mtpa by March 2028; consolidated capacity beyond 242 mtpa.
Management expects a better H2 FY27 cost position if the West Asia conflict eases; India Cements EBITDA of INR1,000 per ton remains the target, with full benefit from Q4 FY28.
Company does not give formal Cables and Wires guidance; net debt to EBITDA expected to remain below 1x for FY27.
capex_capacity: Domestic capacity at 200.1 mtpa and total capacity 205.5 mtpa after commissioning of 8.7 mt of UltraTech capacity (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu) in the quarter.
Projects under execution backed by about INR17,000 crore capex over the next 2-2.5 years; all growth capex funded from internal accruals.
Green power at 1,897 MW (about 47% of power requirement at quarter end); 71 MW renewables and 19 MW WHRS commissioned in the quarter; target 2.5-3 GW shortly.
India Cements cost-improvement capex of about INR2,000 crore (WHR, preheater and cooler upgrades); green power share to rise from about 3% to about 86% by end FY28.
Lead distance down to 360 km from 367 km; AFR substitution ramping up.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong and broadening, citing infrastructure, housing, urban real estate, ports, data centres and metro projects.
All-India exit prices improved through June; East and South led increases, Central and West steady, North consistent.
Premiumisation and blended cement mix support blended realisations; RMC is about 3.5% of UltraTech sales and retail about 65-66%.
Blended coal cost was USD134/ton in the quarter (INR1.9/kcal cited); currently about INR2/kcal and inventory-loaded.
Diesel (industrial) rose from about INR78-80/litre pre-war to about INR150-157, lifting limestone raising costs by about 13-14% QoQ per the raw material index.
Pet coke now costlier than coal on an energy basis, so coal is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: How will growing operating cash flow be deployed across dividends and cement capex, and will cables and wires capex scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flows are fully booked for growth capex and dividends; no further cables and wires investment is foreseen for now, with the business first maturing.

qa_highlights.question: What remains before India Cements is merged into a standalone entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex programme completion and disposal of non-core land are pending; the journey is expected to complete in Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier, with some operating parameters still to bring in line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 FY27 cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increase of INR130-140 per ton expected in Jul-Sep quarter, covering fuel, maintenance, deleverage; Q1 one-off impact was about INR40 on fuel and about INR20 on bags.

qa_highlights.question: Regional demand trends?
qa_highlights.answer: East was slowest in April-June (elections, labour availability); South and North below 15%; West and Central above 15%. East expected to see a multi-year upcycle.

qa_highlights.question: Industry volume growth for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimated at 7-8% based on marketing intelligence; management noted it is early.

qa_highlights.question: Growth beyond 240 mtpa and inorganic options?
qa_highlights.answer: Inorganic opportunities will be examined; the team is working on plans beyond 240 mtpa and details will follow.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and fuel cost volatility: crude above USD100 at the start of the quarter, with ocean freight insurance up to 4-5% from under 1%.
Q2 FY27 margin pressure of INR130-140/ton from fuel, maintenance and monsoon deleverage; watch whether management absorbs part of it.
Monsoon and dry spells (Rajasthan, some other states) could affect rural demand and next-year water-linked construction.
Cables and Wires: Q3 FY27 launch timeline, working capital build-up over the next 6 months, and ramp-up.
Industry capacity plans may be revised, per management comments on the 2027-28 industry capacity number.
India Cements per-ton EBITDA trajectory towards INR1,000/t and the India Cements merger timeline (Q4 FY28).
530005|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with strong emphasis on demand, brand and track record. Management was candid on near-term cost pressure but gave few hard numbers on the longer term; it deflected several questions (e.g., cables and wires guidance, challenges over 5 years, capacity additions by the industry).
key_quotes: We intend to grow like a challenger and not an incumbent.
We absorbed the shock better than any peer, and we will harvest the relief faster than any peer.
We said we will cross 200 million tons; we did a year early.
Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating EBITDA per ton held flat at above INR1,200 in Q1, and a further INR130-140/t cost increase is guided for Q2 FY27 with only partial offset from measures planned.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 to Q4 FY27; ~235 mtpa by Mar 2028
rows.why: 8.7 mt commissioned in Q1 FY27 and about INR17,000 crore of projects under execution take capacity to 212.7 mtpa by end FY27 and about 235 mtpa by March 2028, with utilisation already at 81%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic grey volume grew 13.1% YoY in Q1 FY27 at 81% utilisation, and management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27 on new capacity coming on stream.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 81% (up from 76%), which points to new capacity, but management says the programme is already funded to 235 mtpa and it is working on plans beyond 240 mtpa with details to follow, so timing is not firm.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is targeting double-digit grey volume growth for FY27 but gave no upgrade; Q1 industry volume growth is estimated at 7-8%, and the cost outlook for Q2 is worse.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management guided a INR130-140/t cost increase in Q2 FY27 from fuel, maintenance and monsoon deleverage, and crude is above USD100 with diesel up to INR150-157/litre from about INR78-80.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Cables and Wires commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Oct-Dec 2026 on an INR1,800 crore programme with INR888 crore spent or committed.

rows.label: India Cements EBITDA INR1,000/t target
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA is at INR603/t (from about INR386 in Q2 FY26) with brand migration 100% complete, and the full capex benefit (about INR2,000 crore cost-improvement programme) is expected from Q4 FY28.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA is 0.87x, down from 0.94x at start of year, and management expects it to stay below 1x for FY27 with growth capex funded from internal accruals.

rows.label: Cement price increases
rows.why: All-India exit prices improved through June, but the industry expects prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter, and management says it will attempt higher prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, brand and capacity additions, and candid on the INR130-140/t Q2 cost pressure. Analysts pushed on the cost outlook and the cables and wires plan; management gave few longer-term numbers and deflected some questions.

530005|2026-09.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; spot trade prices ~5% above Q2 average entering Q3.
530005|2026-09.overview: UltraTech reported a strong Q2 FY27 on volume growth of 13.8% and a 21% rise in net profit, despite fuel costs rising sharply on the West Asia conflict. Q2 average trade prices were flat to Q1 (down 1-1.5%), but prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in late September and kept rising in October, with management putting spot about 5% above the Q2 average. Fuel cost rose from INR 45 to INR 51.5 per bag, and management expects the cost pressure to largely persist through Q3-Q4 at roughly INR 2.2 per kcal. Capacity reached 204.7 Mt domestic after 4.6 Mt commissioning in September, and the Ultravolt wires and cables business launched on 3 September. Net debt rose to 1.26x net debt/EBITDA from 0.94x at March-end.

segments.name: Cement - North
segments.commentary: Volumes grew more than 20% YoY; utilisation upwards of 70%; new prices absorbed.

segments.name: Cement - South
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 15-20% YoY on about 50 Mt capacity; utilisation above 70%; capacities fully sold out; prices improving. A greenfield plant was commissioned this quarter.

segments.name: Cement - West
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 10%; utilisation close to 70%; Mumbai prices up 3-4% per bag in September.

segments.name: Cement - East
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 5%; utilisation about 60% due to heavy monsoon; prices fell in August and are now catching up since early October.

segments.name: Cement - Central
segments.commentary: Volumes grew about 10%; utilisation about 60%; pricing described as muted.

segments.name: Ultravolt (wires and cables)
segments.commentary: Launched 3 September 2026; about 25-27 days of operation in Q2. INR 1,100 crore of INR 1,800 crore capex spent or committed; 80,000+ retail points and 1,500+ UBS channel partners signed up; management says it will not talk about revenue or margin yet and expects a meaningful quarter in April-June 2027. Expense attributable to the business is not material per management.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 capex guidance held at about INR 10,000 crore (plus or minus); fuller view promised after Q3 results.
Full benefit of recent price increases expected to reflect in Q3 earnings rather than immediately; management intends to sustain YoY higher EBITDA per ton over the next two quarters.
Pet coke and fuel cost: management sees the INR 2.2/kcal level persisting through Q3-Q4 if $180/t pet coke holds; marginal impact expected in Q4 from inventory pipeline.
Targets 240 Mt capacity as planned; next organic growth phase to be announced before FY27 end, with detailed plans to come.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1x by March 2027.
Business-as-usual delivery of INR 1,400/t EBITDA exit-March 2028 target; cost pressures expected to be covered by price increases.
Ultravolt maturity expected by FY28; Board has not sanctioned capex beyond INR 1,800 crore; target revenue reference of INR 10,000 crore now seen at INR 16,000-18,000 crore on copper prices.
Industry demand expected to grow close to 8% in H1 FY27 and to remain strong through March 2029.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 4.6 Mt in September 2026, including the 3.6 Mt greenfield at Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) and 1 Mt debottlenecking at three units; domestic capacity now 204.7 Mt.
On track for 240 Mt capacity as planned.
Added 116 MW renewable power and 10 MW waste heat recovery; 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use.
AFR systems commissioned at 2 plants; thermal substitution rate about 7.2%.

Ultravolt: INR 1,800 crore plan with about INR 1,100 crore spent or committed; balance expected over about two quarters; mother plant at Jhagadia, Gujarat; 78,000 tpa copper consumption capacity annualised.
demand_pricing: Q2 average trade prices flat vs Q1 (down about 1-1.5%) due to soft August; trade prices rose 7-10 per bag MoM in late September, and exit-September trade was at least about 3% above Q1 average.
Spot realisations in October about 5% above Q2 average, per management.
Trade ratio stable at 65-67% (65.7% in Q2 per management); premium cement 37% of sales; blended cement 67.3%.
Over 25% of trade sales come through the UBS network (about 6,500 stores, target 10,000 by FY28-29).
Industry demand close to 10% YoY in Q2; management says the Q1 industry rate was 6.5%.
Fuel costs: pet coke about $180/t; pet coke share cut to about 25% of mix; domestic coal supply constrained as Coal India prioritises power sector.
Public infrastructure awards picking up; central capex strong through July; road construction weak.

qa_highlights.question: Variable cost inflation in H2 at current spot levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify but noted inventory in the pipeline means Q3 impact is limited and marginal impact in Q4; expects not much additional inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Tamil Nadu levy of INR 160/t: accounted in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is already accounted for in Q2 with no reversal, and the company incurs no additional cost from the effective date.

qa_highlights.question: Capex guidance and H1 capex of INR 5,882 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held full-year capex at about INR 10,000 crore plus or minus, to be refined after Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise about 22% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore NCDs at 7.25% were raised and held for about two months; management said the borrowing was a good decision given current rates.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt increase in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex and dividend payment; net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March-end, with expected to fall below 1x by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is trade volume demand housing-led or industrial-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade ratio stable at 65-67%, indicating retail housing demand holds share; industrial volumes growing faster; industry sold 463 Mt in FY26 vs UltraTech 145 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: Ultravolt capacity and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 10,000 crore revenue target from early 2025 could reach INR 16,000-18,000 crore at current copper prices; no further capex beyond INR 1,800 crore sanctioned; production to double from current levels.

risks_watch: Fuel and energy costs: pet coke about $180/t, domestic coal constraint, and industrial diesel at record highs; West Asia conflict outcome uncertain.
Weak monsoon (fourth lowest since 2001) and drought pockets could soften rural demand.
Ultravolt ramp-up: stock-outs possible, unproven margins, and no revenue disclosure yet; separately reported from next quarter as a division of the standalone financials.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x; capex and dividend are funding needs.
Festive-season slowdown may delay full realisation of price increases until Q3 results.

Management repeatedly deflected to "give us some time" for the new business and declined to quantify cost trajectory beyond INR 2.2/kcal.

rows.why: Fuel cost at INR 51.5/bag vs INR 45 and pet coke around $180/t with domestic coal constrained; weak monsoon (fourth lowest since 2001) could soften rural demand and delay price realisation until Q3 results.

rows.when: already launched 3 Sept 2026; meaningful quarter Apr-Jun 202
rows.why: Ultravolt wires and cables launched 3 September 2026 with INR 1,100 crore of INR 1,800 crore spent or committed and 80,000+ retail points signed up, though revenue and margins are not yet disclosed.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x by March 2027
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x at end-Sep 2026 from 0.94x at March 2026, and management guides below 1x by March 2027 as EBITDA rises with price increases.

rows.label: UBS retail network expansion to 10,000 stores
rows.why: Over 25% of trade sales come through about 6,500 UBS stores, with the target at 10,000 by FY28-29; Ultravolt has 1,500+ UBS channel partners signed up.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and volume momentum with specific numbers, but evasive on Ultravolt margins and utilisation and on H2 cost inflation, deflecting to 'give us some time'; analysts pushed on H2 variable cost inflation, the interest cost jump, and the net debt rise.

530007|2026-03.headline: JK Tyre Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 42% YoY to Rs.546 crore on 12.9% margin, with a further Rs.4,980 crore brownfield expansion approved.
530007|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs.4,233 crore and PAT rose 83% to Rs.188 crore, with FY26 revenue at a record Rs.16,384 crore. Management said volume growth was broad-based, led by domestic OE and TBR, and margin expansion came from volumes, mix and cost control. Raw material costs are expected to rise 18-20% in Q1 FY27, which management is offsetting with staggered price hikes of 4-5% (replacement) and 5-7% (export), with a further 5-6% under way. The Board approved Rs.4,980 crore of additional PCR and TBR brownfield capacity to 2029, on top of the Rs.1,130 crore already under implementation.

segments.name: Consolidated mix Q4 FY26 (by revenue)
segments.commentary: Truck & bus ~56%, PLR ~27%, non-truck bias ~13%, 2/3W ~4%. Market split: replacement 63%, OE 27%, exports ~10%.

segments.name: Standalone mix Q4 FY26
segments.commentary: Truck & bus 59%, PLR 25%, non-truck bias 12%, 2/3W 5%. Standalone replacement 61%, OE 30%.

segments.name: JK Tornel (Mexico)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.2,138 crore (FY25: Rs.2,147 crore); FY26 EBITDA Rs.141 crore, PBT Rs.61 crore (+63%), PAT Rs.42 crore (+91%). Q4 revenue Rs.378 crore, EBITDA Rs.24 crore (+36% YoY); management described Q4 as sluggish on US tariff uncertainty.

segments.name: Domestic India volumes
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic volumes +21% YoY; OE +42%. TBR replacement +19%, TBR OE +53%. Passenger line +16% (replacement +10%, OE +26%). Farm volumes +58% (replacement +30%, OE nearly doubled, exports +44%). 2/3W OE +72%, 2/3W exports +31%.

segments.name: Exports (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 export volumes steady; FY26 export volumes +5%. Passenger exports +20% for FY26. Premium 16-inch+ domestic sales +13% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Raw material prices expected to rise 18-20% in Q1 FY27 vs Q4 FY26 (CFO-level figure stated as 18-19% later in Q&A); management sees some softening in crude and possible raw material relief from Q3 FY27 if conditions hold.
Further price hike of 5-6% under way on top of 4-5% already taken in replacement (5-7% in exports); OEM price increases lag. Mainly taken in Q1 FY27.
Management expects demand to remain buoyant in FY27, with mid-single-digit growth in some categories; no OEM order cuts seen.
Cash outlay of about Rs.1,200 crore per year; total expansion of Rs.6,110 crore (Rs.1,130 crore + Rs.4,980 crore) to complete by FY29, with debt-to-equity of about 2:1 on the projects.
Rs.1,130 crore expansion to complete by Q3 FY28; capacity for TBR and PCR to rise 24%.
capex_capacity: Installed capacities fully utilised across segments; India utilisation above 90% for FY26.
Rs.1,130 crore expansion under implementation (mainly TBR, some PCR), completion by Q3 FY28.
Board approved further brownfield PCR and TBR expansion of Rs.4,980 crore in phases until 2029, increasing TBR and PCR capacity by 24%.
Management stated the Rs.4,980 crore plan is in addition to the Rs.1,130 crore; the total of Rs.6,110 crore is to be spent over three to four years.
2/3W: growth via productivity improvements and expanded outsourcing of 2/3W tyres.
demand_pricing: Q4 price hikes of 4-5% in replacement and 5-7% in export; OEM pricing lags. Competitors have taken hikes in the same range, per management.
Management reports no OEM order book cuts across CV, passenger or other lines, though supply chains were disrupted by the West Asia crisis.
New OEM approvals in FY26 from Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra, Switch Mobility, VECV and Euler Motors; 50+ new brand shops added.
Management cited the Levitas Ultra premium passenger offering, puncture guard and smart tyres, and the 'selling miles' fleet mobility programme as barriers to entry against new entrants.
Management noted a peer's warning on possible demand moderation from price hikes, but did not give a view on Q2/H2 demand impact.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 market and category mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated: replacement 63%, OE 27%, exports ~10%. Truck & bus ~56%, PLR ~27%, non-truck bias ~13%, 2/3W ~4%. Standalone: truck & bus 59%, PLR 25%, replacement 61%, OE 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mexico (JK Tornel) decline QoQ, and was there an impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mexico was sluggish in Q4 due to geopolitical volatility and US tariff uncertainty. FY26 revenue was steady at Rs.2,138 crore vs Rs.2,147 crore. No impairment was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hike came in Q4 vs Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly in Q1 FY27. OEM price increases lag, and a further 5-6% hike is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded, and what is the FY27 outlay?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash outlay of ~Rs.1,200 crore per year. Debt will be taken, supported by higher EBITDA; project funding is about 2:1 debt-to-equity. Leverage expected to stay comfortable at 2-3 year levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds from the Dec-2023 QIP, held in fixed deposits, have been gradually withdrawn and deployed into expansion projects, reducing interest income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook and order book position?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand expected to stay buoyant in FY27, with strong or mid-single-digit growth in some categories. No OEM order cuts seen.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.5,000 crore capex in addition to the Rs.1,130 crore, and when does the Rs.1,130 crore finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the new plan is in addition. The Rs.1,130 crore is under implementation and will complete by Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material outlook for Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs are rising ~18-19% in Q1 FY27. Some softening in crude is expected, which could ease raw material costs beyond Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How has competition responded to price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Competitors have taken price hikes in the same range (about 4-5%).

qa_highlights.question: How will JK Tyre defend its position against new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an entrenched OEM and fleet position, premium products, the selling miles fleet programme, and OEM technical norms in passenger cars.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for 2/3W and off-highway?
qa_highlights.answer: 2/3W growth via productivity gains and outsourcing, with more outsourcing planned. No specific off-highway plan was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Rs.6,000 crore outlay over 3-4 years be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. FY26 cash generation exceeded Rs.1,600 crore; the outlay includes planned borrowings and internal accruals. Spending can rise if needed.

risks_watch: Raw material costs guided up 18-20% (CFO 18-19%) in Q1 FY27; margin sustainability depends on speed and size of price hikes (4-5% taken, further 5-6% under way) and OEM lag effects

Mexico (JK Tornel) Q4 slowdown tied to US tariff uncertainty; Q4 revenue Rs.378 crore; USMCA review due July 2026

Capex execution: Rs 652 crore pool with bulk deploying in H2 FY27; Rs 316 crore Middle East revenue-generating capex expected Q3-Q4 FY27 despite supply-chain disruption; watch OEM delivery and commissioning dates.

Renewable E&C margins and execution: wind E&C margin 18% before unallocated costs (10-12% after); guided to 12-15%; ~15% of Rs 686 crore order book may slip into FY28 on client delays and POCM revenue recognition.

Blended margin dilution as Sangreen grows toward one-third of revenue; FY27 EBITDA guided Rs 525-575 crore, and debt-to-equity of 0.72x gross ceiling (management says net 0.3-0.7x) with cost of debt and blended borrowing cost not disclosed until half-year.
key_quotes: So, overall, we grew the top line and gave back margin and that is the real outcome.
So, Saudi is not a response to India and India is not a response to Saudi Arabia.
So, the ECL provision is expected to normalize in the course of the financial year as we recover debtors which has basically aged.

530075|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose to Rs.90 crore (about 71% margin, Rs.83 crore or 69% ex one-off) on flat volumes; exit guidance 2,500 BOEPD, 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
530075|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs.121.7 crore and net profit of Rs.57.3 crore, with volumes flat QoQ and realised oil down to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl. Management reiterated a 2,500 BOEPD exit for FY27 and 3,500 BOEPD next year, with 5,000 BOPD targeted by FY29 on onshore assets only. The company signed two KG Onshore and Cambay Basin revenue sharing contracts (DSF IV) on 22 October 2026. Bakrol's 10-well campaign is complete, Karjisan's seven-well campaign is under way, and October production was about 2,000 BOEPD. Balance sheet is debt-free with about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments and Rs.780 crore equity.

segments.name: Cambay Basin (Bakrol, Karjisan, Lohar, Cambay)
segments.commentary: Bakrol average about 950 BOE/d in October after the 10-well drilling and fracking campaign; Karjisan (PSC, royalty and cess under 5% of top line) has seven wells planned this fiscal, two drilled but not yet on production. Cambay field (50% JV with Synergia) has one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027.

segments.name: KG Onshore
segments.commentary: Seven new discoveries added, about nine fields in total, of which only Mukkamala is producing; management says resource base may be larger than the offshore portfolio. Single-rig, multi-well appraisal planned; a resource estimate to follow after third-party reserve work. Wells expected to cost about $10 million more than Cambay's roughly $1.5 million.

segments.name: Duarmara (Assam, JV)
segments.commentary: Duarmara-4Z found oil in the TIPAM-1 zone rather than the expected gas; oil recirculated to surface twice. Well cost about Rs.60-70 crore, and a plan covering wells 1, 2 and 4 is due over the next five to six months. Gas monetisation is constrained by Assam's lack of National Grid connection.

segments.name: Offshore
segments.commentary: Treated as optionality; excluded from the 5,000 BOPD guidance, with management focus shifting to it in FY28-29.

guidance_outlook: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD, with Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells as the main drivers; October production was about 2,000 BOEPD (one answer cited about 1,950).
Exit FY28 at about 3,500 BOEPD and FY29 at about 5,000 BOEPD, onshore only; minimal contribution assumed from KG and Duarmara.
EBITDA margin expected to stay above 65% for the year; management says its endeavour is to keep margins in line.
Capex guided at Rs.250 crore for FY27 (against Rs.220 crore in FY26), with funding via internal accruals for now; no commitment on debt or equity raises.
KG Onshore development plan and capex guidance to come after field development plans are filed with regulators; Duarmara oil plan in five to six months.
capex_capacity: Bakrol 10-well campaign complete (drilling and fracking); production response showing Bakrol as a multi-year growth field.
Karjisan: seven wells planned for FY27; two drilled, first perforation expected within about a week, rig back on site.
Cambay field: one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; field area about 160 sq km.
Duarmara: well cost Rs.60-70 crore; TIPAM-1 oil zone; partner alignment needed.
Historical capex: Rs.51 crore (FY23), Rs.160 crore (FY24), Rs.87 crore (FY25), Rs.220 crore (FY26), Rs.250 crore (FY27 target).
demand_pricing: Pricing is linked to international crude benchmarks; Cambay crude sells at about a 10% discount to dated Brent on average, with most volumes to Indian Oil and about 20% to private buyers at a slightly higher discount.
Realised oil ran about $76 in July, $84 in August and above $100 in September.
Royalty and cess are about 30% of top line in Bakrol and Cambay versus under 5% in Karjisan, averaging about 15-16% of revenue.
Variable handling cost is about $1-1.5 per barrel on ONGC tolling; fixed costs are about 70-75% of the cost base.
Management's investment hurdle: double-digit returns at $65-70/bbl, cash back within one to one-and-a-half years, and no loss at $50/bbl.
Assam gas is sold at a discount to APM prices because Assam is not connected to the National Grid; oil is easier to truck out.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins above 65% be sustained for the full year as costs stay flat while volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed costs are 70-75% of the cost base and incremental barrels are cheaper in Cambay; KG will add establishment costs, but margins should hold. Management's stated aim is to keep margins in line, not a firm guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental revenue will Karjisan and Bakrol add, and does the 2,500 exit depend on Cambay?
qa_highlights.answer: Bakrol is at about 950 BOE/d. Karjisan's seven wells are already in the 2,500 exit figure, which management said has no ambiguity; Cambay optionality wells sit outside it and could take production beyond 5,000.

qa_highlights.question: How will KG Onshore be funded and ramped up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to decide between internal accruals, debt or equity; it will start with one rig, drill a couple of wells and then decide on a bigger campaign. Wells cost about $10 million more than Cambay wells.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing formula and price range should be used for sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set by a crude-yield-based discount to dated Brent (about 10%), and investments are screened at $50-70/bbl. Management gave no explicit bear-to-bull range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Duarmara oil potential, capex per well and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Well cost Rs.60-70 crore with 3.5 km wells. Oil is light, and flow and frac options are being studied. A concrete estimate is expected next fiscal, not this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CWIP high and why are deferred tax liabilities rising?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs.100 crore of the Rs.190 crore CWIP is Duarmara, to be capitalised on production. Deferred tax is rising because drilling capex is fully expensed for tax; it may partly reverse if drilling slows.

risks_watch: Duarmara gas evacuation and oil development path are unresolved, with the TIPAM-1 oil zone yet to be tested and the JV partner to be aligned.
KG Onshore high-pressure, high-temperature wells cost about $10 million more each; no resource or reserve estimate yet.
Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells (with Synergia) need to deliver to reach 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
Realisations are sensitive to crude; September's above-$100 prices lifted the average, and private buyers' purchasing has been limited at higher prices.
Growing deferred tax liability and the chance of a funding decision (debt or equity) once KG ramps up.
Management's first investor call; one-off Rs.6.5 crore refund included in other income.
530075|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on the Cambay ramp-up, with a clear 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD FY29 target. Cautious and deliberately vague on KG Onshore, Duarmara and offshore, explicitly declining to give capex, reserve or funding numbers beyond the onshore guidance.
key_quotes: So, at $65-$70, if a project gives me double-digit return and gets me back my cash within year to year and a half, that is a go project for me.
Karjisan has the best fiscals in our portfolio as of today, because it has concessional Cess and royalty rates to it, because it is still in its primary term as a production-sharing contract.
So, the 5000 barrel plant that you have has a very subdued KG or the Cambay optionality in it.
Oil does not need pipeline infrastructure. Oil I can just put into a truck to haul across 300 kilometers and sell to refiner somewhere, right?

rose as new Bakrol wells came into production
nearly 5x vs Rs.11.8 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Cash, bank balances and liquid investments

financial_highlights.value: about Rs.190 crore, of which about Rs.100 crore is Duarmara

rows.why: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD from October run-rate of about 2,000 BOEPD, driven by Karjisan's seven wells (two drilled, first perforation within about a week) and Cambay optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; the 2,500 exit already includes Karjisan but not Cambay optionality.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes rose from about 1,700 BOEPD H1 average toward the 2,000 BOEPD October run-rate and a 2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, but Q2 volumes were flat QoQ and the ramp depends on wells not yet producing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is already guided at Rs.250 crore (up from Rs.220 crore), and KG Onshore development capex and a Duarmara oil plan (Rs.60-70 crore per well) will follow in five to six months or after field development plans are filed, but no figures are committed yet.

rows.why: Guidance was held (2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, 5,000 BOPD FY29), and October production of about 2,000 BOEPD plus Bakrol's 950 BOE/d and Karjisan's wells leave room, but realisations fell to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl and September's above-$100 price lifted the average.

rows.why: Two revenue sharing contracts (KG Onshore and Cambay Basin, DSF IV) were signed on 22 October 2026, adding acreage that supports the onshore growth story.

rows.why: No borrowings and about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments against Rs.250 crore FY27 capex funded from internal accruals for now, though a debt or equity decision is possible once KG ramps up.

530117|2026-03.headline: Privi FY26 revenue rose 21.7% to INR2,582.9 crore and PAT 75% to INR327.5 crore, with a 25.76% EBITDA margin.
530117|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR725.70 crore (up 15.29% YoY), EBITDA INR184.41 crore (up 25.09%) at a 25.41% margin, and PAT INR95.66 crore versus INR63.57 crore a year earlier. For FY26, income grew 21.73% to INR2,582.92 crore, driven by about 6.5% volume growth, roughly 8% price increases and product mix. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target and 20%+ EBITDA margins, with the first capex phase due by 30 June 2026 taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA. The PRIGIV JV turned profitable for the first time in Q4, and the merger with PFSPL and PBPL awaits NCLT approval.

segments.name: Standalone aroma chemicals (core)
segments.commentary: Management said demand for core aroma chemicals is steady, with about 70% of revenue from exports, mostly under contracts. Realisations rose from about INR450/kg to about INR600/kg over five years, per management.

segments.name: PRIGIV JV (with Givaudan, 51:49)
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q4 FY26 for the first time. Revenue is expected at about INR130 crore in FY27 versus INR55 crore last year, with an additional INR50 crore capex. It manufactures high-end specialty chemicals exclusively for Givaudan.

segments.name: Downstream / new specialty molecules
segments.commentary: Silver Amber, Amber Silk, Privilege and Privitolide are in commissioning, with one already commissioned. Ethyl maltol, maltol and cyclopentanone projects target mechanical completion by June 2027, with revenue expected over the next 18 months. Furfural backward integration is about 2 years away, and the vertical is said to reach about INR1,000 crore revenue.

guidance_outlook: Targets 20%+ revenue growth for the coming year on a standalone basis; the 20% excludes merged entities until the scheme is effective.
Expects to sustain 20%+ EBITDA margins going forward; one answer referenced a 24% margin and another 25%.
Long-term target of about INR5,000 crore revenue and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA in 3 to 4 years, roughly 2x.
Post all three capex phases, standalone capacity is expected at about 72,000 MT, around mid-to-late 2028.
Expects the NCLT approval for the merger of PFSPL and PBPL into the parent during FY27, internally targeted for Q3 FY27.
Expects state incentives of about INR13 crore a year, based on 50% of the GST on in-state sales in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: First capex phase to complete by 30 June 2026, taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA, with a calibrated ramp-up over the coming quarters.
Phase 2 of the multi-specialty aroma chemicals project is progressing as planned.

The three new-molecule projects (ethyl maltol, maltol, cyclopentanone) are in detailed engineering with procurement started; the 12 to 15 month build targets mechanical completion by June 2027, followed by about one month of trials.
A biomass-to-value-added-products demonstration plant with capex of about INR70-75 crore is in basic and detailed engineering, expected in about 12 months.
Furfural backward integration is expected around FY28-29, after first establishing the finished goods and sourcing furfural from outside in the meantime.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil attributed it to the timing overlap of annual raw-material and finished-goods contracts, which fall into Q4 and Q1, and said the business should be judged on an annual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth guidance inclusive of the proposed merged entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said the 20% is standalone as it stands today; the merged entities will be consolidated once the scheme takes effect.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital days rise amid the current situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Babani said any increase would be no more than 3-5%, because price rises tend to lengthen customer payment times.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the FY26 forex gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said forex gains of about INR14 crore were recorded in other income, as the company is a net exporter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net-capacity and commissioning timelines after all three phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said about 72,000 MT standalone after the first three phases, with completion around June to September 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Can standalone EBITDA margins of 27-28% be reached at the consolidated level?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said consolidated margins should improve now that PRIGIV has turned profitable, but gave no level.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross margin improve next year given crude-linked input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil said the company will assume gross margin stays at a similar level, and that any upside will come from internal efficiency gains.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in other expenses and power costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil credited the ProMax residual steam and power-saving programme and better freight and logistics contract pricing, per Narayan Iyer.

risks_watch: Crude-linked and West Asia disruption could raise freight, fuel and raw-material costs. Management said shipping may be delayed by a week or two, but stock cover is in place.
Q4 gross margin dip, which management attributed to contract timing; watch whether it reverses in Q1 FY27.
Execution risk on the 54,000 MT capacity ramp-up after 30 June 2026 and on the 2028 target of about 72,000 MT.
The NCLT approval timing for the merger (internally targeted for Q3 FY27) and its effect on consolidated numbers.
Demand for the new molecules at lower price points (for example about $45/kg); management is still testing market elasticity.
Biotech demonstration plant economics and capex, which management called complex and still at engineering stage.
530117|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term 5k story and margin sustainability, but cautious on biotech economics and on new-molecule pricing. Management deflected several questions on customer names and pipeline partners, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: We have delivered 25% plus margins consistently across all quarters and for the FY 26 on the EBITDA numbers.
So we are covered for almost a quarter for regular raw material, which are contracted.
We are definitely likely to get there, because as I said, one of the key parameters there is what kind of products you are making.

demand_pricing: Management said demand for fragrance and flavour ingredients keeps growing, and that customers want reliable, compliant, non-China suppliers.
FY26 growth split: about 6.5% from volume, about 8% from price, and the balance from product mix.
Management said it expects to pass on raw-material-driven price increases, citing customer trust and a 1-2% price premium for supplier reliability.

Raw-material cover: renewable inputs under annual contracts have about 1 to 1.5 months of inventory plus about 1 month in transit. Other inputs have about 3 months in stock and 2 to 3 months in pipeline.
Management said about 70% of raw materials are imported, which partly offsets rupee-driven realisation gains.
Management said it is in discussions with other MNC partners but is too early to disclose.

530117|2026-06.headline: Privi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.22% YoY to Rs 666 crore; consolidated EBITDA Rs 167.47 crore at 24.58% margin, PAT Rs 83.2 crore.
530117|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 consolidated total income of Rs 681.42 crore (+20.01% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 167.47 crore (+18.73% YoY) at about 24.58% margin, and PAT of about Rs 83.2 crore versus Rs 61.46 crore a year earlier. Growth was attributed to volume, price and product mix. Phase-1 capacity expansion (48,000 to 54,000 MT) is slated to commercialise within about 15 days, while the Phase-2 completion timeline has slipped to September 2027 for the final 12,000 MT. Gross margin compression (about 650 bps YoY per an analyst) was explained as a base effect from low-cost raw materials in CY25 and a normalising RM/sales ratio of 52-55%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 61.46 crore in Q1 FY26
vs ~51% in Q1 FY26 (~650 bps decline, not disputed by management)

segments.name: PRIGIV JV (with Givaudan)
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 18 crore in Q1 with EBITDA margin of about 14-15%; output sold exclusively to Givaudan. Additional equity of Rs 50 crore agreed for next expansion phase.

segments.name: Camphor
segments.commentary: Management says camphor is about 4-6% of revenue (figures given as 5-6% and 4-5%), made via CST route; not treated as a strategic product.

guidance_outlook: Rs 5,000 crore revenue and Rs 1,000 crore+ EBITDA target reiterated, over three to four years (about 2x); management said no change in guidance.
Chairman: targeting ~20% CAGR with similar EBITDA margins, benchmarked off prior-year numbers.
EBITDA margin expected around 24.6% to nearer 25% going forward; RM/sales guided at 52-54%.
New specialty and furfural-based (Maltol, Ethyl Maltol, Cyclopentanone, Musk T) plants mechanically complete by about mid-FY28 with contributions from H2 FY28.
Privi Speciality / Privi Fine Sciences / Privi Biotechnologies merger: scheme filed with NCLT; completion expected this financial year (by FY27 year-end).
capex_capacity: Phase-1: capacity from 48,000 to 54,000 MT of existing products, expected to commercialise in about 15 days from the call; earlier 6,000 MT tranche slipped from June 2026 to September 2026.
Phase-2: additional 12,000 MT (54,000 to 66,000 MT) to be completed by September 2027; Phase-2 has commenced.
Phase-3 (multi-specialty aroma) expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027; funding mainly internal accruals with bank borrowing as needed.
Capex outlook for FY27 and next two years: Rs 850-900 crore, covering Phase-2 and Phase-3.
Post-merger, about 6,000 MT of Privi Fine Sciences capacity to be added to Privi portfolio. Utilisation at around 90% of installed capacity.
Demonstration plant in Navi Mumbai for 2 TPD biomass processing; 12-15 months to build, then about a year of operation before a large-scale plant (outside the 5K/1K plan).
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy across fragrance and flavour value chain despite global headwinds; customers diversifying supply chains.
Growth attributed to volume, price increases and product mix; no quarterly volume/realisation split given (to be disclosed annually).
Crude-based raw materials ~15-18% of purchases; alpha-pinene from GTO at historic highs, but CST purchases are back-to-back with customers.
Management claims Iran war and Hormuz freight impact limited; Red Sea freight impact seen as ongoing for years with no margin concern.

530365|2026-03.headline: Orient Bell Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 66% YoY to INR16.4 crores, with margin up 270 bps, after ~20% cumulative price hikes in March-April.
530365|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 7% and revenue rose 7.5% YoY, with FY26 volumes up 4.4% and revenue up 3.1%. Consolidated EBITDA for Q4 was INR16.4 crores (up 66% YoY, margin up 270 bps) and PBT was INR8.4 crores versus INR3.6 crores a year earlier. Management took roughly 20% cumulative price increases in March and April to offset a roughly 30% rise in gas prices, and said the company is debt free with surplus cash. Management declined to give forward guidance on volumes, margins or capacity utilisation, citing gas-supply uncertainty in Morbi.

Management expects FY26 margins to be better than FY25, and said margins have improved year-on-year for the last three quarters.

Management said Morbi oversupply has been cut by the crisis; exports were flat in FY26 and the unorganised sector did poorly.
Digital initiatives: 50,000 new designs added monthly by dealers via AI room visualisation; online lead generation contributing sales for 350-plus dealers monthly.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the margin trajectory to continue; Q4 margin was 7.7% versus about 6% in Q3 (per management's description). Price hikes of about 20% were taken in March-April and further gradual increases are expected depending on gas and diesel prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are gas prices and the Q4 blended INR per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas pricing is formula-linked and changes every few days, with the mix moving from 80% formula to 55% normal and 45% spot. Overall gas prices are up about 30%, and Q4 blended cost averaged about INR45 per SCM.

530367|2026-03.headline: NRB Bearings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to INR372 crores, EBITDA margin 19.5%, and FY26 PAT up 77% to INR146 crores.
530367|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR372 crores, with EBITDA up 17% to INR74 crores (19.5% margin) and PAT of INR42 crores. The call focused on the diversification push into aerospace (via the MTR/Mahant Tool acquisition), electrification, off-highway, and robotics, plus a revised FY31 revenue outlook. 530475|2026-03.headline: Tinna Rubber Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to over 18% on revenue of INR157 crores, up 22% YoY, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25%.
530475|2026-03.overview: Management reported record tire processing volumes in FY26 and a standalone EBITDA margin of 17.2%, up 286 bps. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY and 13% QoQ to INR157 crores, with EBITDA up 63% YoY to INR29 crores. Subsidiaries and new projects (Oman, South Africa, Saudi, TP Buildtech, PCMB, pyrolysis and rCB) carried start-up costs and geopolitical drag that management expects to normalise through FY27. Infra segment softened on bitumen shortages, which management expects to be temporary.

qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects better realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP to offset any infra softness, and says the bitumen-driven slowdown is temporary.

530517|2026-03.headline: Relaxo Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.1% YoY to INR 751 crore, with EBITDA margin at 16.5%, aided partly by GST cut-driven channel restocking.

rows.why: Management was cautious: it said June is too early to call, gave no guidance beyond the 1pp margin uplift and 4-5% volume goal, and the Q4 lift was partly one-off GST-cut restocking.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Demand after 15-18% price hikes is unproven (June unknown), Haryana wage inflation is above 30%, and analysts questioned whether 4-5% volume growth fits with 100 new EBOs; FY26 revenue already fell to INR 2,702 crore from INR 2,790 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; the call covered the existing Sparx, Hawaii and Flite brands and the EBO rollout only.

rows.label: Price hikes not rolled back; no price cuts guided
rows.why: Blended consumer price increase of 15-18% over 2-3 hikes is locked in, with management saying wage costs are unlikely to fall and it is too early to guide on cuts; competitors Bata, Red Tape and Metro had not yet raised prices per analysts.

rows.label: GST-cut distributor pipeline cleared; Q4 restock unwinds
rows.why: Management said distributors carried stock and the pipeline has largely cleared, so the one-off channel restock in Q4's 8.1% revenue growth is unlikely to repeat against underlying growth of 5-6%.

rows.label: Raw material softening vs persistent labour inflation
rows.why: Raw material prices are softening, but labour costs are rising 25-30% in one state and 10-15% in others, with management expecting labour increases to persist against 15-20% total cost inflation.

tone.note: Management was confident about Q4 momentum, the 1pp FY27 margin uplift and the EBO rollout, but qualified everything with the unknown demand response to price hikes and geopolitical risk.
